News.title: Jess Phillips blasts Channel 4 for giving paedo Huw Edwards a ‘platform’ while ignoring victims in ‘irresponsible’ doc
News.content:
Next

EX-SAFEGUARDING minister Jess Phillips has furiously hit out at Channel 4 for giving paedophile Huw Edwards a “platform” while ignoring victims.

The broadcaster is facing a storm of controversy over its decision to make an hour-long documentary with the disgraced ex BBC newsreader.



Edwards – who announced the Queen’s death on the Beeb – was convicted in 2024 of making indecent images of children.

But he has made the show in a shameless attempt to rehabilitate his shattered reputation.



Responding to a desperate attempt to defend the show by Channel 4, Ms Phillips demanded to know if they bothered speaking to victims before putting shamed Edwards front and centre.

She exclusively told The Sun on Sunday: “Was the editor experienced in child sexual abuse?



“Because if not, how can they be assured that they are asking the right questions, or know if they are hearing exactly what these perpetrators always say?

“Did they seek any guidance from victims or victims groups on this? It is irresponsible if victims of this crime are not also front and centre in this.



“Does the experienced director even know if the children in those images are now safe? They may very well still be enslaved.

“Have they interviewed any of the thousands of other men who have been convicted of this crime to hear their side of the story or is it just interesting because he was famous?”

She added: “I am happy to confront things I don’t like, I have to do it all day every day.

“They should admit that the reason they picked Huw Edwards not any of the thousands of other men who have done this is because it sells, it’s not about confronting the issue.

“Unless they had the express permission of his victims and they were part of the process it’s just more platforming his voice while theirs remains silent.”



She was speaking after Louisa Compton, Director of News, Digital and Audience Trust at Channel 4, was forced to issue a statement defending the programme after it was criticised by No10.

She said it is “reasonable to ask why Channel 4 has made this film, and why now” but insisted it was proper journalism.

She said: “Huw Edwards is not being allowed to tell his story unchallenged or on his own terms.



“He is questioned throughout by an experienced director; he was not paid; he had no control over the content of the film; and there were no restrictions on the questions he could be asked.”

But in an apparent admission that victims do not appear in the documentary – due to be aired on Tuesday – she added: “We are also acutely conscious that behind offences involving indecent images are real children and real victims – including those as young as seven – who have been abused.

“Nothing about making this film diminishes the seriousness of that harm, nor does Edwards’ participation entitle him to sympathy, redemption or rehabilitation.”

Charities and victims groups have condemned the documentary, which was made in collaboration with The Observer.

Chris Sherwood, CEO of the NSPCC, told The Sun on Sunday: “There are serious questions media outlets and broadcasters will need to answer about the choices they have made.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“There should not be any attempt to downplay the significance of Huw Edwards’ crimes.

“We hope any programme, interview or report will have the wellbeing of children at its heart and will use this as an opportunity to focus on the devastating impact grooming, exploitation and child sexual abuse offences have on the young people who are subjected to these crimes and the urgent need for better protections for children – on and offline.”

News.title: Wild moment huge brawl erupts in market town as women throw shop signs and punch each other in cocktail dress smackdown
News.content:
Next

SCANTILY-CLAD women in mini dresses have been filmed wildly trading blows in a barbaric street brawl.

At one point in the violent clip a man launches an advertising board into a group, sending two people toppling to the ground.



A barefooted woman in a mini dress then appears to pick up the display and attempt to hurl it back at the group.

Several men and women can be seen throwing punches as the chaotic melee spills across Week Street in Maidstone, Kent.



In one brutal moment, a woman sat on top of another and repeatedly punched her in the face before being dragged off.

Men are also seen exchanging punches, with several dropping to the pavement as the fracas ensues.

The shocking scenes unfolded in front of stunned onlookers, with bottles also heard smashing during the chaos.

The footage was filmed during a night of chaos in the early hours of Sunday, November 22.



At various points, people attempt to drag others away from the fighting as the two groups clash.

But the violence eventually appears to die down, with the majority of those involved scarpering in two vehicles.

The heavy board was used as a weapon multiple times during the brawl.



Cops arrive shortly after as the clip draws to a close.

Around 15 people are believed to have been involved in the disturbance.

Cops have since confirmed a woman, 21, from Chatham has been arrested on suspicion of affray.



She was released on bail while police continue their investigation.

Kent Police said officers were called at 2.59am following reports of two groups fighting.

They arrived within five minutes but those involved had already fled the scene.

No injuries were reported.

Investigating officer PC Biken Rana-Magar said: “We believe there were approximately 15 people involved in the disturbance who are aged between 18 and 30.



“I’m aware there is online footage showing the incident and those involved, and I would encourage anyone with information to contact us.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Cops are now urging anyone who witnessed the violence or recognises those involved to come forward.

Anyone with information is asked to call Kent Police, quoting reference 46/193242/26.

News.title: Zelensky vows to launch crippling new strikes to completely demolish Putin’s £3bn Crimea bridge as 9 killed in Ukraine
News.content:
Next

VOLODYMYR Zelensky has vowed to obliterate the rest of Vladimir Putin’s prized Crimea Bridge with a fresh round of devastating strikes.

The Ukrainian president declared he would finish off the £3billion transport link following a crippling wave of missiles and drones earlier this month.



The comments come as Moscow exchanged heavy barrages of overnight strikes with Kyiv, leaving nine innocent civilians dead across the war-ravaged country.

A massive chunk of Putin’s beloved bridge linking mainland Russia to the annexed Ukrainian territory of Crimea was rendered useless on November 18 – one of the biggest blows to Moscow since the war broke out.



It has significantly hampered the Kremlin’s supply lines – with the destruction of a four-lane road on the crossing making it harder to supply Russian troops in the region.

But now, Zelensky wants to finish off the remainder of the 11-mile structure for good.



Taking out the remains of the bridge would render the lengthy structure completely useless and mark a damning blow to Putin’s war machine.

An emboldened Zelensky has his eyes set on this next objective, military officials in Kyiv told The Telegraph.



One source said: “The president wants it demolished completely.”

The strike earlier this month was the latest boost to Kyiv’s confidence in unleashing defensive strikes against logistical targets in Russia.

Destroying the crossing could help reverse Putin’s grip on Crimea, which has been occupied by Moscow since 2014.



Ukraine has tried to destroy the bridge several times since the invasion broke out.

Only the November 18 attempt was successful – made possible by a wave of pre-emptive strikes taking out surrounding air defences.

Incredible footage showed the moment the bridge exploded and was toppled over after the stunning missile and drone onslaught.

An enormous fireball was seen lighting up the night sky before a second blast collapsed one of the bridge’s giant 745ft-wide arches.

Kyiv’s spooks spent weeks plotting their mission to target the highway – a symbol of Russia’s illegal annexation of Crimea in 2014.



A source familiar with the operation said they unleashed a “considerable” barrage of Neptune anti-ship cruise missiles from undisclosed locations.

Servicemen from various Ukrainian units struck the bridge in the hours following.

Putin personally attended the opening of the structure in 2018 – driving a truck over it to celebrate.

Following the blast, the road was made unusable but it is believed the rail track is still operable.

Maritime routes between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea have also been disrupted.



Putin also vowed to deliver a “painful revenge” to Ukraine for the attack.

The Russian tyrant delivered his stark warning just minutes after discussing the need for peace with the US and China.

It comes after Ukraine’s stunning strike on a Russian warship in Libya – another massive hit to Putin’s expanding war efforts.

Amid these successful operations carried out by Kyiv, Russia has continued to kill Ukrainian civilians.

At least nine people across Ukraine were reported killed on Saturday.



Seven people were killed and seven others wounded in a Russian attack on an enterprise in Nizhyn, in Ukraine’s northern Chernihiv region.

In Russian-occupied Ukraine, two people died and two others were wounded when a Ukrainian drone struck a hospital vehicle in the southern Zaporizhzhia region.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Meanwhile, Russia said it had downed a near-record number of Ukrainian drones during the night.

News.title: Woman, 21, dies in horror crash after police chase – as man, 23, arrested and two rushed to hospital
News.content:
TRAGIC SMASH Woman, 21, dies in horror crash after police chase – as man, 23, arrested and two rushed to hospital







Next

A 21-YEAR-OLD woman has died after a crash following a police pursuit with cops arresting a man, aged 23.

The horror collision, involving a Seat Ibiza and a Vauxhall Astra, took place in Hednesford, Staffordshire, shortly after 11pm on Friday.



The crash on Rugeley Road followed a police pursuit involving a police vehicle and the Seat, according to Staffordshire Police.

The woman who died at the scene was the front-seat passenger in the Seat, cops added.



Cops confirmed that a 23-year-old man from the Walsall area has been arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving.

The driver of the Astra is helping with police inquiries, the force added.

Two other people were taken to hospital, with their injuries not believed to be life threatening or life changing.

The woman’s next of kin have been informed and are being supported by specially trained officers at this difficult time.

Cops have urged any witnesses to come forward immediately following the tragedy.

Staffordshire Police said in a statement: “We’re keen to speak to anyone who was in the area at the time, or those who saw the vehicles in the lead up to the collision.



“Contact us by calling 101, or via our website, quoting incident 893 of 27 November.

“To speak to collision investigators directly, email ciu@staffordshire.police.uk.”

The incident has been referred to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) due to the police activity prior to the collision.

News.title: Argentina loses bid to block Falklands oil project as UK declares verdict ‘vindicates’ British sovereignty over islands
News.content:
Next

ARGENTINA has lost its shameless bid to stop a major oil exploration project near the Falklands islands.

The Argentine government had demanded the joint UK-Israeli Sea Lion venture be halted as it claimed there was an ongoing dispute over the sovereignty of the Falklands.



President Javier Milei has ramped up his rhetoric in recent months demanding the Falklands are Argentinian.

The UK has always said the Falklands are a British territory – a viewpoint also held by the islanders themselves after a resounding election in favour of Britain.



Milei’s attempt to stop the oil venture was today rejected by a UN-backed international tribunal in Germany.

The head of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea blocked Buenos Aires’ move as he ruled the court was unable to rule on questions of sovereignty.

The British government hailed the decision as a “vindication” of UK control over the islands.

But raging Milei fumed at the annoucement as he again reiterated his stance that the Falkland islands “are Argentine”.

The thwarted president said he would “respect” the court’s ruling but warned: “This decision is not the final word.”

Meanwhile Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband and Attorney General Ellie Reeves urged Argentina to “respect the right of the Falkland Islanders to determine their own future” and end its ecomic pressure on the islands.



Speaking in a joint statement they said: “Argentina sought to stop the Falkland Islanders making their own sovereign decisions and failed in this attempt.

“The UK has no doubt of our sovereignty of the Falkland Islands, our sovereignty and sovereign rights over the surrounding maritime areas, and the right of self-determination of the Falkland Islanders.”

The Sea Lion oilfield holds an estimated 1.7 billion barrels of oil and could keep pumping for decades.



It is located around 130 miles from the coats of the Falklands – with the regional government approving its development late last year.

In April 2026, Labour approved the decision – allowing the project to move to full production.

It is understood that the major venture would not have been allowed to go ahead without UK backing.

The tribunal ruled in favour of letting the oil field go ahead because Argentina’s challenge rested on a territorial dispute – which the court did not have the power to rule on.

Milei’s government argued that drilling could not go ahead inside disputed waters under international law.



But judges ruled 18-3 in favour of rejecting Argentina’s claims.

Once extraction begins – estimated to start within two years – revenues of up to £4 billion could pour into the coffers of the island’s 3,500 residents.

A 2013 referendum saw 99.8 per cent of Falklanders voting to remain a British Overseas Territory.

But the dispute exploded again over the summer when Argentine footballers taunted England with a huge banner claiming the islands as their own after their victory over the Three Lions.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Former Tottenham star Giovani Lo Celso was among the Argentina players involved in celebrations featuring a flag bearing the words: “Las Malvinas Son Argentinas”, meaning “The Falklands are Argentine.”



But the nation was slapped with a £237,000 fine by FIFA over the disgraceful display.

News.title: Shocking videos show ‘new gen’ bus drivers ‘DRIFTING’ around corners and racing 14-tonne double-deckers around London
News.content:
Next

A NEW generation of London bus drivers has taken to the capital’s roads, allegedly speeding through the streets and “drifting” around corners, leaving passengers fearing for their safety.

Footage uploaded to TikTok also appears to show a number of iconic red double-decker buses hurtling along roads while aggressively beeping horns and flashing their lights.



One video appears to show two buses being driven side by side having a ‘race’, while another depicts a Transport for London bus swerving across lanes before repeatedly doing laps of a roundabout.

Several clips appear to show buses dangerously lurching to one side as their weight shifts while hurtling around corners.





Numerous videos on TikTok show a “New Generation” of bus drivers posing for cameras, making gun gestures with their fingers, and occasionally wearing balaclavas with their hoods up.

In one clip posted on social media, the driver stops the bus to speak to the video camera while wearing a Guy Fawkes face mask.

None of the footage seen by The Sun was filmed by the drivers themselves, but they appear to be playing up to cameras while driving their 14-tonne vehicles.

It is unclear whether the drivers were on duty when some of the footage was filmed.



They have been dubbed the “New Gen” or “Mandem” bus drivers by some TikTok users, who even praise them for getting passengers from ‘A to B’ at breakneck speed.

Mandem is a London slang term commonly used to refer to a group of friends.



Many of the clips on social media are accompanied by rap or drill music and often make light of TfL’s slogan “Every Journey Matters“.

Some of the footage uploaded to social media does not appear to show passengers on board, but a number of users have raised concerns about these young drivers’ conduct on the roads.

Influencer Ameenah Ore took to social media and said: “Has anyone noticed how the younger generation of bus drivers drive so fast? It’s so scary.”

She continued: “This is no BMW, this is a double-decker bus. This is not a bus race. This is not Formula One… This is a bus that has 30 people on it. There are no seatbelts!”



The TikToker added: “Sometimes the way these drivers go round the bend I feel like the bus is going to tip over!”

Another user claimed that if the bus has its wing mirrors tilted at 45 degrees: “He’s from the hood, he’s going to drive like he’s getting chased by the police. And he’s definitely not going to be driving at 20mph.”

But the aggressive driving style and speed of some drivers have been welcomed by a surprising number of social media users who claim they have helped get them across the capital quicker.

One social media user commented: “Getting places in good time, I’m here for it.”



Another added: “I always hope they’re my bus drivers, like yes, I want a 40 min bus journey turned into a 20 min one.”

A third said: “Big them up! A to B fast, the older ones be driving like snails.”



One London bus driver told The Sun: “The tilted mirrors, the speeding, yeah I’ve seen it. I’m against it and there’s a lot of other drivers who are too.”

“Collisions caused by them are common… Tilted mirrors do not cover the correct blind spots as the normal position does.”

He added: “Bus drivers are also wearing face coverings and still wearing non uniform too. I thought there was a ‘uniform policy’?”

He joked: “Sometimes ninjas are driving the bus you’re getting on, speeding down the road and making the ride dangerous.”

According to TfL’s bus safety dashboard, there were some 28,368 collisions in 2025, which works out to 78 every day, or one every 18 minutes.



TfL also reported that 10 people were killed in collisions involving a bus, but insists this is the lowest number since 2021.

There is no suggestion that the individuals filmed in these videos were involved in or responsible for the collisions or deaths.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A TfL spokesperson said: “Buses enable millions of safe journeys across London each day and we work closely with London’s operators to ensure that they are driven carefully and safely.

“We support operators in taking action against any drivers found to be driving inappropriately and work with them to investigate any allegations of this nature.”

News.title: Boy, 10, rushed to hospital with stomach pain as doctors find ‘5.5inch SKELETON with tiny arms & legs’ growing in belly
News.content:
GRIM DISCOVERY Boy, 10, rushed to hospital with stomach pain as doctors find ‘5.5inch SKELETON with tiny arms & legs’ growing in belly







Next

A BOY has been found with a 5.5 inch skeleton growing in his belly after being rushed to hospital with stomach pain.

Doctors were left horrified when they discovered another body – complete with limbs, nails, and hair – inside the 10-year-old youngster.



Medics in Pakistan said the “fetal skeleton” had been quietly growing inside the boy’s abdomen before it was removed on June 16.

In the days leading up to the boy’s hospital visit, he reportedly lost a lot of weight, suffered from a bad fever, and had pain in his tummy.



Upon seeing him, doctors noticed his abdomen was quite swollen and tender, particularly to the left side.

They ran a CT scan on him before finding a large mass inside his body.

It was roughly the length of a standard iPhone.

The boy went under the knife, with surgeons removing the sizable mass which was attached to major blood vessels near his small intestine.

But when doctors opened up the growth, they were left in complete shock.



It had fatty tissue, tooth-like deposits, and a “well-formed fetal skeleton”.

They could make out its miniature arms and legs, as well as its hair and nails.

It even had a recognisable backbone upon further inspection.

Medics believe the growth was the result of a rare condition called fetus-in-fetu or FIF – which translates to “fetus within a fetus”.

The extremely rare condition occurs in roughly one in every 500,000 live births.



Less than 250 cases have been reported worldwide – most involving boys.

Growths like these usually develop in the abdomen, but can occasionally show up near other body parts.

In July, a similar case made headlines when Chinese surgeons found one of these masses inside a one-year-old girl’s brain.

It is unclear what causes FIF.

But scientists have two main theories.



The first and more widely accepted explanation is that it stems from a rare complication during the development of identical twins.

In certain cases, when the fertilised egg splits into two embryos, one embryo gets most of the cells and grows normally while the other becomes trapped inside it.

The larger one keeps growing, swallowing up the small embryo while it continues to swell.

The smaller twin can continue receiving blood from its sibling, allowing some body parts to develop – but it never finishes development.

Boffins also theorise the condition could be the result of a type of tumor called teratoma.



These growths can be a mix of body tissues, including hair, muscle, teeth and bone.

Some are harmless, while others can be cancerous.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The boy managed to recover well and doctors found no signs of cancer.

He was discharged from hospital 11 days after being admitted.

News.title: Britain to be battered by heavy rain and brisk winds this weekend as Atlantic blast washes away snow hopes
News.content:
SNOW HOPE Britain to be battered by heavy rain and brisk winds this weekend as Atlantic blast washes away snow hopes







Next

HEAVY rain and wind have squashed any chance of snow this weekend, as an atlantic blast batters Britain.

Hopes of snow to fall across Britain have been squashed, with heavy rain and mild weather sweeps across the country today.



The Met Office has reported the sight of snow is very unlikely across the UK now, apart from the highest Scottish mountains.

The dry and chilly weather in the second half of the week will instead cause more wind and rain due to a brisk wind coming in from the Atlantic.



Saturday will see a broad area of rain move across the north east of the UK, with rain appearing particularly heavy in the south west.

The Met Office has issued yellow weather warnings covering parts of England and Wales, in force from midday on Monday until just before midnight on Tuesday.



The warnings cover Cumbria in north-west England, as well as large parts of north and south Wales, where “heavy and persistent rain” will develop on Monday.

Downpours will continue until the end of the day on Tuesday, with forecasters predicting 30-60mm of rain widely, with the potential for more than 100mm in the wettest locations.

As the downpour makes its way to Scotland, it will fall as snow above 600 metres, with the rest of the country receiving rain instead.

A separate yellow weather warning for rain was issued for Scotland, stretching from the southern coast to the Highlands and due to be in force from 3am on Monday until midday on Tuesday.



The Met Office warned any flooding could cause disruption to travel, with possible road closures, as well as delays and cancellations to train and bus services.

Flooding is more likely in areas where the ground becomes saturated or a build-up of fallen leaves blocks drainage.

It added that there is a small chance homes and businesses could be damaged by flooding, and that fast flowing or deep floodwater could cause danger to life.

Spray and flooding could lead to difficult driving conditions and lead to some roads being closed, the forecaster added.

The biggest part of the wet weather will be over by Saturday evening, with cold and brisk winds taking its place.



The wind will drag smaller showers into western and northern areas, causing more snow over the Scottish mountains.

Sunday should see a brighter Britain, following another chilly start to the day.

Dry weather and sunny spells will be broken by rain approaching from the west, which the Met Office has warned to be rather heavy and blustery.

The Met Office has also reported that there is likely to be no chance of snow next week either, with south westerly winds dragging through mild air.

Temperatures will instead be higher than the average for this time of year, especially during the night.



There is a strong chance of heavy rain too, mainly in the west of the UK.

However, by the middle of next week, there are signs that night frost and early fog may appear across the country.

Met Office meteorologist Dan Holley said in a morning weather update on Saturday: “If we look at the bigger picture into next week, we’ve got a conveyer belt of frontal systems coming in Sunday night onwards.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“For several days, Monday, Tuesday, we could see a fair bit of rain piling onto these westerns hills of the UK, initially in the north west, and then that focus will slip further south as we head through Tuesday.

“So, the potential for quite a bit of rain on western hills, another watch point where we might see a little bit of flooding.”

News.title: Andy Burnham must be more ambitious with energy bill support, top union chief warns
News.content:
Andy Burnham must be more ambitious with energy bill support, top union chief warns

EXCLUSIVE: TUC General Secretary Paul Nowak said it is 'obvious' the Prime Minister must do more as households brace for a 26% rise in energy bills this winter

View 3 Images Andy Burnham must be more ambitious in helping cash-strapped families with energy support, a union chief has warned (Image: Thomas Krych/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

Andy Burnham must be more ambitious in helping cash-strapped families with energy support, a union chief has warned.

‌



‌



TUC General Secretary Paul Nowak said it is “obvious” the Prime Minister must do more as households brace for a 26% rise in bills this winter. He said immediate support is urgently needed as well as a long-term strategy to fix Britain’s broken energy market in the 10-year plan.

‌



Regulator Ofgem on Wednesday confirmed that its price cap for a typical household using gas and electricity and paying by monthly direct debit will leap by £443 a year, to £2,166. Donald Trump’s war in Iran has been blamed for the sharp increase, which is the biggest since Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images TUC chief Paul Nowak said immediate support is urgently needed as well as a long-term plan to fix Britain’s broken energy market in the 10-year plan (Image: Tim Merry/Staff Photographer)

Asked if the Government’s £100 energy support set out at the Budget is enough, Mr Nowak told The Mirror: “Any support the government can give is going to be useful, and I think it was absolutely right to tax the banks to take that £100 off 20 million people's energy bills.

‌



But I mean, I think it's clear, it's obvious with bills going up by what 26%, £443 a year for the average household, the government is going to have to do more, and it's going to need to be more ambitious.”

Mr Burnham will set out his 10-year plan for Britain in mid-December, which he has promised will lay “out a path from where we are now to where I believe we all want Britain to be”. Government advisers are currently holding discussions and roundtables with think tanks, researchers and unions for the plan.

‌



Mr Nowak said there is “a lot riding” on the plan to deliver the circuit breaker in British politics promised by the PM when he entered Downing Street.

The union chief said he must face down those with vested interests, including banks and business lobbyists, and present a clear vision showing voters he’s on their side.

‌



“I think that there is a lot riding on this because the Prime Minister came into office saying he was going to deliver a circuit breaker in our politics, and they've done some really good things, but we haven't quite got to that circuit breaker moment yet,” he said.

The TUC is calling for a Fair Energy Price plan, which would introduce a social tariff to permanently cut bills for the majority of households. Under the plan, the lowest income households would save up to £650 per year, which would be paid for by upping taxes on banks.

‌



View 3 Images Chancellor John Healey raised the bank surcharge from 3% to 6% for a 15-month period from January to pay for energy support (Image: Tejas Sandhu/SOPA Images/Shutterstock)

At last month’s Budget, Chancellor John Healey raised the bank surcharge from 3% to 6% for a 15-month period from January to pay for energy support. But it was a smaller increase than expected. “I thought it was the right thing to do, but I just thought the government should have been more ambitious,” Mr Nowak said.

‌



“I mean, we are at an unprecedented time when our members are struggling to pay their heating bills. The financial services industry is handing out £25billion in bonuses and were at record levels of profits. Those profits are going to be sustained because interest rates are still high because of Trump's war in Iran.

“I think they could have been more ambitious, and so, if they would have just taken up to 8%, which is where the Tories had, it raises another £10.5billion over the next four years.”

‌



He said he is clear he wants a successful banking industry, but added: “You can have a successful banking industry and ask them to pay a fair share of tax. The two things go hand in hand. So yeah, I mean, I think it was a step in the right direction. But I think the government should have been more ambitious.”

More widely, on the 10-year plan, Mr Nowak said he will be looking for ambitious plans on public control of services, delivery on public sector insourcing, and a reindustrialisation plan that will help turn the tide on a decline in British manufacturing jobs.

‌



On energy bills, he said the plan must set out a “more cohesive approach to energy policy”, with more input from the public sector, to stop both households and businesses being clobbered by bills.

He said: “They said that they're going to use the 10-year plan to set out what the Prime Minister means by public control and public ownership. And part of the reason we're in this mess is because we've got a privatised, fragmented energy market.

‌



“And so, I want the government to be ambitious to say: ‘No, we can't be in this position.’ I mean, we're almost unique in Europe in terms of households being clobbered by these energy prices, manufacturers being clobbered by these energy prices. How do we have a much more cohesive approach to energy policy? And I think there's got to be an increased role for the public sector in that.”

He added that the Government needs to set out the options for increased public control, be it in the energy sector or the water industry.

‌



Asked whether the plan should be a reset for Britain, Mr Nowak added: “I think it's a once in a generation opportunity, and I don't say that sort of lightly. I think the government has sent all the right signals around reindustrialisation, about saying actually we do care where we make stuff, it makes a difference.

“We do care about the way that we deliver our public services, that makes a difference as well. But now they're going to have to flesh that out.”

‌



Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh has repeatedly said affordability is her number one priority. In an interview with the Mirror in the summer, she admitted the public are right to be “impatient” over further rises to energy bills.

The Government has already pressed ahead with some energy support including a temporary 20% VAT cut on electricity bills, which came into force last month. Mr Healey also used the Budget to announce the removal of gas standing charges, as well as a £100 energy bills payment for those living in council tax bands A-D.

Article continues below

Polly Billington, Minister for Energy Consumers, suggested the 10-year plan will include details on improving the energy market through "cheap, clean, power" and improvements to the grid. The plan is expected to set out how to build cheaper, faster electricity network through GB Grid, and reform the complex web of institutions that govern the system.

She told the Mirror: "We are providing breathing space now, with 20 million households getting £100 towards their energy costs from January and VAT being cut from electricity bills, while making the big changes needed to bring bills down for good and put the public interest back at the heart of the system. As part of the Plan for Britain we will reform the broken energy market and bring costs in line with our European neighbours, through cheap, clean power and a faster, cheaper grid."

News.title: 'I almost died in shark attack – I'm still haunted by what I saw as my skin was torn off'
News.content:
'I almost died in shark attack – I'm still haunted by what I saw as my skin was torn off'

WARNING - DISTRESSING DETAILS: Leah Stewart's "quick-ish swim" turned into a nightmare after an encounter with the largest predatory shark in the world left her catastrophically injured

View 3 Images A woman who almost lost her life in a shark attack has admitted she's "still haunted” (Image: Getty Images)

A woman who almost lost her life in a gruesome shark attack has admitted she's "still haunted by its little black beady eyes". Earlier this year, what Leah Stewart, 35, described as a "quick-ish swim" turned into a nightmare after an encounter with the largest predatory shark in the world left her catastrophically injured and in a coma for 11 days.

‌



‌



On June 13, she entered the water at Coogee Beach in Sydney, Australia, only to be attacked by a great white shark, suffering horrific injuries to her arm and narrowly escaping with her life.

‌



As she swam in the bay, Leah heard screams and turned toward the commotion, spotting a "huge fin" behind two girls - but beachgoers on shore hadn’t seen it.

‌



Leah was about to swim back when the 4m shark "torpedoed" towards her, then slowed down and began circling her ominously. She was trapped, and the animal was getting closer.

View 3 Images Leah Stewart’s "quick-ish swim" turned into a nightmare (Image: GoFundMe)

She told The Times: "I'm still haunted by its little black beady eyes just looking at me. I know it's an animal, but the terror in me was somewhere between getting thrown off a building, someone standing at the end of your bed with a knife, getting woken up - It was electricity running through my body."

‌



Leah added: "Everything in my body was saying, 'Turn away… try and get away'. But I just knew that if I turned, it would have launched at me from behind."

Forced to make a life-or-death decision in a matter of seconds, Leah - who is right-handed - bravely decided to guard herself with her left arm, and the shark locked on to it.

‌



In grisly detail, she described how she watched as the shark "shred the skin" and muscle off her arm. She suffered an injury called "degloving", where skin and subcutaneous fat are torn away.

As her terrifying ordeal continued, the shark stopped, then charged at her. It went on to bite her thigh and attempt to drag her down into the depths, but Leah fought back, thinking about her young daughter.

‌



View 3 Images Ocean Pool at Coogee Beach, Sydney, Australia (Image: Getty Images)

She punched the shark with her right hand, damaging her tendons, and the shark ultimately released its grip. Severely injured and surrounded by blood, thankfully, Leah was able to reach a paddleboarder.

‌



On the beach, medics carried out a life-saving emergency procedure, drilling into her collarbone to administer blood. And although they feared the worst at St Vincent's Hospital, Leah eventually emerged from her coma.

Perhaps most surprising is that Leah, now recovered but with an amputated arm, has re-entered the water. However, she decided, at least for the time being, to use a different beach.

News.title: GTA 6 could be 'life-saving' in real emergency, charity claims
News.content:
GTA 6 could be 'life-saving' in real emergency, charity claims

It’s not the kind of video game tip you’d expect to see online

View 2 Images Grand Theft Auto VI was released worldwide earlier this month (Image: Marcin Golba/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

The British Heart Foundation has made a surprising claim about one feature included in Grand Theft Auto 6. In an online post, the charity claims that one of the most viral pop tracks featured in the game could be life-saving in the right hands.

‌



‌



In a TikTok clip, the charity says that Carly Rae Jepsen’s 'Run Away With Me' is more than just a revival hit with a catchy tune. It could be an ideal pace to remember when giving chest compressions steadily during CPR.

‌



The charity said: "Plot twist - the GTA VI soundtrack could actually help you save a life. Carly Rae Jepsen’s trending song ‘Run Away With Me’ is the right tempo for CPR."

‌



The video claims the popular track, first released in 2015 but gaining popularity over a decade later, plays at around 119 beats per minute. The charity claims that this is the "perfect tempo" for performing CPR.

The ideal tempo for CPR chest compressions is 100 to 120 beats per minute (BPM) which is roughly two compressions per second. Several songs fall into that range, such as Stayin' Alive by the Bee Gees (103BPM), Sabrina Carpenter's Espresso (104BPM) and Dancing Queen by Abba (100BPM).

‌



Adrenaline often causes rescuers to push too fast. Choosing a song closer to 100 or 110 BPM (like Stayin' Alive or Espresso) provides a helpful buffer so you do not exceed 120 compressions per minute while still allowing the chest to fully recoil between pushes.

The most common need for CPR is to help during cardiac arrest. This usually happens without warning and is when the heart suddenly stops pumping blood around the body.

‌



Studies show that sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) continues to be a significant global health issue, particularly when it occurs outside of hospital settings. It is the primary cause of death in European countries and the United States.
