News.title: ‘Super’ El Nino could be about to take a dramatic turn, forecaster warns
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The “Super” El Niño weather phenomenon is set to “rapidly” collapse next year after reaching record strengths this winter, a meteorologist has claimed, which would bring consequences across the global.

El Niño is the warm phase of a two-part oscillation in surface temperatures on the tropical Pacific Ocean, which affects weather patterns worldwide.

The current trend is expected to peak in December before making way for a corresponding ‘La Niña’ phase, bringing increased rainfall, flooding risks and tropical cyclones to some regions.

La Niña events can last from several months to years and would likely bring colder, wetter and stormier conditions across the UK through autumn and winter.

open image in gallery People navigate a flooded street by boat in Piura, Peru, on November 27, 2026, following heavy rains ( AFP/Getty )

Andrej Flis, a weather and climate analyst and forecaster, wrote on Friday that data shows El Niño nearing its peak as temperatures in a key patch of the Pacific rise 6C above normal.

Unusual highs in the region have seen this year’s El Niño called the strongest in at least eighty years of record keeping, which researchers believe could bring more extreme weather later on.

The current phase has been building since the start of this summer, with warmer surface temperatures weakening trade winds and pushing warm waters east towards the Americas.

That usually causes wetter weather, including flooding, off the coast of South America and in parts of the southeast United States, while bringing drought and wildfires to southeast Asia, Australia, the Amazon and southern Africa, according to the WWF.

The UN's World Food Program has projected that the phase could push an additional 49 million people into hunger due to impacts on agriculture.

open image in gallery Hurricane Melissa churns through the Caribbean Sea, in October 2025. The last La Niña phase lasted from late 2025 through until early 2026 ( NOAA )

But Flis said a cold anomaly emerging in the western waters looks more like the start of a La Niña phase, which would end the status quo.

A forecasting model showed the relative temperature anomaly rising through until the new year before falling to 0C by late summer 2027 and -2C by January 2028.

“The forecast drops to around -2 degrees by winter 2027/2028, which is strong La Niña territory,” he wrote in analysis for Severe Weather Europe.

“This forecast is in relative anomalies, which indicates that the coming La Niña could have a stronger weather impact than the raw ocean temperatures might suggest.”

Both phases generally begin developing between March and June and reach their peak intensity between November and February, according to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).

open image in gallery Massive waves coming ashore during a king tide event in Pacifica, California, on November 25, 2026. Californians are preparing for a confluence of exceptionally high tides and El Nino-fueled weather that threatens coastal areas with extreme flooding ( AFP/Getty )

La Niña would see stronger trade winds blowing east, pushing warm water towards Asia and Australia, with cooler water below the surface rising to replace it near South America.

Those cold waters could lead to drought in the southern US and heavy rains and flooding in the Pacific Northwest and Canada, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

La Niña suppresses hurricane activity in the central and eastern Pacific basins, around California and Central America, but enhances it in the Atlantic basin, affecting the Caribbean.

The last La Niña phase lasted from late 2025 through until early 2026.

Simon Mason, senior scientist at the Stockholm Environment Institute, wrote this week that the current phase could continue to strengthen for another few weeks, even after forecasters said it had likely peaked.

“Regardless of whether the El Niño strengthens further, plateaus, or weakens, there will be an exceptionally strong El Niño for the next few months,” he said.

“Because we can be sure El Niño conditions will persist into early 2027, we can continue to expect disruptions in weather patterns around the world.”

News.title: Black Friday 2026 live: Expert analysis on which deals to shop (and which to avoid)
News.content:
It’s official: Black Friday 2026 was the highest-spending online shopping day this country has ever seen, with over £1.3bn spent, according to Adobe Digital Insights (ADI).

Black Friday weekend has given us plenty of incentive to shop, with good deals on a vast array of products. It’s not too late to find a gem, as many retailers will continue to offer discounts until Cyber Monday.

The Telegraph Recommended team spends most of the year testing and reviewing the things you’re likely to buy, from mattresses to running shoes. So we’re well qualified to help you find the best genuine deals as Black Friday weekend progresses, including offers on tech gadgets, home appliances and sleep products.

Equally important are our data analysts, who vet each deal using price-tracking tools, spreadsheets and a healthy dose of scepticism. Our team of expert deal-hunters has manually checked and verified hundreds of deals this week, and only 27 per cent of them met our criteria for a genuine deal (more on these below).

The best Black Friday 2026 deals: At a glance

How we find Black Friday deals

You can’t always trust the percentage discounts you see advertised. Just because a website lists an RRP (or recommended retail price) doesn’t mean that product is often – or, indeed, ever – sold at that price.

To work out whether a deal actually offers value for money, our Telegraph Recommended deal-hunters use independent price-tracking tools like CamelCamelCamel or PriceRunner.

In order to recommend a deal, we want to see that it’s selling for at least 10 per cent less than its average price over the past six months. Very occasionally, we’ll use our editorial discretion to recommend deals that don’t quite hit that 10 per cent target if sales on that brand are rare and we think it’s really worth the money.

News.title: Alonso crisis deepens as chaotic Chelsea lose and fans taunt own player
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea.

The City Ground hosts the Premier League clash tonight, with two sides who are both falling short of expectations.

Forest head coach Oliver Glasner brought with him a sense of optimism after he left Crystal Palace, but the club are just outside the bottom three, sitting in 17th position with only nine points. As things stand, they are only clear of 18th-placed Sunderland because of superior goal difference.

Beneath them, Glasner’s former club Palace are bottom, two points away from them, and then Manchester United come in 19th, a single point behind. With Thomas Frank and Mauricio Pochettino now installed at Selhurst Park and Old Trafford, respectively, the pressure could soon be felt yet more keenly.

There have been flashes of encouragement, with a 3-1 win over Manchester City in early November, spearheaded by a brace from Liam Delap, who left Chelsea in the summer. However, last Saturday they lost 2-0 at Bournemouth to dent any nascent momentum, and the match was the sixth in 11 league games where the club have failed to score. Forest have scored nine times this season, with only Sunderland having a worse record in attack.

Chelsea’s Xabi Alonso has also endured a tough time of late. They were trounced 4-1 against Leeds United at home on Saturday, despite taking the lead in the first half.

That worrying collapse was the fourth loss in five league matches, and it followed a 1-0 defeat against Sunderland at the Stadium of Light before the recent international break.

There is speculation that Chelsea will move for a central defender in January, with 20 goals conceded in the Premier League so far.

Chelsea are currently in eighth place in the league with 16 points, five points behind Liverpool in fourth. Tonight, they could leapfrog Bournemouth, who are in fifth, two points ahead of them. Another loss, though, could see them in the bottom half once the weekend’s fixtures are completed.

News.title: Ireland beat Australia in front of 50,000 empty seats
News.content:
Farrell said he had not had time to fully digest what he made of the format, but he admitted the Friday double-header was a difficult sell, particularly at just five days’ notice, or the decision to stage every game at the same venue.

“Off the top of my head I don’t know whether the Friday night thing works, or the same venue [for every game],” he said. “Obviously they look like little things but they’re not to fans, when you don’t know when to book your flights or hotels.

“I loved the razzmatazz. Coming into the ground, it felt different. It felt like an event, a concert. It was just a shame we couldn’t get the people through the door.

“The 4.40pm kick off earlier… I felt for those boys,” Farrell added of the Fiji-Italy game earlier in the day, which was played out to even fewer fans. “But it’s not our job to make sense of it. Our job is to play rugby.”

Ireland did not do much of that initially, albeit it was always going to be difficult to top their statement win over South Africa last weekend.

They got off to a terrible start, coughing up four penalties in the first 10 minutes alone, two of them from their usually dominant scrum.

Australia responded with some truly awful kicking. First Carter Gordon turned down the chance to go for goal, opting instead to kick for the corner only to miss it by miles. Then they sliced another ball out on the full from centre field.

The Wallabies played much the better rugby in the first 20 minutes, though, with scrum-half Kalani Thomas particularly lively around the fringes on his first start.

After Carlo Tizzano broke clear from Brandon Paenga-Amosa’s offload, the Wallabies ought to have scored in the corner, only for Tom Wright to fumble.

Williams finally notched the first points of the evening, a close-range try after Ireland coughed up yet another penalty on their own five-metre line. But as Wallabies head coach Les Kiss admitted later, they should have scored more with nearly 80 per cent possession up to that point.

The try stung Ireland into action and they hit back immediately with Stuart McCloskey spinning out of a tackle and putting Henshaw over. Timoney added a second after Kurtley Beale came off the bench for his first international appearance for five years at the age of 37, and promptly missed a tackle on the short side. Prendergast added a penalty on the stroke of half-time as Ireland went into the break 17-7 up, having been 7-0 down.

News.title: Italy edge out Fiji in Nations Championship at sparse Twickenham
News.content:
Italy clung on against Fiji to put the first point on the board for the northern hemisphere in Nations Championship finals weekend, although their entertaining 23-21 victory was played out to a quarter-full Allianz Stadium.

Perhaps that was no surprise given the timing of the kick-off: 4.40pm on a Friday.

But with only 32,000 tickets sold for Friday’s double-header – Ireland vs Australia takes place later in the evening – the sparse nature of the crowd has raised questions about the new format.

It was a shame there were so few fans packed in for this game, because it was a fun match to watch, as Fiji’s games often are.

Gonzalo Quesada’s Italy had lost to the same opposition 16-21 in Rome last weekend, and they entered this game the only team from either hemisphere not to have won a single Nations Championship match. But their 17-7 half-time lead thanks to tries from Federico Mori and Giacomo Nicotera was no more than they deserved. Fiji only made one entry into Italy’s 22m in the first half, although it did yield a try from Sale’s 6ft5in Ponepati Loganimasi, who was allowed to race home from the halfway line.

Fiji scored their second try from their second entry into Italy’s 22m, and it was another beauty, Jiuta Wainiqolo sucking in two defenders before offloading to Peniasi Dakuwaqa, who stepped inside Stephen Varney to score.

Fiji’s third was the best of the lot, 13 phases of wonderful offloading rugby before a Dakuwaqa grubber kick released Wainiqolo., who in turn managed to offload to Sawala to score.

That nudged Fiji 21-20 in front. But a late Tommaso Allan penalty put Italy back ahead, as Fiji opted to kick for the corner with a minute remaining rather than go for the posts.

Italy held on, Andrea Bocelli blasting out over the public address at full-time in front of 60,000 empty seats. First blood to the northern hemisphere.

News.title: Vaccine gaps fuelling global measles resurgence, WHO warns
News.content:
Measles is one of the most contagious viruses known to humans and requires 95 per cent of the community to be vaccinated to prevent outbreaks. Children under-five, pregnant women and people with weakened immune systems are at greatest risk.

According to the WHO, it can cause pneumonia, brain infection, deafness and blindness, death and “immune amnesia”, where the virus can weaken the immune system for months or even years.

The measles vaccine, which used a weakened (live attenuated) virus in two doses, is safe and highly effective.

Dr O’Brien said: “Some of the more recent graduates have never seen a case of measles, but it is back”.

Diana Chang Blanc, unit head of the essential programme on immunisation at the WHO, said the spread of cases across income levels showed that even in places with strong health systems, small drops in coverage can leave pockets of unvaccinated people that can spread risks far beyond those areas.

In 2025, 59 countries had “large or disruptive outbreaks”, defined as more than 20 cases per million people over 12 months. Of them, 11 were previously declared measles-free. The US was not among them, as its outbreaks didn’t reach the threshold.

“It can take years to regain elimination status, whereas it takes only a 12-month period to lose elimination status,” said Dr O’Brien. “These are hard-fought gains that countries have made, and protecting them now is more important than ever”.

News.title: Australia embarrassed by remarkable Overton spell
News.content:
So often English cricketers have left the “Gabbatoir” looking dazed and confused after yet another horror show. This time, it was an insipid Australian side’s turn to be embarrassed and overawed by a remarkable showing from Jamie Overton. It was a batting display as ugly as anything Australian cricket has served up in the sandpaper civil war, which rumbles on.

As Australia were bowled for a meagre 108, Overton recorded figures of five for 12, the second-best in T20 by an Englishman and the best by any man in T20 fixtures between these old rivals. That was Australia’s lowest T20 total against England since the sides’ first meeting, ahead of the 2005 Ashes, when they were bundled out for 79 chasing 180. Back then, T20 was a bit of fun, now it is big business, and this was altogether more chastening.

A combination of rain, which delayed play three times and led to a DLS-reduced target, and Riley Meredith, who was gifted three wickets, meant that England’s batting lacked the freewheeling fun of their bowling performance.

But the chase was a formality, and England won by seven wickets. The Gabba was just a third full, with some hardy Barmy Army types in fine voice as England celebrated their win. With England leading the five-match series 2-1, it is hard to imagine too many Aussies racing to buy tickets for the final two games in Sydney and Canberra. England are flying out Rehan Ahmed and the uncapped Glamorgan batsman Asa Tribe as they manage a long list of absentees, which will include the South Africa-bound captain Harry Brook and keeper Jordan Cox by Canberra.

News.title: Colombia earthquake triggers surge in malaria cases
News.content:
Cases of malaria in rural Colombia have surged after a devastating earthquake left towns and villages in ruins, according to local charities.

Colombia has recorded over 74,360 cases of malaria this year, 40 per cent of which have been concentrated in Chocó – the epicentre of the earthquake which struck in August, killing at least 335 people and injuring 4,500 more.

The region has seen a 46 per cent surge in cases of the mosquito-borne disease compared to last year, up from 23,757 cases in 2025 to 34,759 cases so far in 2026.

Malaria can be very serious at any age, but it is the most dangerous for young children under five. If left untreated, it can become a medical emergency in as little as 24 hours and result in death.

While Africa accounts for around 94 per cent of global malaria cases, an estimated half a million infections occur in South America every year, mostly in the countries surrounding the Amazon basin – Colombia, Brazil, and Venezuela.

The earthquake hit at 7.4 on the Richter scale and was the strongest Colombia has seen in a decade, destroying roads and buildings. It hit during the rainy season, and water has collected in and around destroyed buildings, allowing mosquitoes, which breed in stagnant water, to survive and multiply, according to Save the Children.

Following the earthquake, thousands of people in Chocó have moved into overcrowded and unsanitary shelters after their homes were destroyed, increasing the spread of infectious diseases including malaria – which is carried between people via infected mosquitoes.

“The earthquake has worsened the conditions that favour the transmission of malaria,” Maria Mercedes Liévano, Save the Children’s Country Director in Colombia, told The Telegraph.

“Because we’re now seeing collapsed and damaged homes, families that are sleeping in overcrowded conditions out in the open, and are dealing with a health network that is overwhelmed,” Ms Liévano added.

Sports.title: Project Lionesses: The blueprint for transforming British football with 2035 World Cup
Sports.content:
Winning the bid to host the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup will be a nailed on triumph for the UK women’s game, in what the Government is calling ‘a decade of change.’ Since the Lionesses roared to victory when England hosted the 2022 UEFA Women’s Euros, an additional 2.3 million UK women and girls have started playing the beautiful game.

The mere news that we will be the hosts in 2035 - our first World Cup on home turf since the men’s 1966 victory - will attract another one million female players in the run-up to the tournament. Then, especially if there’s a UK win, the possibilities, say Government sources, are endless. Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy says: “We are lighting up the world when it comes to women’s sport and we’re showing a whole generation of young girls, not just here in the UK, but right around the world, what is possible.

“It has got to be the moment where we say girls don’t just belong on any pitch they choose to play on, but they belong in the boardroom and they belong in the locker room as coaches.”

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 6 Images The Lionesses looking forward to the 2035 World Cup (Image: UEFA via Getty Images)

Sports Minister Stephanie Peacock adds: “Hosting the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2035 in the UK will be our catalyst to get more women and girls than ever before involved in sport - and that means shaping, as well as playing, the games we all love.”

The FA’s director of women’s football, Sue Day, also recognises the amazing progressive opportunities for women’s sport which will open up, thanks to winning the World Cup bid. She says: “Something so big and impactful can change perspective, and that’s the goal here. I appreciate it’s overused, but this is genuinely once in a lifetime, a once-in-a-generation opportunity.

“We need to collectively grasp this moment and think of it as a catalyst for growth, inspiration and something to springboard from.This can touch everyone in the country and show everyone that girls can do this, too, so for me it’s a DNA leveller.”

Financial experts are also predicting a boost to the economy of at least £1.9 billion, with 31,000 new jobs created. Scottish Football Association chief executive Ian Maxwell says winning the bid will see a positive investment in women’s football from here on in. He says: “The level of investment into coaching, facilities and player pathways in the years beforehand will shape the future of the game for the generations to come."

View 6 Images England legend Karen Carney "excited" by World Cup in 2035 (Image: Getty Images)

And players, past and present, agree that this is a life changing moment for the women’s game. England legend Karen Carney, 39, who is now a broadcaster, says: “It’s very exciting. We’ve got nine years to make it the best tournament to date. “Economically, visibility, legacy - it will be inspiring a generation. Every year, every tournament is getting better, so imagine what it will be like in nine years time.

“We will need so many roles for that tournament - in sponsorship, marketing, physios, CEOs, sport scientists, producers of TV shows. It’s amazing. My friend said it’s ‘project Lionesses.’ In nine years time, your little girl could play for the Lionesses. How incredible is that?”

And yet, 60 years ago, when Geoff Hurst scored the two goals in extra time that propelled England to a 4-2 win against West Germany at Wembley, women’s football was still officially banned in this country. Women weren’t even allowed to attend the winner’s banquet on the night of the final.

Yet, England’s greatest ever boss, Sir Alf Ramsey, would have been all for the women’s game, according to his biographer Grant Bage. He says: “Alf's focus was always football, and in professional contexts he judged other people on their football knowledge, enthusiasm and love of the game. Consequently, I have no doubt he would wholeheartedly have welcomed the Women's World Cup coming to the UK and admired how professional and competitive women's football has become.”

View 6 Images Wendy Bell, with her husband Derek, is delighted World Cup is coming to UK in 2035

And yet, there was barely a female face in sight in pictures of the legendary 1966 final. But Wendy Bell, now 76, was just 15 when she was lucky enough to go to the game with her dad, Geoffrey Jackson - albeit as a substitute for her brother, Tim, who had broken his leg. Despite her presence there being “accidental,” she says: “Looking back, it was one of the most memorable days of my life.

“We had seats near the royal box. When we got inside, there was a young police officer wearing his helmet and my dad asked him if we were going to sit down when the game started and he smiled - said he would.

“I’m so pleased the women’s World Cup is coming to the UK in 2035. What took so long? The Lionesses have done so much to promote women in sport in this country and around the world. think all women in England are so proud of what they achieved and let’s hope they can get the same result the men did in 1966.”

View 6 Images Michelle Agyemang so excited by 2035 World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

For Michelle Agyemang, 20 - who was made Young Player of the Tournament when England won the Euros in 2025 - playing in the first World Cup on home turf since 1966 could be a reality. She says: “To have the chance to play in a home World Cup would be a dream.

“Even more exciting is thinking about all the girls watching who might see 2035 and believe they can be part of it one day. “The thought of another generation growing up knowing that the biggest stage in the game is coming to their home country is amazing.”

Her team-mate, Erica Meg Parkinson, 18, who played in the recent qualifier for next year’s World Cup agrees. She says: “I think it’s ‘extra fuel’ for us players who are trying to make it through the pathway, knowing that we have something like that - so grand - to look forward to in the future.

“Historically, it has a big impact on a lot of players. It fuels you to really want to make it to the seniors even more - and to stay there because you can break through. But then you need to be at a top level for a decade to be able to play in that and to stay there. That’s really exciting and motivating.”

View 6 Images Respected historian Steve Bolton whose grandmother Lizzy Ashcroft was a trailblazing legend (Image: STEVE FINN PHOTOGRAPHY)

The grandson of one of England’s greatest ever women players, Lizzy Ashcroft,who played throughout the 1920s and 1930s, during the FA’s ban on women’s football - which was finally lifted in 1971 - says playing in the World Cup would have been a dream come true for her.

Steve Bolton says of his grandmother, who played for St Helens Ladies FC and Dick, Kerr Ladies: “Granny was one of the trailblazers and it’s thanks to her and her team-mates that paved the way for the success of the game now. She would have dreamed of playing in a women’s World Cup in England.” At least she helped make other football mad women’s dreams come true.

Sports.title: Man Utd boss's drastic action after Brentford match left stars gasping for breath
Sports.content:
Man Utd boss's drastic action after Brentford match left stars gasping for breath

A LOOK BACK: Manchester United take on Brentford this Saturday and Red Devils supporters will be hoping to avoid a repeat of their humiliating 4-0 loss under Erik ten Hag in 2022

View 2 Images Manchester United's players were put through their paces (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

It's considered by many to the be the worst result in Manchester United's Premier League history. On a sweltering hot West London evening in August 2022, the Red Devils found themselves 4-0 down by half-time against a Brentford side who'd only been in the top flight for one season.

‌



‌



Erik ten Hag had been in charge for even less time. It was just his second game in charge, having also tasted defeat at the hands of Brighton on the opening weekend.

‌



United managed not to concede in the second half, but the tale of that match wasn't all told by the full-time whistle. The next day, Ten Hag ordered his players back to Carrington and disciplined them the old fashioned way.

‌



After learning that Brentford's players had run a combined 13.8km more than his flops, the Dutchman demanded they all run that distance in 33-degree heat back up north. Ten Hag even took part in the gruelling exercise himself, matching his players step-for-step over eight-and-a-half miles.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Years later, it emerged that Cristiano Ronaldo only managed two of the three laps in another move that fractured the relationship between the United megastar and his boss. But other players were impressed by Ten Hag's commitment to the cause, even though it left all who participated shattered and gasping for breath.

‌



It worked in the short term, too. United bounced back from the Brentford loss to beat Liverpool 2-1 in their next outing, sparking a relatively successful season that included a third-place finish, Carabao Cup win and an FA Cup final appearance.

Perhaps Mauricio Pochettino will take a leaf out of Ten Hag's book if his side suffer the same fate at Old Trafford this Saturday. Coincidentally, it'll also be his second Premier League game since being appointed by the Red Devils.

‌



View 2 Images Erik ten Hag was furious with his players' lack of running (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

During his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon, Pochettino notably hit back at suggestions that he's become too nice. "Do not misunderstand my words," the Argentine set off.

‌



"Sometimes we are confusing two words that mean maybe something similar; nice and good. I am not nice. I am not nice. We have to be good. That is a different thing. I am not nice. I am trying to be good.

"We know when we need to push, when we need to be strong and when we need to build something to improve the atmosphere and relationship and everything. These two things are different."

Sports.content:
13 players could miss Man Utd vs Brentford as Mauricio Pochettino confirms major doubt

Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino and Brentford boss Keith Andrews both have several injury headaches ahead of the Premier League clash between their sides

Crisis-ridden Manchester United welcome high-flying Brentford to Old Trafford on Saturday, with the two teams having drastically different seasons in the Premier League. United are languishing in the relegation zone, winning just one of their 11 top-flight fixtures this term.

‌



‌



Mauricio Pochettino's reign got off to a wretched start with an eye-opening 4-0 defeat away to Liverpool. That was followed by a frustrating 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League which did little to improve the mood.

‌



Contrastingly, Brentford are sitting pretty in sixth place after Monday's 4-0 win at home to Everton. But one similarity between the sides are their injury problems.

‌



Mirror Football runs through who's set to miss Saturday's clash.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Man Utd

Having inherited an already injury-hit squad, the last thing that Pochettino needed was Bruno Fernandes picking up an issue in midweek. The United captain has been ill and his manager confirmed on Friday that he remains a doubt.

‌



"We don't know (if Fernandes can play)," Pochettino told a press conference. "He's affected by a virus from Portugal. He finished the game a little bit with a problem, and, today, he cannot be part of the training session. We'll see.

"We are going to see during the day and tomorrow, how he wakes up, and we'll see. We're not going to take any risks, because you know when this type of situation happens, you don't feel [you can]. We are going to pay attention but, still, we decide nothing."

Sports.title: 'Sir Alex Ferguson betrayed me - I put the phone down on him and we haven't spoken since'
Sports.content:
EXCLUSIVE: 'Sir Alex Ferguson betrayed me - I put the phone down on him and we haven't spoken since'

EXCLUSIVE: A former Premier League manager says his relationship with Sir Alex Ferguson has never been the same since the legendary Manchester United boss "betrayed" him

View 4 Images Neil Warnock has never forgive Sir Alex Ferguson for what he did (Image: Lewis Storey/Getty Images)

Neil Warnock has lifted the lid on his explosive falling out with Sir Alex Ferguson, revealing he slammed the phone down on the Manchester United icon after feeling "betrayed".

‌



‌



Nearly two decades on, the veteran boss insists the bad blood has never faded - and admits he has still not forgiven his old managerial rival.

‌



During the 2006/07 season, Warnock was living the dream at his boyhood club Sheffield United, having just ended the Blades' 12-year exile from the Premier League. But a fairytale campaign turned into a nightmare on the final day as United suffered a heartbreaking drop back to the Championship.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Man Utd identify Bruno Fernandes replacement after captain makes contract stance clear READ MORE :

Aston Villa make decision on Alejandro Garnacho as Unai Emery completes huge U-turn READ MORE :

To make matters worse, survival slipped through their fingers because Manchester United crashed to a 1-0 home defeat against West Ham. Had the Hammers lost at Old Trafford, Warnock's men would have stayed up. But with the title already wrapped up - and an FA Cup final against Chelsea to come - Ferguson fielded a heavily weakened team, and West Ham ruthlessly took advantage.

"Alex phoned me the next day and apologised and I just put the phone down. I can never forgive things like that. He let me down badly," Warnock said, speaking exclusively to Mirror Football on behalf of Famous Grouse, who have appointed the 77-year-old as their new 'Chief of Socks'.

‌



Asked whether the pair had previously been close, Warnock said: "Originally yes. I had a good relationship with him. He used to speak to every manager and would send messages when you got promoted etc. But I could never forgive him for that."

View 4 Images Neil Warnock's relationship with Sir Alex Ferguson has been non-existent since 2007 (Image: Getty)

‌



Warnock's fury wasn't reserved solely for Ferguson, either. West Ham's survival owed much to the controversial third-party ownership saga involving Argentine duo Carlos Tevez and Javier Mascherano, who stunned football by arriving at Upton Park in the summer of 2006.

Poetically - and painfully - it was Tevez who scored the winner at Old Trafford that ultimate sank the Blades. Despite breaching Premier League rules over the pair's signings, West Ham were hit with a £5.5million fine rather than a points deduction - leaving Warnock convinced the London club were let off the hook.

‌



"If it had been the other way around [Sheffield United signing Tevez and Mascherano], we'd have got done with points," he said. "It's not what you know, it's who you know. They got away with murder. I was quite pleased when they went down this year if I'm honest."

View 4 Images West Ham signed Carlos Tevez and Javier Mascherano in 2006 under controversial circumstances (Image: Getty)

‌



Warnock resigned as Sheffield United manager just days after relegation was confirmed, bringing an end to an eight-year spell in charge of the club. But the fallout didn't stop at the touchline, with the 77-year-old revealing the drop into the Championship cost him a massive seven-figure sum - and another cherished relationship, this time at boardroom level.

The Blades subsequently pursued a high-profile legal battle against West Ham over the Tevez-Mascherano affair, eventually securing a lucrative out-of-court compensation settlement. Warnock, however, claims he never saw a penny of the money - even though he was promised his survival bonus if the club won compensation.

‌



"I got stitched up for a million pounds if we'd have stayed up," he said. "My chairman [Terry Robinson] at Sheffield United told me, 'I'll look after you legally, we'll get that money for you.'

View 4 Images Neil Warnock - a licensed chiropodist -has been appointed Chief of Socks by Famous Grouse (Image: Famous Grouse / Happy Socks)

‌



"They went legally against West Ham and I think they got £25m. And I never got my money. And that's someone I knew for 20 years... to be let down by someone I trusted really disappointed me."

Warnock, who also managed Queens Park Rangers, Crystal Palace and Cardiff City in the top flight, remains one of English football's most outspoken and box-office characters. Across a remarkable career spanning five decades and 16 clubs from non-league to the Premier League, the Yorkshireman has secured a record-breaking eight promotions.

Article continues below

He is also the second-most experienced manager in the history of the sport with 2,003 matches in the dugout. Only Sir Alex Ferguson boasts more with 2,115 - a record Warnock would doubtless love to surpass, even if he still wouldn't answer the phone when Fergie rang to congratulate him.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta shows true colours with response to Man City charges question
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta shows true colours with response to Man City charges question

Manchester City could receive a record points deduction which would rule them out of the Premier League title race, but Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta doesn't want his team benefiting from any hands-outs

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is only focussed on Arsenal's affairs (Image: Hayters TV)

Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are determined to win the title on the pitch - and not rely on Manchester City being clobbered with a points deduction.

Arsenal face their arch rivals at the Emirates on Sunday with City still waiting for the outcome of their appeal against the Premier League charges and punishment. There is an expectation that City will get hit with a record points deduction which could see them relegated and several bookmakers have made them favourites for the drop as a result.

When asked whether Arsenal want to win the title on the pitch, Arteta said: "That's the only thing that we should put the energy and the focus on. There's nothing else."

Arteta also says he does not want the case to overshadow Sunday's showdown. "I hope that it doesn't because, as well, it's a process that is still open, it's not resolved and we don't know what is going to happen," he said.

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"So, no, I think when we have two teams at the level that both teams are at right now with the quality players that are on that pitch, it's a massive game and a big game to enjoy, I think."

City made a sensational start to the season which saw them win the first seven games in the Premier League. But they are now stuck in a rut with just one win from their last seven in all competitions.

That stark drop off in form has followed City being found guilty of the 115 Premier League charges and facing the prospect of a points deduction and record fine. City will be guaranteed another red-hot reception when they visit the Emirates on Sunday and yet Arteta says he is not sure whether the two things are linked.

Will Arsenal beat Manchester City? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 2 Images Manchester City's season could be ravaged by a points deduction (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Arteta added: "I don't know, that's a question for them. What I can see is when I watch them play, there's a lot of the games that they have to win, because this is football, to win games, and that's the way that they play, and what everyone else is doing.

"I don't think it’s in form or in performance. I think as well that they've been very, very unlucky with certain results."

Arteta is expected to have David Raya fit after the Spain keeper went off injured at Newcastle last weekend which also meant that he missed the draw with Borussia Dortmund. Arteta said he hopes Raya will be involved and added: "Every player has the same mindset; they want to be available, they want to be in the best possible condition, and there's no difference between them."

Sports.title: Man Utd trigger new Bruno Fernandes contract extension - but he could still leave this summer
Sports.content:
Man Utd trigger new Bruno Fernandes contract extension - but he could still leave this summer

Manchester United have used a club option to extend Bruno Fernandes' contract for a further year to avoid losing their influential captain for nothing in the summer

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes of Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have triggered an option in Bruno Fernandes' contract to extend the playmaker's terms by a further 12 months, it has emerged.

‌



‌



Fernandes, 32, was due to become a free agent at the end of this season, though United's actions mean that will now no longer be the case.

‌



But the Portugal international could theoretically still quit Old Trafford this summer after recently revealing he had put contract talks on ice following the latest managerial change at the club, with United currently in the relegation zone after a poor start to the season.

‌



Manchester Evening News have confirmed that United triggered their option to keep Fernandes on their books beyond this season and into 2028.

Should talks over a new contract fail to yield an agreement when they resume then it remains a possibility that Fernandes could still be sold in the summer transfer window, particularly if United receive substantial offers for their talisman.

It's understood Fernandes remains a player with plenty of admirers both within Europe and further afield. He was courted heavily by clubs from Saudi Arabia last summer and interest from the Middle East has not waned.

‌



Fernandes confirmed last week that he had been offered a new contract by United. "No, there's no negotiations ongoing," he told Sky Sports. "But I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years.

"If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

‌



View 2 Images Fernandes and United have put talks over a new contract on ice

"Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here. The thing is, I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club.

"And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it's time for me to move on, I will move on. I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Manchester United.

"They're going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, 'Bruno, it's time to part ways', I'm going to be the first one walking out the door."

He added: "We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games."

Sports.title: Tonda Eckert wants Spygate to be forgotten - but Southampton aren't helping him
Sports.content:
Tonda Eckert wants Spygate to be forgotten - but Southampton aren't helping him

Southampton face Middlesbrough in a Championship clash packed full of intrigue and backstory on Friday night at St Mary's Stadium following the bitter Spygate saga

View 3 Images Tonda Eckert faces Middlesbrough in a Spygate rematch (Image: Matt Watson/Southampton FC via Getty Images)

Tonda Eckert wants everyone to move on.

The Southampton boss has apologised, been punished and would prefer it if the Spygate saga was never mentioned again.

But with Middlesbrough in town on Friday for a mouth-watering clash at the top of the Championship, that was never going to happen.

Southampton have not shaken off the Spygate saga, which came to a conclusion in early October when the FA announced that Eckert had been fined £28,000 and given a suspended six-week ban from football to go with Saints' earlier four-point deduction from the EFL.

Eckert invited the Sky Sports cameras into his world this week for some soft-focus PR work, to emphasise the man behind the spying scandal. Southampton backed their manager, ignoring the calls to sack him over the summer before handing him a new contract last week, so they could do with his image being rehabilitated.

Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The humble words of Kim Hellberg this week helped their case, with the Boro boss saying he respects Eckert and considers it water under the bridge. "I will never hold a grudge against anyone in life, things will happen and you have to move on," Hellberg said.

It was therefore not the wisest move by Southampton to commission an influencer to voice over a provocative social media video to ramp up the tension ahead of the Middlesbrough game.

The video recalls Southampton's play-off campaign, their two-legged win over Boro and how success was "ours... until it wasn't". It notes that Boro "got another go" before Oli McBurnie's winner at Wembley for Hull. "People talk about last season, but we're focused on this one," the narrator says without a hint of irony.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 3 Images Southampton's video previewing the Middlesbrough game has ramped up the tension (Image: X/Southampton FC)

Eckert has conceded that "there will be a different emotion" inside St Mary's on Friday night as Saints face Boro for the first time since their not-so-subtle spying was uncovered and everything unravelled.

The truth is that the only way the German will effectively move on from the saga is by achieving the objective he was hired for. Southampton are sixth in the Championship table, seven points behind pace-setters Boro in a tight contest.

Having put their play-off final disappointment behind them, Boro have only lost twice this season in the league and, in Will Lankshear, have the Championship's best striker and top scorer. Spygate or no Spygate, they are currently the team Saints have to measure themselves against, with a trip to face second-placed Wolves on the horizon the following weekend.

View 3 Images Southampton have been exceptional at home this year (Image: Matt Watson/Southampton FC via Getty Images)

Southampton have been exceptional at home this season, taking 22 points from a possible 24. They have not lost at home since January. It is away from the south coast where they have struggled, taking two points from the last nine on the road, against West Brom, Preston and Sheffield United.

With Leo Scienza and Caspar Jander back in contention after injuries and top scorer Cyle Larin back among the ranks, Southampton have the players to inflict Boro's third defeat of the season.

Ultimately, it is only victories in such matches that will help Eckert clean his image and develop a new reputation. It was his underhand approach that cost them a shot at promotion last season - and it is on him to right his wrongs this time around, starting tonight.

Sports.title: What it's REALLY been like covering Man City's 115 charges and seeing through the lies
Sports.content:
Our colleagues at the Manchester Evening News are celebrating 12 months of providing brilliant Premium content for subscribers.

As part of their look back at the last 12 months, Manchester City correspondent Simon Bajkowski takes readers behind the scenes of covering what has become arguably the biggest story in Premier League history.

-----------

Going back a few years, as luck would have it I found myself in front of one of the most important characters in the Manchester City case and they were happy for me to ask a question on the condition that our conversation was strictly off the record. I asked, they answered, and subsequent developments have shown it to be a bare-faced lie.

‌



I had suspected it was at the time, which is why it never saw the light of day. But had I taken in good faith something in a situation where there was no reason for there to be bad faith and reported it - and it would have made for a decent story - I would have looked (even more) stupid down the line as yet another report to be completely and hopelessly wrong.

At another point, the word was out that the verdict was coming in the international break. It was the talk of the press box, broadcasters contacted me to try and confirm my availability for their programmes when the news dropped, and the BBC put together a four-part podcast appetiser on everything that has happened so far hosted by Clive Myrie so that they could dominate the market audience once the news broke.

Three Premier League clubs want Man City owners to be forced into sale after guilty verdict READ MORE :

Jamie Carragher thinks Erling Haaland could leave Man City very soon on one condition READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

I was going away on holiday, but with the amount of noise, I was asked to write a piece based on my best guess of the verdict. That was March 2025.

‌



Eighteen months later, the news finally dropped, there was nothing in my piece that could be used and even poor Clive Myrie couldn't be found because somebody else was hosting a podcast and on their app it starts with three minutes of a midnight news bulletin.

Eighteen months. 18. Not a day out or a week out or even a month out but more than a year wide of the mark, and we all just shrug our shoulders and move on, hoping the next information is not as embarrassingly bad.

These two stories are a large part of why I find covering the 115 case a thoroughly depressing exercise that nobody emerges from with an enhanced reputation. When people you would expect to be reliable aren't massively wide of the mark, they're deliberately lying to your face.

Journalism is about working with the information you get and trying to piece together as much of the full story as possible. That's harder when, for understandable reasons even if it isn't popular, the whole of the disciplinary process takes place behind closed doors and is confidential.

‌



View 3 Images The saga around Manchester City's charges is yet to be concluded (Image: 2026 CameraSport)

Nearly four years after the charges were first brought, and two years after the hearing, we are still in limbo wondering if the verdict of the independent commission will be deemed correct or - as so many other times already - completely wrong and in need of a radical rewrite. The judgment has to be trusted so this is no conspiracy theory, yet there have been so many concerns around process along the way that the complete overhaul that City believe should happen cannot be ruled out at this stage.

In short, nobody knows anything and until that changes I prefer to abstain from making strong statements about what City have or haven't done; others in the profession have not had such trouble, which will make for some about-turns if an appeal is successful. The 40-page document is damning but says that it should be read alongside appendices containing all the evidence that, inexplicably, haven't yet been published.

City are wrong to say they have irrefutable evidence to support their position when a three-person independent panel have indeed refuted it. However, it should be remembered that while their word should be respected, we still await a full picture of the evidence used to reach a verdict while the appendices remain unpublished.

‌



And what a world to be in, where appendices and an arbitration panel will decide the fate of the last 20 years of Premier League history. Everybody involved in bringing football to this position should take a moment to reflect on how absurd and rubbish it is for those who have played no part in it.

View 3 Images Man City were found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought about by the Premier League

As with the actual game on the pitch, how wild as well that such huge consequences will hinge on the outcome only. Lose the appeal and City's owners will be seen as everything wrong in football and the club could get a points deduction so big it will be relegated from the Premier League; win the appeal and City would have every right to ask for points to be added to this season's total as part of the reparations for the reputational damage they have suffered.

In many respects, people have already made their minds up anyway. A YouGov poll of 1,000 fans on the day the charges were announced in 2023 found that three in every four believe that City broke the rules, and that number should be even higher now that the verdict is in.

‌



So little is known about the expertise of the panel that have made the decision, and taken so long to make it, yet a prominent view across media is that City can only win their appeal on a technicality - or, in other words, the rules of the competition. And again, we know roughly when the appeal will take place but can't know what will be said and won't know the outcome until the next press release or leak randomly drops.

It is unedifying in every sense, and with so little information the pages and the airwaves have been filled with speculation. Nobody knows what could happen, but fans of at least five out of twenty clubs enjoy hearing how badly City could be punished.

When this is all done and dusted, whatever the outcome, there should be some serious reflection from everyone - starting with City's hierarchy. If it all goes wrong they will have deceived not just the Premier League but also Blues all around the world, preying on their loyalty to the club to form a blind defence of cooking the books on an enormous scale, and that would be a far bigger offence than what they look set to be punished for.

‌



Finally, football is about fans. If City are relegated through the divisions, their supporters will - as their recent song additions say - follow them down to League Two.

This should not be hard to understand, yet so many characterisations of City fans since the charges were announced have been so wide of the mark. If you are questioning why fans are still supporting the team - whether dressed as a banana or not - then football isn't for you and your opinion isn't worth anything however big a platform you have.

Sports.title: Wakefield to take on Sydney Roosters in World Club Challenge
Sports.content:
Super League champions Wakefield Trinity will face Sydney Roosters in the World Club Challenge at Headingley on February 19.

A maiden appearance in the match between the winners of Super League and the NRL is Wakefield's reward for an astonishing season, which culminated in their 23-10 Grand Final victory over Warrington Wolves at Old Trafford in October, just three years after relegation to the Championship.

Trinity will be looking to make it four straight wins for English clubs in this contest.

St Helens pipped Penrith in 2023 before Wigan and Hull KR recorded wins over Penrith and Brisbane Broncos respectively in 2024 and 2026.

Sports.title: Explosive Fury vs Klitschko canvas row revisited
Sports.content:
On this day in 2015 Tyson Fury scaled his Everest. He dethroned Wladimir Klitschko, the dominant heavyweight of that era, to win the unified WBO, IBF and WBA world heavyweight championships.

It was the goal Fury had targeted throughout his career. Klitschko had ruled the division for a decade and was selling out stadiums in Germany.

Fury travelled to Dusseldorf as the underdog but utterly confident he had the tools to unravel Klitschko.

However on the day of the fight, an explosive row at the Esprit Arena threatened to scuttle the whole event.

Image: Tyson Fury outboxed Wladimir Klitschko

Peter Fury, Tyson's uncle and then trainer, decided he wanted to inspect the ring in advance. Then they spotted something they hadn't expected. Feeling the canvas, they realised that the layers under it were spongy.

Tyson Fury climbed through the ropes to bounce on the balls of his feet on the canvas where he was due, a few hours later, to stage a remarkable win.

"No way you can fight on that," his father John Fury said.

"You know what they've done that for," the then heavyweight title challenger said, "so I can't move."

Speaking to the camera, Tyson Fury declared: "They must have half a foot deep of sponge on the canvas. It's like training on a beach on the sand. It's absolutely ridiculous and I can tell you now, Sky Sports viewers, there's no fight if that ring ain't sorted.

"I'm a mover and I move, that's the way I fight. I can't move in that ring."

Image: Tyson Fury celebrates his momentous 2015 title victory

History could have been very different. If he'd gone ahead with the fight, he could - probably would - have lost. He certainly wouldn't have been able to box in the way he did so successfully later that night.

"My fighter is not fighting in quicksand," his trainer Peter Fury declared at the time.

They undid the ring canvas to look underneath; there were two soft layers that they insisted had to be removed.

Vitali Klitschko, Wladimir's older brother and a fearsome former world heavyweight champion himself, was on hand to respond. He stood in the ring himself, towering over the top rope and glowering down at Fury's team on the floor of the arena.

Mick Hennessy, Fury's promoter, told him: "You're trying to control this but it's not in the interest of health and safety. So we need it sorted.

"Your ankle or your knee could go on this, it's too thick."

Vitali, a formidable advocate for his brother, argued fiercely, gesturing animatedly as he said: "Both fighters have the same conditions. Same gloves, same ring and you're unhappy always.

"Everything you say is excuses," he roared. "Do you want to fight or not?"

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking whilst attending the Las Vegas Grand Prix, Evander Holyfield backed Tyson Fury to defeat Anthony Joshua during their clash in December

Fury's team weren't bluffing though. They were prepared to walk away.

John Fury raged at Bernd Boente, Klitschko's manager, in a corridor at the arena. He told him directly: "The fight's off, forget about it." Then he stormed off.

He later said: "If they hadn't replaced it, there wouldn't have been a fight."

Fury's team got their way. The offending layers were removed and Fury did indeed use his footwork and mobile long-range boxing to defuse Klitschko, a dangerous puncher, so adept normally at controlling distance but who just couldn't pin down an inspired Fury.

That blazing row did change the course of the heavyweight division. It was an important element in a monumental victory for the Englishman. Fury became the dominant figure in the weight class. He was unable to meet Klitschko again in a rematch; struggling with depression, he stepped away from the sport.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury reveals the long history of his struggles with mental health which has seen him diagnosed with bipolar disorder and schizophrenia. 'TYSON FURY' premieres on Netflix on November 27th

But Fury's mental health improved and he was able to make a famous comeback. He cemented his legend against Deontay Wilder, becoming a two-time heavyweight world champion without losing a fight.

Now he has the chance to become a three-time champion when he fights his great rival Anthony Joshua for the first time with a vacant WBA title on the line.

That climactic fight is two weeks away as Fury looks to start the final chapter in a championship story that began 11 years ago today.

Sports.title: No Rodgers, no problem! Steelers shock Broncos after dramatic week
Sports.content:
It had been a week clouded by Aaron Rodgers and his explosive claims regarding head coach Mike McCarthy, but the Pittsburgh Steelers swatted at the storm to claim a shock 27-5 win over the Super Bowl-contending Denver Broncos on Black Friday.

Broncos quarterback Bo Nix endured a miserable afternoon as he surrendered two interceptions and a lost fumble that resulted in two defensive touchdowns for the Steelers.

Denver trailed 24-5 after a dire first half in which they were limited to just 58 yards of offense, becoming just the third team since 1991 to post fewer than 60 yards while conceding two defensive touchdowns over the first two quarters of a game.

TJ Watt scored with an end zone fumble recovery, Jalen Ramsey returned a Nix interception to the house and D.K. Metcalf recorded a touchdown catch before appearing to celebrate by holding up eight fingers in an apparent support of Rodgers.

The Broncos looked anything but a contender as they slumped to 8-3, while the Steelers distanced themselves from a reflection of turmoil to improve to 7-4 in their push for the playoffs.

The Rodgers saga had lingered as an unwelcome backdrop heading into the game after the four-time MVP quarterback was released this week in the wake of his sensational appearance on the Pat McAfee Show.

Rodgers had claimed that head coach McCarthy fell asleep in team meetings, rebuffed suggestions to connect better with Pittsburgh's defensive players and accidentally shouted "one, two, three, Packers!" at the end of a team talk against the Philadelphia Eagles, the latter of which McCarthy would admit as an embarrassing moment.

Rodgers was subsequently cut amid what is set to mark the final season of his NFL career, though the storyline resurfaced during the game as broadcaster Al Michaels read a supposed text from the 42-year-old in which he is said to have claimed the Steelers had "barred" him from the team facility after he was benched for Mason Rudolph.

Rudolph started in place of Rodgers for the first time since the incident as he went nine of 15 passing for 142 yards and a touchdown, while Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren combined for 117 yards on the ground.

Reflecting on their win after such an eventful week, Rudolph said: "We just sort of rallied around Coach McCarthy, and I think in a weird way, the adversity brought us brought us closer together.

"It was a lot. Sort of unprecedented - certainly like nothing I've ever been through, and probably the same for all of my team-mates.

"I'm just so proud of the way we turned the page from [Aaron Rodgers' release on] Wednesday, and the veteran leadership - the Cam Haywards, the Jalen Ramseys, the TJ Watts - they really led us forward."

Such was the story of their night that Denver failed to capitalise as their resulting drive ended in Wil Lutz missing a 53-yard field goal at the beginning of the fourth quarter.

Rudolph followed up by launching a downfield strike to Roman Wilson for 37 yards to set up Chris Boswell's 33-yard field goal for a 27-5 lead with 11.16 to play.

For so long defense has been the heartbeat of the Steelers operation, and it leapt to the occasion in the opening exchanges by way of TJ Watt as their stalwart edge rusher downed Nix's finger-slip fumble in the end zone for a deadlock-breaking touchdown in the first quarter.

Pittsburgh then forced a swift three-and-out to pave the way for Rudolph's 22-yard touchdown strike to Metcalf, who did outstandingly to haul in a back-pedalling catch while facing man coverage from star corner Pat Surtain II.

Denver turned to their own defense as a potential route back into the game when Alex Singleton stuffed Warren in the end zone for a safety, before Lutz and Boswell exchanged a pair of 44 and 47-yard field goals.

The Steelers then stretched their lead with a second defensive first-half touchdown when Ramsey turned a Nix interception into a 36-yard slaloming pick-six with 1.33 to play.

Sports.title: Dawson: Rashid is still England's No 1 white-ball spinner
Sports.content:
Liam Dawson insists Adil Rashid remains England's No 1 white-ball spinner - even though he has seemingly taken the Yorkshireman's place as first-choice pick in ODIs.

Stalwart Rashid, 38, has been left out of England's last six 50-over encounters - three in Pakistan and then three in Australia - with Dawson the frontline slow bowler for those games.

The duo form a potent pairing in T20 internationals, though, and bowled economically - and in Dawson's case prolifically, as he took 3-16 from three overs - in Brisbane on Friday as England took a 2-1 lead over Australia in the five-match series.

Image: Rashid played his 156th men's T20 international in Brisbane on Friday, putting him fifth on the all-time list of appearance makers in that format

Speaking ahead of Sunday's fourth fixture in Sydney (8.15am UK), Dawson, 36, said: "I'm not sure I've knocked him out [of the team] because it's all conditions dependent, but he's still England's best white-ball spinner, without doubt," he said.

"I wouldn't look too far into what's happened on this trip, or in Pakistan before that. He'll certainly come good again because he's a world-class performer."

On his own ascent into a key player for England, Dawson said: "Having the backing of [captain Harry Brook] for the past 18 months, and to play as much as I have, has been brilliant. I've really enjoyed it and hopefully I can carry on and keep performing.

Image: Dawson (left) toom 3-16 at The Gabba, including two wickets in the powerplay

"It's obviously nice but I'm very realistic from a personal point of view. I know how good Rash is, everybody in world cricket knows how good he is."

'Ahmed has a fantastic attitude'

Dawson also hailed two more England spinners, in Sussex's James Coles, who made his debut against Australia in this T20 series, and Rehan Ahmed, who has been added to the squad for the final two fixtures following Will Jacks' trip ending early due to a broken hand.

The Hampshire bowler added: "Colesy has done so well for someone so young, I think people forget that, and he's got a hell of a lot of cricket ahead of him.

Image: Leg-spinning all-rounder Rehan Ahmed has been added to England's squad for the final two T20s in Australia

"Rehan's a great lad, I've known him a couple of years now and he's one of the hardest workers - always wants to bat, always wants to bowl, always wants to field. He's got a fantastic attitude.

"I've played a lot of cricket and I'm a lot older than those guys so I'll chat to them in training.

"You've always got to find your own way as well, work it out a little bit, but I'm very happy to speak to them both and help, of course."

Sports.title: Price out in Players Championship Finals first round in night of upsets
Sports.content:
Three of darts' biggest names were subject to shock upsets in the Players Championship Finals as Grand Slam champion Gerwyn Price, World No 2 Gian Van Veen, and No 1 seed Wessel Nijman were all knocked out in the first round at Minehead.

Price was beaten by 6-4 Sebastian Bialecki - the first time the Pole had beaten the Welshman in his career - while Jeffery de Graaf won two legs on the bounce to consign van Veen to defeat by the same scoreline.

Nijman was upset by 20-year-old Henry Coates despite posting an average of 110 - the second-highest average in Players Championship Finals history.

Image: Luke Humphries recorded a routine win against Darryl Pilgrim

World No 4 Luke Humphries, meanwhile, battled through his recurring back injury to secure a routine 6-3 victory against Darryl Pilgrim, while Michael van Gerwen withstood Connor Scutt to secure safe passage with a 6-3 first-round win of his own.

Beau Greaves also progressed to the second round with a scrappy 6-3 victory against former Lakeside champion Christian Kist despite a mediocre average of 89.64, and will face Rob Owen in the next round.

Van Veen, Nijman and Price joined James Wade, Gary Anderson, and Rob Cross as six of the top 25 players in the world were eliminated at the first opportunity in the last major before the World Darts Championship, which is live on Sky Sports from December 11th.

Wade was beaten 6-4 by Justin Hood and 2014 winner Anderson slipped to a 6-4 loss against Karel Sedlacek, while Cross fell to a thrilling 6-5 loss to Mickey Mansell.

Top players crumble on night of shock Minehead results

Image: Gian van Veen lost in the first round of the match to Jeffrey de Graaf

Van Veen - who finished runner-up to Price at the Grand Slam - struggled from the outset and throughout his match, managing only one maximum and checking out a lowly 15% of his finishes.

The Dutchman had three darts at double 16 to keep himself in the tournament, but failed to level the scores at 5-5 before de Graaf ruthlessly produced a 112 checkout to produce the first upset of the round.

Price, fresh off his first major win in four years after three successive final defeats, was heavily favoured against 22-year-old Bialecki, and looked to have rediscovered his tournament-winning form at the perfect moment when he produced a stunning 120 checkout to peg the deficit back to 5-4.

Image: Michael van Gerwen is into the next round

But Bialecki kept his cool and threw for the match, claiming his first career win against Price at the seventh attempt. The Pole will face off against de Graaf in round two.

The status quo was somewhat restored when Humphries and van Gerwen produced characteristically routine wins against lower-ranked opponents, with Humphries silencing doubters by averaging 93.32 in a week dominated by coverage of his injury.

Image: Stephen Bunting won a last-leg thriller against Max Hopp

But the show was stolen by Coates. The Derby native overcame his opponent's stellar average by notching an incredible 85.71% checkout success rate to claim victory in only his fourth-ever televised game.

Elsewhere, Stephen Bunting edged into the next round after beating German Max Hopp in a last-leg decider, while Kevin Doets averaged 107.34 in his win over Ritchie Edhouse and Chris Dobey came from behind to beat Mike De Decker 6-4.
