Sports.title: Audi loses F1 appeal over Tsunoda’s Italian GP restart – here’s why
Sports.content:
More than two months after the Formula 1 race at Monza, the result of the Italian Grand Prix has finally been confirmed.

Audi believed that Racing Bulls driver Yuki Tsunoda – who was given the opportunity to stand in following Isack Hadjar's wrist injury and Liam Lawson's subsequent promotion – deserved a penalty for a potential restart infringement.

Following Charles Leclerc's heavy crash, there was a standing restart at the Temple of Speed, with Tsunoda initially heading towards the left side of the grid and therefore the wrong grid spot. After a late manoeuvre towards his actual grid spot, an extra formation lap followed.

The sporting regulations stipulate that a driver who caused an extra formation lap must start from the end of the pitlane. Failure to do so could result in the offence being punished with a stop-and-go penalty. In Tsunoda's case, he started from the grid as normal, but the stewards decided to take no further action over the incident after the race.

It was enough for Audi to challenge the matter at the International Court of Appeal (ICA). Gabriel Bortoleto and Nico Hulkenberg finished 11th and 12th behind Tsunoda at Monza, and given the battle with Haas for seventh place in the constructors' championship, any additional point would have been welcomed.

However, Audi will not gain that extra point from the Monza race. During the race weekend in Qatar, the International Court of Appeal announced that while Audi's initial request to appeal was deemed “admissible”, the appeal itself was subsequently “dismissed on the merits”.

Yuki Tsunoda, Racing Bulls Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

The full explanation of this decision will take longer to arrive. In the interests of expediency, the ICA always communicates its decision first, with the full reasoning only being released at a later stage.

The ICA simply refers back to the FIA's original decision (document 69), which is still deemed valid. In that document, the stewards accepted Racing Bulls' defence and added that Tsunoda could not have known at the time that he was being considered the cause of the extra formation lap:

“Further, Article B5.9.4 goes on to specify that if a driver who causes the extra formation lap and is then able to start the extra formation lap, he must enter the Pit Lane at the end of the lap and start from the Pit Lane. It is only then, if the driver fails to do this, that the mandatory penalty of a Stop and Go penalty is imposed.

“In other words, the penalty is for failing to come into the Pit Lane and start from there. The penalty is not for causing the extra formation lap, if indeed, he caused the extra formation lap in the first place.

“A critical issue emerges here, in that in order to comply with the requirement to enter and start from the Pit Lane, a driver would need to know that he was the cause of the extra formation lap. The team representative quoted situations where extra formation laps have been commenced due to extraneous circumstances such as the position of a photographer etc. In this case, no message was sent to the team or the driver, advising them that they were the cause of the extra formation lap.

“The team, based on the fact that the car was positioned within its starting grid box in compliance with the regulations, had, in our determination, no reason to instruct its driver to enter and start from the Pit Lane.

“Accordingly, irrespective of whether or not the driver directly caused the extra formation lap, the team and driver were unaware that they were being considered as the cause, therefore we determine that we are unable to impose a Stop and Go penalty in this case, and decide to take no further action.”

Sports.title: FIA details F1 engine freeze and imposes testing restrictions ahead of V8 return
Sports.content:
Formula 1 manufacturers will no longer be allowed to work on the current generation of power units from mid-2028, the FIA's single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis has revealed in an exclusive interview with Autosport.

First revealed by Autosport over the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend, the measure is intended to prevent manufacturers from having to work on two projects simultaneously and also to prevent some from gaining an advantage. For the same reasons, work on the upcoming V8 engines is largely prohibited until that same point in time.

In practice, this means that development of the current hybrid V6 power units will be frozen from the 13th race of the 2028 season. From that point onwards, only reliability updates will be permitted, with no further performance upgrades allowed.

Prior to that point, restrictions will be in place on the development of the 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 for 2030. Until 1 October 2027, F1 manufacturers will not be allowed to carry out dyno work with a single cylinder, while no dyno work with the full power unit – in other words, the entire V8 – will be permitted until 1 July 2028.

These restrictions do not apply to newcomers, meaning General Motors will be allowed to carry out simulation work for their Cadillac power unit earlier.

The date of 1 July 2028 roughly coincides with the 13th race of that year, and therefore with the engine freeze for the current power units. In this way, the FIA is preventing manufacturers from having to work on two projects simultaneously, which would result in high costs and a development race spiralling out of control.

The governing body also wants to prevent a situation in which one manufacturer – such as Honda – is still significantly behind when the freeze comes into effect. This is closely linked to the ADUO rethink that is deemed necessary in the paddock, although according to Tombazis, no final decision has yet been made on that front.

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

“We've been concentrating on the PU framework and, frankly speaking, we are a bit late on the ADUO side,” Tombazis told Autosport.

“We need to consider this whole topic in relation to our intention and what we've discussed with the PU manufacturers, so to freeze the current generation of engines from a certain point onwards. That will be mid-2028. What we want to avoid for cost reasons is that they have two parallel programs.”

There is also another reason for the engine freeze: without these restrictions, a manufacturer with a highly competitive power unit under the current ruleset would be able to shift its focus to 2030 earlier than a manufacturer that is lagging behind and needs to pull out all the stops to make its current engine more competitive.

“What we also want to avoid is that some of the current PU manufacturers may get a significant advantage if they are very competitive at the moment. They can stop earlier and then others who may be chasing may have a disadvantage,” Tombazis said.

“So, we have this topic to address and all of that is related to ADUO as a discussion point. And therefore, we need to just pause and think carefully of what we do.”

The engine freeze has been confirmed and agreed with all parties involved, but the next step is to establish the changes to ADUO and ensure that no manufacturer is still facing a huge deficit in mid-2028 that can no longer be made up once the freeze comes into effect.

“Clearly, we need to give the opportunity for as much convergence as possible before that time. We don't want somebody to be frozen and to be way down,” Tombazis continued.

“So, we have these topics to address which are related to ADUO and there are some delicate matters that we need to basically assess before we move forward.”

Sports.title: F1 Qatar GP: Antonelli leads Russell in opening practice
Sports.content:
Newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli has comfortably topped first practice at Formula 1's Qatar Grand Prix, holding off Mercedes team-mate George Russell as drivers grappled with the tricky Lusail circuit.

One week on from the high-speed drag race on the streets of Las Vegas, drivers and teams were facing a completely different challenge as they sampled the high downforce motorcycle track of Lusail.

In the opening stages of the first hour of practice on the smooth swoops of the Doha track, they deployed both Pirelli's medium and hard tyre compounds to get the lay of the land and gather data.

This year's world champion Antonelli led all the way through, setting an early benchmark of 1m24.057s on mediums and then gradually chipping away on subsequent run, establishing a 1m23.217s lap after 20-odd minutes to head Mercedes team-mate Russell by seven tenths.

The Mercedes pair led the cars of Red Bull, McLaren and Ferrari as they populated the leaderboard two by two, until teams started switching to the soft-tyre compound at the halfway point.

But despite deploying the softer and faster tyre compounds, Antonelli's early benchmark proved tough to topple. Russell, who was experimenting with different wing configurations, came short by half a second, while Antonelli also couldn't touch his own medium-tyre lap as the Lusail surface became littered with gravel from the many off-track excursions.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Photo by: Karim Jaafar / AFP via Getty Images

In the Red Bull Isack Hadjar set third, 0.661 in arrears, followed by a nervous looking pair of McLaren cars in the hands of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri, who both conceded eight tenths, and Las Vegas winner Max Verstappen.

Ferrari was the fourth-fastest team after a muted session, with Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton over 1.2s adrift from Antonelli after grappling with massive front tyre degradation.

Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad led the midfield aboard the VCARB 03, with Alpine's Pierre Gasly rounding out the top 10.

Sports.title: Formula 1 planning new engine development freeze before 2030 rules change | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 intends to freeze power unit development again before introducing its new engine regulations in 2030.

Engine development was previously frozen between 2022 and 2025 before the current power unit rules were introduced this year. Dissatisfaction with the new V6 turbo hybrids led the FIA, Formula One Management and the teams to unanimously agree to replace them in 2030.

The series intends to introduce V8 turbo hybrid power units which generate a much greater proportion of their total energy from the internal combustion engine. Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies said the decision to hasten the replacement of the current power units was “probably one of the unique moments in the last five, 10 or 15 years that we pretty much all agreed on a direction.”

“It was very much pushed by the FIA,” he said, “but all the teams have been finding their way into the regulations and I think we’re all quite excited to go to it.”

In order to spare manufacturers the cost of simultaneously developing the current power units as well as the forthcoming ones, a freeze is planned for the final season under the current regulations, which is already a little over two years away. Mekies said the FIA plans to permit limited types of development work on the new power units before then.

“In terms of transition, it’s something that is part of the framework we have discussed,” he said. “The transition proposed has a current engine freeze for 2029. Then there are some dates in place into the framework before which you cannot start working on the V8, both in terms of single-cylinder work and in terms of complete V8 work.

“So that’s very much made in such a way that you minimise the difficult transition decisions that all the teams will have to take otherwise between, say, the 2028 or the 2029 campaign and the 2030 campaign. So that has been, at the moment, pre-set into these regulations.

“I’m sure it will need refinement and there will be many, many loops of refinement. But the big principle to ensure the basics that you are talking about are in it.”

Sports.title: Vowles explains why Williams exceeded F1’s cost cap by £627,000 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Williams has become the second Formula 1 team to over-spend under the cost cap introduced five years ago.

The team has accepted it spent £627,000 more than it was allowed to during 2025, exceeding the cost cap by 0.48%. The FIA announced the team has been fined – but did not declare how much it was fined by – and given a 1.5% reduction in the amount of aerodynamic testing time it is permitted next year.

In comparison, Red Bull exceeded the budget cap by £1.86 million – 1.6% – in 2021. They were fined £6,059,092 and given a 10% reduction in their CFD allocation.

Vowles said Williams breached the gap because it incurred costs he expected would not count towards the cap while restructuring its business.

“The background to it is that the company structure of Williams was largely unchanged from 1977 and wasn’t really fit for purpose in a modern world,” he said. “We went into it with every intention of being open and transparent with the FIA, which is what we held all the way throughout, but believed those costs, because it’s company restructuring, not to be a cost cap expense.

“It was the company restructuring that put us over, and as you saw, put us over by £600,000 in that circumstance. The FIA themselves have noted we haven’t had any financial benefit from it, no sporting benefit as a result of it. And you can see that the penalty is pretty much adjusted to be in line with that as well at the same time.

“But it was our interpretation that those costs are out of cap. The FIA’s interpretation of it is that they are in cap. And obviously, we went with the FIA’s interpretation after much discussion.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The change which led to the overspend was a one-off adjustment, said Vowles. “You don’t restructure your company every year,” he said. “Ideally, you do it one-off.”

Williams has been in discussions with the FIA about the breach for around a month. “They approached us and let us know that there was a potential overspend,” he said.

“I have to say the FIA have been very good throughout. I think they have a terribly difficult job of adjudicating this, not just us, up and down the grid as a result of it.

“And yes, as I said, we went into it really with every belief that what we were doing was compliant with the cost cap. We put our hands up and go, fine, it’s an overspend. We’ll accept it.”

Vowles has criticised F1’s cost cap in recent months, arguing it makes it difficult for midfield teams to make the investment needed to improve their systems and catch the front runners. He said Williams’s overspend was “nothing to do with what I’ve been talking about.”

“That was very much that I think the sport would benefit from a closing up as a result of things. What you can see, though, is we are right on the knife edge.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“I’m just trying to do basic things like restructure a company, which, up and down the grid, by the way, this structure is pretty much the norm. The difference is I’m trying to do it in a cost cap now as a result of it.

“So, I think it reinforces the message that we’re on the back foot here a little bit, and this is hurting.”

Sports.title: F1’s ‘NASCAR-style’ racing at Las Vegas won’t disappear in 2027, say teams | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The extreme ‘yo-yo racing’ seen in Las Vegas will remain a feature at some tracks despite next year’s rules changes, team principals believe.

Multiple factors combined to produce over 350 exchanges of position during last weekend’s race: the low energy harvesting limit applied at Las Vegas, Overtake Mode, the power of the slipstream and the low track temperatures.

New rules for next year will slightly decrease the power of F1 cars’ electrical systems compared to their internal combustion engines. However team principals suspect tracks like Las Vegas, where drivers have limited opportunities to generate electrical energy, will still see frequent swaps of position.

“Vegas is more complicated than just energy,” said Williams team principal James Vowles. “What was really happening there is the tyres definitely were below their temperature window and we could push absolutely flat-out. In fact, you gained a benefit by being in the tow of someone else, and your surface temperatures just came up a little bit more.

“There’s a second effect, which is these regulations, once you have a build-up of cars, almost like NASCAR, you’ve actually got quite a powerful tow effect once you’re the fourth, sixth, seventh car in that whole sequence. So I wouldn’t focus too much on the energy starvation.

“I think actually there are other factors that came in there together at the same time. I don’t think next year’s regulations – this is now personal opinion, looking at sims – are going to kill what happened if we can recreate those circumstances.”

After the race Lando Norris pointed out drivers often swapped positions because of differences in their power deployment patterns. “Some overtakes weren’t overtakes,” the McLaren driver pointed out.

Vowles said the Las Vegas Grand Prix was “great racing.”

“I know there’s controversy around it. I thought it was absolutely fantastic. I was listening in to what Max [Verstappen] and the team were talking about, and they were thinking ahead to how do we do a chess play in the last lap, same as what Carlos [Sainz] was doing at the same time. That, for me, is extraordinary.

Several drivers pointed out they deliberately slowed down before reaching the detection point for Overtake Mode at times in order to ensure they passed through it after the car ahead of them and gained the subsequent power boost. However Vowles claimed they were “pushing to the absolute limit.”

“It really was qualifying laps and [they were] still able to think about how we’re going to fight each other on the last dying metres of a track,” he said.

Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies said the fact teams will be able to generate more power from their internal combustion engines next year won’t alter the nature of the racing at tracks like Las Vegas.

“Technically, we don’t think the 5% increase in fuel flow will change the nature of what is giving the nice battles in the race,” he said. “So we think you will still have those nice gaming possibilities with energy management.

“But we will hopefully and pretty much surely move a little bit closer to flat-out qualifying or to flat-out racing. Then in 2028, there is another step in the same direction, same thing.

“I don’t think it will remove the increased battles that we have been seeing this year, which most of us enjoy. But it will again move the balance towards flat-out racing.”

Sports.title: “Not worth thinking about” being able to beat Mercedes even with new floor – Norris | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lando Norris says Mercedes are too quick for McLaren to be able to compete with them in this weekend’s Qatar Grand Prix.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli lapped four tenths of a second faster than Norris in second practice. However Antonelli set his quickest time on the medium compound tyres and had to abandon his later lap on the softs.

Norris says McLaren are in good shape compared to the rest of the competition but Mercedes are comfortably ahead of the field.

“It depends how you want to look at it,” he said. “I don’t think we’re too bad relative to most, but to Mercedes, I don’t think we’ve been further off.

“They just seem in a different category compared to us today. Quicker in every single corner by a mile.

“I would say the battle’s for [third] and we seem in relatively decent position. We seem similar in pace to Red Bull and similar-ish to Ferrari. So I would say there’s things we need to improve and things that can certainly be better but I guess you always look to the top. So when you look at ourselves compared to the Mercedes we need to improve a lot everywhere.”

McLaren did not run their latest floor specification in practice due to concerns over potentially damaging it on Losail’s punishing kerbs. But Norris doubts they will be significantly closer to Mercedes when they fit the new floor again tomorrow.

“I don’t know how much that will help around here relative to Vegas and other things but I’ll see tonight and see how much we can gain from that,” he said.

“It’s not going to be the gap that we need. I would say we’re around six or seven tenths – probably seven tenths off the Mercedes a lap. So it’s not even worth thinking about them.

“I think relative to the rest, we seem like in a good place. The fact that we can have the new floor on tomorrow will add a little bit, but a little bit is always better than nothing, so we seem in a relatively decent place.”

Sports.title: Antonelli leads another Mercedes one-two despite red flag interruptions | Formula 1
Sports.content:
For the second practice session in a row, Andrea Kimi Antonelli topped the times despite setting his best lap on the mediums compound tyres.

He and several of his rivals had to abandon their flying laps on soft rubber due to a pair of red flags.

Antonelli exchanged quickest times with team mate George Russell early in the session on the medium tyre compound. He set his quickest time on 1’23.077 on his seventh lap.

The Red Bull drivers were unable to improve their times when they switched to the soft rubber. The McLaren pair did lap quicker but were unable to beat the two Mercedes drivers.

Russell began his first run on the soft rubber strongly, setting the quickest times through the first two seconds. As he approached the final corner he looked set to take the fastest time, but he had to back off as race control threw a red flag.

The session was interrupted to allow marshals to clear away gravel and a piece of debris left when Charles Leclerc had a dramatic spin at turn seven. That forced the Ferrari driver to pit for floor repairs.

Soon after the session restart, Antonelli took to the track on a set of soft tyres. But in a repeat of what happened to his team mate, the red flags flew as he neared the end of his lap.

This time Pierre Gasly was responsible. The Alpine driver dropped his left-hand wheels into the gravel at the exit of turn 14 and lost control, spinning into a gravel trap from which he never emerged.

That put paid to Antonelli’s hopes of improving his lap time, but nor was any other driver able to do better. He therefore ended the session on top, followed by his team mate and the two McLarens.

Max Verstappen, fifth fastest, was unimpressed to be overtaken by Lewis Hamilton as he began one lap. “You saw that under braking?” he asked his team. “My God.” Verstappen had overtaken Hamilton approaching the finishing line moments earlier. The stewards chose not to investigate the incident.

Hamilton ended the session eighth-fastest behind his team mate. However the Ferrari driver suffered a power unit problem shortly before the chequered flag appeared.

The two Racing Bull drivers made it five consecutive pairs of team mates in the top 10, Liam Lawson ahead of Arvid Lindblad.

Despite his spin, Gasly set the 12th fastest time behind Gabriel Bortoleto. Franco Colapinto took 15th after a near-missed with Carlos Sainz Jnr at turn one.

Sports.title: Court of Appeal rejects Audi’s call for Tsunoda penalty in Italian Grand Prix | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The International Court of Appeal has rejected Audi’s attempt to have a penalty applied to Yuki Tsunoda in the Italian Grand Prix.

Audi argued the Racing Bulls driver should have received a stop-and-go penalty for causing an aborted start.

The ICA upheld the stewards’ decision not to penalise Tsunoda.

Audi brought the case after Gabriel Bortoleto finished 11th behind Tsunoda in the Italian Grand Prix. The original start of the race was abandoned and an extra formation lap ordered by the race director and the stewards noted Tsunoda had not lined up in his grid box correctly.

However the stewards ruled Tsunoda’s position in his grid box was not the cause of the extra formation lap, meaning he should not receive a penalty. Audi contested the decision and Bortoleto said they had a “straightforward” case against the Racing Bulls driver.

The FIA is yet to issue the full reasoning for the ICA’s decision to uphold the stewards’ original decision.

Tsunoda made the second of his three appearances for Racing Bulls at the Italian Grand Prix. His 10th place finish was the only point he scored during his stint substituting for Liam Lawson.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

This is the second decision by the ICA concerned a grand prix this year. In September the ICA overturned a decision by the stewards of the Monaco Grand Prix and re-applied two penalties to Pierre Gasly, dropping him from third place to seventh.

FIA statement on ICA’s decision

The following hearing of the International Court of Appeal took place on 25 November 2026 in Paris: Hearing A Case ICA-2016-14: Appeal lodged by Audi Revolut F1 Team against Decision No. 69 of the Stewards of the 2026 Italian Grand Prix, dated 6 September 2026, counting towards the 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship. On 6 September 2026, at the end of the formation lap during the race restart following a red flag, the Race Director ordered an additional formation lap. Following the race, the Stewards investigated a potential breach of Article B5.9.4 of the 2026 FIA Formula 1 Sporting Regulations by Mr Yuki Tsunoda (Driver of Car No. 22), which requires any driver who caused an extra formation lap to start from the end of the pit lane. Failure to do so, a Stop-and-Go penalty should be imposed on the Driver. In Decision No. 69, the Stewards decided to take no further action against Mr Yuki Tsunoda. On 9 September 2026, Audi Revolut F1 Team lodged an appeal against that decision, arguing that Mr Yuki Tsunoda had caused the extra formation lap and should therefore have received the prescribed Stop-and-Go penalty.

Decision of the International Court of Appeal The Court, after having heard the parties and examined their submissions, decided to: – declare the appeal admissible; – dismiss the appeal on the merits; – uphold the Decision No. 69 of the Stewards of the 2026 Italian Grand Prix, dated 6 September 2026, counting towards the 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship; – and order the competent Sporting Authority to draw, as appropriate, the consequences of this ruling. The International Court of Appeal was presided over by Mr Laurent Anselmi (Monaco), and included, Mr Mark Kletter (Austria), Mr Philip Moser (United Kingdom) and Mr Laurent Nuss (France). Sports.title: Bam Rodriguez Could Lose Naoya Inoue Payday Over Hearn Purse Demands
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn sounds like he is expecting Fort Knox money for Jesse “Bam” Rodriguez to fight Naoya Inoue in Japan next spring, and it could end up costing his fighter the biggest payday of his career.

During a media roundtable on Friday, Hearn revealed that Matchroom had gotten an offer for ‘Bam’ Rodriguez to fight undisputed super bantamweight champion Inoue. Hearn turned it down as “not close” and said the two top pound for pound fighters need to be rewarded.

“We received an offer which wasn’t enough,” Hearn said to The Ring. “We’ve gone back, and now hopefully we will be negotiating to the point where that fight gets made. I think it’s the best fight in boxing, but Bam is making a lot of money in his weight class, and this could be No. 1 vs. No. 2 pound-for-pound or 1 vs. 3. These guys have got to be rewarded.”

Hearn’s focus on pound for pound lists as a reason to hold out for a better financial deal for Rodriguez ignores the huge difference in accomplishments and star power between Inoue and his fighter.

Inoue is a four division world champion and a two weight undisputed king who sells out the Tokyo Dome and brings in massive purses. In Japan, he is a massive superstar. In contrast, Rodriguez (24-0, 17 KOs) isn’t a national superstar. He’s got a following in Arizona and Texas, but he’s not a star throughout the U.S. His fights on DAZN do not move the needle with casual fans, and he’s failed to gain a following like the one Ryan Garcia has, who has accomplished far less.

If Hearn blows this deal with his clumsy approach to negotiations, it’s going to leave Bam with few options for good fights that can bring in anywhere near the same kind of money. Unless Bam moves up to a live division like lightweight, he could be stuck where he is at career and paycheck wise.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Needs WBA Belt for 400% Ryan Garcia Payday
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez has no interest in fighting Jack Catterall right now, and his manager Keith Connolly basically admitted the WBA welterweight belt is only useful for getting more cash out of WBC champion Ryan Garcia. Connolly traded comments with Catterall on X and let it slip that Lopez makes “roughly 400% more” in a unification fight with Garcia on February 6 than if he is without the belt. Teofimo needs that belt because without it, he is negotiating in a position of weakness with Ryan.

That tells you everything you need to know about what is really going on here, and why the WBA strap has not been vacated. Lopez (23-2, 13 KOs) is coming off a razor-thin 12-round majority decision over Rolando ‘Rolly’ Romero in August after getting completely dominated 12-0 by Shakur Stevenson earlier this year in January. He has no business asking Ryan Garcia (26-2, 21 KOs) for a 50-50 purse split even with that WBA strap around his waist, because Garcia brings all the ticket sales and PPV buys to the table. He is the money man in the welterweight division. If Garcia gives Lopez parity just to get the fight signed, he is making a big mistake when Lopez has nowhere else to go for real money.

Catterall (33-2, 14 KOs) called out Lopez’s whole game on X. “Lopez coming off a 12 zip loss and got rewarded with a title shot that belonged to me. The mandatory is due and all this going to court shit to avoid it is absolutely pathetic. If you want to fight Ryan go ahead but it shouldn’t be and won’t be for the @WBABoxing title !!!”

Connolly then posted a reply to Catterall with the money excuse. “Jack you’re a great fighter and a great person but we are looking to do a fight where Teo makes roughly 400% more it’s a unification and legacy wise a bigger fight so to act like we are afraid to fight you is disingenuous. We fought Loma & Shakur”

Eddie Hearn says Catterall is finished waiting around and will not take step-aside money before next week’s purse bid. “I get the other team, they want to do a unification, but guess what? Tough.” Hearn added, “Jack don’t want to do that. Jack’s been messed around for too long.” His message to the WBA made it clear what he wants: “Give the man either the championship or the fight.”

Hearn added that he expects Lopez to vacate the belt rather than risk getting outboxed by Catterall. They have Conah Walker lined up as a possible replacement if he beats Alexis Rocha on December 5. Hearn sees it this way: Lopez either fights his mandatory or walks into the Garcia negotiations empty-handed.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Campaigning to Move Joe Cordina vs. Mauricio Lara to Main Card
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is campaigning hard to move Joe Cordina vs. Mauricio Lara onto the Netflix main card for Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua on December 11 in Cardiff, upset and confused about why organizers left what he considers a major fight off the broadcast. In reality, a ten-round non-title lightweight bout between two rebuilding fighters belongs right where it’s currently placed on the prelim portion of the card.

On Friday, Hearn told Matchroom Boxing that he was “completely baffled” to see Cordina (19-1, 9 KOs) and Lara (31-3-2, 24 KOs) placed on the YouTube and TikTok prelims before the four-fight heavyweight main broadcast at Principality Stadium. Hearn even congratulated himself for pressuring Sela and Turki Alalshikh to add the bout, predicting “Netflix will have no choice but to elevate Joe Cordina to the main card.”

When looking at the less than stellar opposition Cordina and Lara have been fighting since they were beaten, you can give the organizers of the event credit for getting the placement right. Their fight isn’t big enough to be a value add to what is already a weak main card.

Two Rebuilding Fighters With Nothing on the Line

From a quality standpoint, Hearn should be grateful Cordina made the show at all rather than demanding he be placed on the main card. The 34-year-old Welshman lost his IBF 130-pound belt in May 2024 when Anthony Cacace stopped him in eight rounds in Riyadh, and his two wins since moving up to lightweight came against Jaret Gonzalez Quiroz and Gabriel Flores Jr. We’re not talking about murderers’ row type fighters. Based on those two wins over lower-level opposition, this feels like Cordina is placed right where he belongs.

Netflix Wants Heavyweights for American Viewers

Hearn criticized Sela advisors Dana White and Nick Khan for not being in tune with British boxing, saying fans in Wales will go mad for Cordina over main-card heavyweights like Da’Mazion Vanhouter against Michael Essomba and Moses Jolly against Igor Adiel Macedo.

The Netflix card is built for an American audience tuning in at 8 p.m. ET. With the way the main card has been put together, the organizers are betting that four heavyweight fights will draw more interest than Cordina and Lara trying to rebuild their careers.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Stalling Ben Whittaker Mandatory Shot Against Dmitry Bivol
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is dressing up another protective detour as major news, claiming a “big domestic fight” for Ben Whittaker is “pretty much signed” for early 2027. Hearn didn’t name the opponent, though it is safe to say it won’t be a rematch with Conor Wallace after Whittaker (13-0-1, 9 KOs) barely survived him in their IBF final eliminator last October in Birmingham.

Whittaker already holds the mandatory spot for the Dmitry Bivol vs. Callum Smith winner. Hearn admitted in a Matchroom interview that “coming off the back of the last fight, I think he needs one more fight.” That tells you Whittaker had major problems against Wallace, came close to losing, and Matchroom knows he would get battered by Bivol or Smith.

Matchroom Branding Over Real Contenders

A genuine domestic test would mean matching the 29-year-old Whittaker against Joshua Buatsi or Willy Hutchinson. Instead, Matchroom is protecting him like a young prospect by looking toward worn-out UK names like Craig Richards, Dan Azeez, or Lyndon Arthur, guys who sell tickets without risking Whittaker’s payday against Bivol.

If Hearn believes one soft outing prepares Whittaker for Bivol, he is kidding himself. Facing a non-pressing domestic opponent actually hurts Whittaker by letting him get away with showboating and lazy movement, building bad habits that Bivol will punish.

The Canelo Waiting Game on Bivol

What we are likely seeing is a stalling strategy to age out the 35-year-old Bivol, who is already dealing with injuries from a long career. After Whittaker wins this domestic bout, Hearn can easily claim he needs another tune-up, stringing things out the same way Canelo Alvarez waited until Gennady Golovkin turned 35 and lost a step.

Putting Whittaker in with Bivol in 2027 would ruin years of careful building. Judging by how Whittaker looked against Wallace, he is not cut out for the top of the 175-pound division, and turning him into a protected ticket-seller like Conor Benn is a bad look for the sport.

Sports.title: Andy Cruz Wins IBF Title as One Judge Backs Artur Subkhankulov
Sports.content:
Andy Cruz beat Artur Subkhankulov by a competitive 12 round split decision to win the vacant IBF lightweight title Friday in Ufa, Russia. The split was difficult to explain. Subkhankulov had one round at best, even with a knockdown in the eighth, and somehow convinced a judge that he’d done enough to win the fight.

What was strange was how often Subkhankulov threw rabbit punches and got away with it without being penalized until late in the fight. It was like clockwork: he hit Cruz in the back of the head whenever they clinched, and there were a lot of those. The clinching was mostly initiated by Cruz, who had no real inside game to speak of. Still, the referee should have taken points off Subkhankulov much earlier for the fouling.

Two judges scored it 116-110 for Cruz, while the third had it 114-112 for Subkhankulov. Even the two cards for Cruz made the fight look closer than it was. The 2020 Olympic gold medalist scored knockdowns in rounds two and eight and spent most of the 12 rounds catching the hometown fighter with jabs and straight right hands as he came forward.

Cruz turned what could have been an easy fight for him into a difficult one by failing to let his hands go consistently against the weaker-punching Subkhankulov. It was as if Cruz lacked an overdrive gear to press with nonstop punches. He’d shown repeatedly that the Russian fighter was vulnerable to his right hand, yet he was selective in throwing it for some reason.

Both Fighters Go Down in the Eighth

Cruz had the better of the fight at a distance from early on, dropping Subkhankulov in the second round. His jab kept the southpaw from getting set, and when Subkhankulov tried to close the distance, Cruz had the timing to catch him with the right hand. Subkhankulov kept pressing with swelling around an eye, but he was taking the cleaner punches on the way in and rarely did enough once he got there.

The eighth was the one round in which Subkhankulov gave Cruz real trouble. Cruz hurt him with a right hand and put him down early in the round. Subkhankulov got up and dropped Cruz late in the same round, forcing him to take a count for the first time as a professional. Subkhankulov also had a point deducted during the fight for repeated punches behind the head.

The knockdown gave Subkhankulov his best opening of the night, but he couldn’t build on it. Cruz recovered and went back to landing straight rights, and Subkhankulov’s pressure lost some of its bite in the closing rounds. With two knockdowns banked and the cleaner work on either side of the eighth, Cruz was clearly in command down the stretch. The 114-112 card for Subkhankulov was completely baffling because he didn’t win the fight based on the action. Even in a couple of rounds, he appeared to win late in the fight, eating jabs and hard right hands.

Cruz Takes the Belt on His Second Try

Cruz (8-1, 4 KOs) had wanted a stoppage after losing a close majority decision to Raymond Muratalla in his first title attempt in January. Muratalla subsequently moved up and vacated the IBF belt, giving Cruz another shot at it against Subkhankulov (12-1, 6 KOs) in the IBA Pro 22 main event at the Wrestling Palace.

The two had met as amateurs in 2019, when Cruz also won a split decision. Seven years later, Subkhankulov gave him a scare in front of his home crowd, then spent the closing rounds trying to get past the same jab and right hand that had troubled him all night. Cruz left Ufa with his first professional world title. The eighth showed what Subkhankulov could do when he got close enough to land, but the rest of the fight showed how rarely Cruz let him do it.

All in all, it was not an impressive performance by Cruz, given how tentative he was against a fighter that wasn’t a devastating puncher. Cruz showed the same flaws in this fight that led to his loss to Raymond Muratalla: he didn’t attack aggressively and focused too much on single right hands. He spent too much time on his defense, and not enough on attacking Subkhankulov.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Medical Clearance Keeps $100M Anthony Joshua Cash Out on Track
Sports.content:
It’s interesting how quickly Tyson Fury’s medical diagnosis changes when huge cash is involved in a fight. Fury (36-2-1, 25 KOs) has been cleared by the British Boxing Board of Control to face Anthony Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) on December 11.

All it took for the British Boxing Board of Control was three sentences from board secretary Robert Smith and Fury’s wife, Paris Fury, retracting her comments about Tyson Fury being diagnosed with schizophrenia.

“Fury cleared last night. All up to date medicals cleared. Promoter told this morning,” Smith said to Sky Sports.

Earlier in the week, video on Netflix showed Paris saying that Fury had been told by doctors that he had mild schizophrenia after his victory over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015. Fury even said to the Guardian a week ago that he “went to a leading specialist and was diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar.”

Things changed quickly after BBBofC General Secretary Robert Smith revealed that the board was looking into the comments. On Thursday, Paris said that Fury had never been diagnosed with schizophrenia. Netflix edited footage of the earlier comments from Paris before Friday’s release, and now Robert Smith has confirmed that Fury has passed his pre-fight medicals and is clear to face Joshua on December 11.

Nobody should be surprised that this got ironed out overnight without the fight being canceled after Paris’s revelation about Fury. Losing this fight would have likely led to a stampede of fans wanting their money back from ticket sales.

If the BBBofC pulled Fury’s license, the entire December 11 card would have fallen apart, wiping out the huge rumored $100 million paydays that 38-year-old Fury and 37-year-old Joshua are getting for this.

The undercard lacks any marquee-level fights that could be moved into the main event to save the ticket sales. And there’s zero chance fans would subscribe in large numbers to watch the event without Fury facing Joshua in the main event. The co-feature bout is Deontay Wilder vs. Martin Bakole, a fight widely criticized as lackluster.

Even if Joshua had stayed on the card, it would be impossible to find a big enough name to create interest without someone like Moses Itauma or Daniel Dubois stepping in at the last minute. That would be highly unlikely.

Fury and Joshua are both at a career stage where they’re fighting on fumes with little left of the talent they once had. Neither of them can be thrown into the general population with the younger top heavyweights without being plundered and left in pieces.

They’ve both been in protective situations lately, matched against the weakest possible opponents to ensure they don’t get beaten again before they meet for their cash-out fight. It’s kind of pathetic, but this is what it’s come to for these two aging fighters in their retirement run. Get the money on their way out of the sport.

The board cleared the paperwork, Netflix edited their video, and the gravy train stays on the tracks for December 11.

Sports.title: UK Boxing Pundits Worry Saudi Gravy Train Is Stopping
Sports.content:
All-expenses-paid trips to Riyadh are becoming scarce, and some in the British boxing media worry the Saudi gold rush is running dry.

Ade Oladipo and Gareth A. Davies are remembering when they had it good during the brief two-year span from 2023 to 2025, when UK commentators got used to the red-carpet treatment of traveling to Saudi Arabia for big events.

“It felt like we were out there every week. Like we were in the sky on the way to Riyadh every single week for these big cards that you never thought were going to stop,” Oladipo said on talkSPORT Boxing.

Those big events have largely disappeared, leaving Ade and Gareth wondering if Turki Alalshikh will close up shop for UK fighters after Tyson Fury (36-2-1, 25 KOs) fights Anthony Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) on December 11. You kind of knew it would end sooner or later, with wealthy, underperforming fighters doing the minimum to win and events that failed to attract PPV buys.

Oladipo harped about it being six or seven months since he was flown out to Riyadh, saying he was not even sent over for Canelo Alvarez’s fight against Christian Mbilli on October 31. That was an expensive event for fans, who had to pay $79.99 in the U.S. and £24.99 in the UK.

Not Built for U.S. Fans

Gareth questioned whether the British media are now “at the close of a particular era” when the Fury vs. Joshua event concludes in Cardiff. For Riyadh Season, that would be them finishing with a bang, but only because they are giving UK fans the fight they wanted, not because it is a matchup that non-Brits want to see.

If this is it for Turki and Riyadh Season, it is not a great deal for Americans, watching two heavyweights 10 years past their prime fight it out for the vacant WBA Super belt.

Riyadh Season Did Not Leave Boxing

Turki has not stopped spending money on the sport entirely. Instead, he is putting money into Zuffa events, which are less costly than massive cards like Canelo Alvarez vs. Terence Crawford and Fury vs. Joshua.

The difference is that Zuffa cards involve less well-known fighters who put on surprisingly more entertaining fights than the well-paid superstars. What those fights have shown is that Zuffa does not have to pay huge money to get good action.

For the last three years, British promoters leaned on Saudi budgets to bail out domestic matchups that could not sell on UK pay-per-view alone. If Saudi money disappears for average British cards in 2027, UK promoters will have to pay fighters based on what they actually bring in for ticket and PPV sales. It is going to be a shock for British promoters to go back to the old ways of putting events together.

Ghana News.title: Unposted medical officers haven’t declined postings — AUMO challenges Health Minister over figures
Ghana News.content:
The Association of Unposted Medical Officers (AUMO) has dismissed claims that doctors awaiting employment have declined postings from the Ministry of Health, insisting that none of its affected members has received an official posting letter.

The association has consequently challenged Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh to publish the number of medical officers who have been posted and those still awaiting deployment, as well as those who have declined appointments.

In a statement released on November 28, AUMO said more than 500 of its members remained without postings despite completing their housemanship, with some having waited for up to 12 months.

"It has been suggested that doctors at home declined postings. We state categorically that AUMO's members have received no posting letter and have declined same," the association stated.

It further challenged the Minister to make the relevant figures public, saying: "We therefore dare the Minister to release data on the number of medical officers waiting postings and those that he has already posted."

The association's response follows the Minister's assertion during the 2027 Budget debate in Parliament that every medical officer had been posted and none remained at home awaiting employment.

AUMO rejected the claim as "totally false", maintaining that its members, who completed housemanship from December 2025, were still waiting for permanent appointments.

It said the affected doctors could be verified individually through their names, Medical and Dental Council (MDC) registration numbers and housemanship completion dates.

AUMO questions Ministry's recruitment figures

To challenge the Minister's position, the association cited a November 2026 statement by the Ministry of Health indicating that the 36th batch of medical officers was receiving permanent employment ahead of the 37th batch.

According to AUMO, the announcement points to a batch-by-batch placement process rather than evidence that all medical officers have been employed.

"The Ministry's own November 2026 statement said the 36th batch was receiving permanent jobs ahead of the 37th. That shows batch-by-batch placement, not that no one is waiting," it said.

The association also addressed the Health Minister's reference to an arrangement between the Ministries of Health and Finance intended to prevent doctors from remaining at home after completing housemanship.

It argued that the arrangement does not resolve the situation of those who have already completed their training but are still awaiting postings.

"An arrangement that spares future graduates the wait does not post those already waiting," AUMO stated.

It also recalled comments made by the Minister in February 2026, when he reportedly indicated that vacancies would be used to employ medical officers who had completed housemanship but remained at home.

The association questioned why the Minister would previously acknowledge the existence of unposted doctors but subsequently tell Parliament that none remained at home.

Questions over doctor shortages

The association also questioned the apparent contradiction between the Minister's acknowledgement that some districts have no medical doctors and the presence of qualified medical officers awaiting employment.

"The Minister has said there are districts without a single medical doctor. Trained doctors are at home. These two facts cannot both be left standing," AUMO stated.

It argued that deploying the affected medical officers could help address staffing shortages in underserved districts while providing employment for doctors who have completed their training.

The association has expressed its readiness to engage the Ministry and accept postings to any part of the country.

Ghana News.title: Ghanaian farming households face higher risk of food insecurity – Ghana Statistical Service
Ghana News.content:
Households engaged in agriculture are more than twice as likely to experience vulnerable food consumption as the national average. This alarming statistic exposes a troubling contradiction in Ghana's efforts to achieve food security: those who are responsible for producing the country's food are often the ones who struggle the most to feed their families. This situation raises important questions about the broader implications for social equity and economic stability within the agricultural sector.

The Ghana Statistical Service's (GSS) Third Quarter 2026 Mobile Vulnerability Analysis and Mapping (mVAM) report highlights that 15.9% of agriculture-dependent households experienced vulnerable food consumption between July and September 2026. This statistic starkly contrasts with the national average of 6.6%, suggesting a critical need for targeted interventions that support vulnerable farmers and their families.

This finding raises fundamental questions about whether increased agricultural production is directly translating into improved livelihoods and food security for the farmers at the center of Ghana's agricultural economy. The disconnect between food production and food security highlights an urgent need for policy reforms that address the root causes of food insecurity among farming households.

Additionally, it challenges the assumption that households engaged in food production necessarily enjoy better access to adequate food. The reality is often more complex, and many farmers find themselves trapped in a cycle of poverty that undermines their ability to provide for their families, despite their role in the food supply chain.

For many smallholder farmers, producing food does not automatically guarantee sufficient household food consumption. Factors such as seasonal harvests, fluctuating farmgate prices, high production costs, post-harvest losses, and limited access to profitable markets can significantly undermine the financial returns from farming. It's essential to shed light on these challenges and explore solutions that can support farmers in achieving better financial stability and food security.

Farmers who depend on seasonal incomes may also struggle to meet household food needs during periods between harvests, when food stocks are depleted and purchasing food from the market becomes necessary. The financial strain during these lean seasons can lead to difficult choices, where families may have to sacrifice nutritional quality for quantity, resulting in a detrimental impact on health and well-being.

This contradiction is particularly significant at a time when Ghana is pursuing agricultural transformation through interventions aimed at increasing domestic food production, strengthening value chains, and reducing dependence on imported food. The effectiveness of these interventions should be evaluated not only on food production metrics but also on their capacity to enhance the livelihoods of agricultural workers.

The GSS findings suggest that agricultural success must be measured not only by how much food the country produces but also by whether farmers earn enough from their activities to feed their families adequately. This dual focus on production and farmer income is crucial for ensuring sustainable food systems that support both economic and social goals.

Market access is another important dimension of the problem. The report found that 22.6% of households, representing approximately 2.1 million homes, experienced difficulties accessing markets during the month preceding the survey. This lack of access not only affects farmers' ability to sell their produce but also limits their purchasing power, exacerbating food insecurity.

Households without full market access recorded vulnerable food consumption of 13.5%, compared with 4.4% among those with uninterrupted access. The stark difference indicates that improving market infrastructure and access for smallholder farmers could be a pivotal factor in reducing food insecurity and enhancing livelihoods.

For agricultural households, inadequate market infrastructure can create a double burden: difficulty selling their produce at competitive prices and difficulty accessing food and other essential commodities. This situation highlights the need for comprehensive policies aimed at strengthening market systems and ensuring that farmers can compete effectively while accessing the necessary resources for their families.

Regional disparities further highlight the challenge. The North East Region recorded the highest proportion of households experiencing vulnerable food consumption at 42.2%, followed by Upper East at 30.1% and Upper West at 29.5%. These variations underscore the importance of tailored interventions that account for the unique challenges faced by different regions in Ghana.

The GSS findings reinforce the need to move beyond production-focused agricultural interventions towards policies that improve farmer incomes, market access, storage, processing, and resilience. By addressing these interconnected issues, Ghana can create a more sustainable agricultural landscape that supports the well-being of all its citizens.

Ultimately, Ghana's food security ambitions will remain incomplete if the households producing the country's food cannot afford to maintain adequate food consumption themselves. A holistic approach that prioritizes the welfare of farmers and their families will be essential to achieving lasting food security and economic stability in the country.

In conclusion, addressing the issue of food insecurity among farming households in Ghana is not only a matter of social justice but also a crucial element in ensuring the nation's agricultural sustainability. Policymakers must prioritize initiatives that empower farmers through access to resources, education, and fair market opportunities. By fostering an environment where farmers can thrive, Ghana can build a resilient food system that benefits all and moves towards a future of food security.

Ghana News.title: Labour Ministry urges stronger reporting to tackle child labour
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Labour, Jobs and Employment has urged institutions and development partners involved in the fight against child labour to strengthen reporting and data-sharing to improve national coordination, policy formulation and accountability.

It said accurate and timely reporting was essential to identifying vulnerable communities, directing resources and assessing the effectiveness of interventions to eliminate child labour.

The Director of the Child Labour Unit (CLU) of the Ministry, Esther Ofori Agyemang, made the call at a stakeholders’ forum in Accra last Wednesday to discuss the 2024 Child Labour Report and examine its findings and recommendations.

She said reports submitted by implementing partners provided important information for government and international institutions assessing the country’s progress in addressing child labour and human trafficking.

Mrs Agyemang said the Gender Ministry intended to make the annual review of child labour reports a regular exercise to enable stakeholders to assess progress, identify gaps and determine necessary interventions.

Although the seminar focused on the 2024 report, the Director said data collection and analysis for the 2025 report had been completed, with the final document expected to be shared with stakeholders.

She, however, called for a more comprehensive national approach to tackling child labour and warned that the concentration of interventions and reporting in the cocoa sector could obscure the extent of the problem in other sectors.

Mrs Agyemang said greater attention must be given to other sectors, particularly illegal small-scale mining, domestic work and commercial sexual exploitation, where children were also vulnerable to exploitation.

The Director of the Child Labour Unit said addressing child labour in only one sector could, therefore, undermine national efforts to eliminate the practice, stressing the need for coordinated interventions across all sectors.

Mrs Agyemang urged implementing agencies under the National Plan of Action to integrate child labour interventions into their institutional budgets and activities.

She said inadequate resources, limited understanding of institutional responsibilities and poor reporting remained major implementation challenges.

“This report is critical in helping us identify regions where children are at risk and where partners should direct their attention and resources.” she said.

Presenting the report, a consultant, Emmanuel Antwi Boasiako, said the number of children identified engaging in child labour declined from more than 27,000 in 2023 to about 14,000 in 2024, representing a reduction of approximately 49 per cent.

The proportion of children identified in the worst forms of child labour also fell from 16.7 per cent to 11 per cent.

However, Mr Boasiako said, only 40 per cent of male children and 35 per cent of female children identified as being in or at risk of child labour received the necessary support.

He expressed concern about declining economic assistance to vulnerable households, saying support for income-generating activities fell from about 3,700 beneficiaries in 2023 to 1,001 in 2024, while cash transfer support dropped from 1,320 beneficiaries to zero.

Mr Boasiako said only three of the 54 activities scheduled under the country's five-year strategic plan for 2024 were fully completed, while 63 per cent were ongoing and 31 per cent had not been implemented.

He recommended increased funding, stronger community child protection structures, improved coordination and vocational training for children aged 15 to 17.

“We need to move beyond awareness creation and provide robust solutions to address the poverty and economic challenges that drive child labour.” he said

The Director of Justice Projects, International Justice Mission Ghana (IJM), Anita Budu, called for stronger support for state institutions, including the Department of Social Welfare, the Ghana Police Service and the Judiciary, to address child exploitation.

Citing Section 87 of the Children's Act, 1998 (Act 560), she said efforts must address all forms of exploitative work that threatened children's health, education and development.

Ms Budu cautioned against establishing parallel structures and urged stakeholders to strengthen existing child protection institutions.

She also called for the report to be produced annually and its findings widely disseminated to ensure that the information translated into practical action to protect children.

IJM Ghana’s Director of Justice Projects said although progress had been made in capacity building and awareness creation, significant gaps remained in the identification and remediation of children engaged in the worst forms of child labour.

Ms Budu said the support must address the children’s overall well-being and welfare, rather than focusing solely on removing them from exploitative situations.

Ghana News.title: Kwasi Twum, six others honoured at UPSA Eminent Achievement Award
Ghana News.content:
The University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA), has honoured seven distinguished personalities from the banking, media, finance, pharmaceutical and entrepreneurial sectors for their contributions to industry, institution-building and national development.

The personalities were recognised at the second edition of the Faculty of Accounting and Finance (FAF) Eminent Achievement Awards held on Friday, November 27, 2026, at the Kofi Ohene-Konadu Auditorium.

The ceremony was held under the theme, “Celebrating Excellence. Honouring Legacies. Inspiring National Transformation.” and brought together personalities from academia, business and industry to celebrate professional accomplishments and encourage the next generation of leaders.

The awards were instituted by the Faculty of Accounting and Finance to recognise individuals whose careers have contributed to excellence, innovation and transformation across accounting, finance, banking, economics and related sectors.

The seven awardees were Dr Philip Oti-Mensah, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Universal Merchant Bank; Kwasi Twum, Founder of the Multimedia Group; Joe Jackson, Chief Executive Officer of Dalex Finance and Leasing Company Limited; and Chief Dr Doli-Wura Awushi Abdul-Malik Seidu Zakaria, Managing Director of National Investment Bank.

The others were Ernest De-Graft Egyir, Founder of Ghana CEO Summit and Chief Executives Network Ghana; Dhananjay Tripathi, Founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Pharmanova Group and Atlantic Lifesciences Limited; and Dr Samuel Amo Tobbin, Founder and Executive Chairman of Tobinco Group of Companies.

The Chairman of the occasion, Nana Appiah Dankawoso II, urged young people to prioritise learning, hard work and integrity over the pursuit of titles and wealth.

He said the seven awardees had built successful businesses across various sectors, with their contributions reflected in jobs created, families supported and confidence in Ghanaian businesses strengthened.

“But every great tree started as a seed, and every awardee here once sat where our students sit today. To the young people in this hall, I say, do not be in a hurry for titles. Be in a hurry to learn, to work earnestly, and to keep your name clean,” he said. MyJoyOnline

Nana Appiah Dankawoso II cautioned that while wealth could be rebuilt, a damaged reputation was much harder to restore, drawing on Proverbs 22, which emphasises the value of a good name.

Meanwhile, the Member of Parliament for Madina, Francis-Xavier Sosu, commended private sector businesses for their contributions to national development but urged them to expand their operations to create more employment opportunities for Ghanaians.

Speaking at the ceremony, he said recognition of business leaders should also focus on how their achievements translate into opportunities for the wider population, particularly amid concerns over unemployment.

He appealed to the awardees and other business leaders to support UPSA and its students through internship opportunities, improved learning facilities and other forms of collaboration to prepare young people for the world of work. MyJoyOnline

Among the awardees, Mr Kwasi Twum was recognised in the Media Enterprise, Corporate Governance and Economic Discourse category for his contribution to Ghana’s media industry.

The recognition highlighted his role in establishing Joy FM in 1995 and building the Multimedia Group into a major player in broadcasting and digital media, with its platforms contributing to national discourse, public accountability and democratic participation. MyJoyOnline

The second edition of the awards builds on the inaugural ceremony held in November 2025, which recognised four industry leaders and two institutions for their contributions to accounting, finance and economics.

The initiative forms part of the Faculty’s broader commitment to promoting professional excellence, strengthening academia-industry partnerships and creating platforms for knowledge-sharing, mentorship and collaboration between experienced industry practitioners and students.

The ceremony is expected to reinforce the university’s role in bridging the gap between academic training and industry practice while celebrating individuals whose professional journeys continue to inspire future generations.

Ghana News.title: MTTD mounts speed cameras on accident-prone roads in Ashanti Region
Ghana News.content:
The Motor Traffic and Transport Directorate (MTTD) has revealed areas in the Ashanti Region where speed cameras have been mounted as part of the new automated traffic enforcement system, TraffiTech-GH.

The MTTD showed that currently the cameras have been mounted only on the Kentinkrono-Accra Road, Tanoso-Sunyani Road, and Santasi-Obuasi Road, where the speed limit is 50 kilometres per hour.

Regional MTTD Commander, Superintendent Emmanuel Kwame Boadi, says these areas were targeted after recording of a trend of fatal accidents on those stretches despite the conspicuous speed limit signage.

"At the moment, we have been directed to mount cameras at locations where road signs indicate the speed limits. And therefore we have been mounting our cameras on the Kentinkrono-Accra road, Tanoso-Sunyani road, and Santasi-Obuasi road. These areas are supposed to be 50 kilometres per hour, but we have been recording serious accidents there, and that is why we have been advised to mount our cameras at those locations," he said.

In line with TrafficTech rules, Commander Boadi added that educational road signs have also been mounted at the locations with the installed cameras to inform drivers of the speed limits.

He further explained that apart from the fixed cameras, the MTTD also deploys mobile vehicle cameras across the city and to the outskirts of town to monitor speeding of vehicles.

"For now, these are the only locations where we mount the cameras. However, we also have vehicle cameras that move anywhere within the city, and sometimes to the outskirts of town, especially on the Mankranso-Tepa road where there is a need to control speeding," Supt. Boadi added.

He urged motorists plying those roads to observe the 50-kilometre-per-hour speed limit and comply with the TrafficTech enforcement measures to avoid violations.

The intensified enforcement forms part of the MTTD's road safety operations ahead of Christmas, being undertaken in partnership with Street Sense Organisation.

The organisation has presented 200 reflective vests to the Ashanti Regional MTTD office to support officers particularly during night operations and road safety activities.

The Ashanti Regional Commander of the MTTD said the new reflective vests will facilitate easy identification of MTTD officers during operations on major roads.

He commended the safety advocacy initiative and called for more collaborations between the police and stakeholders to improve road safety in the region.

"We have about 500 MTTD officers in the region, and we have so far received a donation of 200 reflective vests. We still need 300 more, so we are appealing to other corporate bodies, NGOs, and stakeholders to follow the good example of the Street Sense Organisation and support us with the remaining vests," he stated.

Public Relations Officer (PRO) of the Street Sense Organisation, Prince Odame Amoako, said the partnership is aimed at strengthening public education and supporting the police in their efforts to reduce road crashes.

He urged drivers to cooperate with officers and comply with the new TrafficTech enforcement measures to avoid road traffic violations.

Mr Odame also called on the authorities of TrafficTech to intensify public education and ensure that wherever speed limit cameras are mounted, there are clear warning signals to alert motorists.

Ghana News.title: Accelerated grade placement, Category A SHS placement driving early BECE registrations – Africa Education Watch
Ghana News.content:
The Executive Director of Africa Education Watch, Kofi Asare, has attributed the growing practice of students sitting the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) earlier than scheduled to accelerated grade placement and the desire to secure admission to Category A senior high schools.

According to him, the increasing movement of pupils from private to public basic schools is largely driven by parents seeking to take advantage of opportunities within Ghana’s public education system, particularly the benefits associated with the placement of public Junior High School (JHS) candidates.

Mr Asare made these remarks on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, November 28, amid discussions surrounding the directive to prevent JHS 1 and JHS 2 students from registering for the BECE before completing the required level of basic education.

He explained that Ghana’s education system had experienced changing patterns of movement between public and private schools over the past decade, with a notable shift from private to public institutions since 2021.

Mr Asare explained that the earlier movement from public to private schools was largely motivated by parents who wanted their children to complete basic education and progress to tertiary institutions at a relatively younger age.

However, he said the recent movement from private to public basic schools was being driven by two major considerations: the desire to accelerate children's progression to tertiary education and the opportunity to benefit from the placement arrangements for Category A senior high schools.

He identified the 30 per cent allocation protocol for candidates from public JHSs as a particularly significant incentive influencing parents' decisions.

According to him, parents increasingly transfer their children from private to public basic schools to benefit from both accelerated grade placement and improved opportunities for admission to Category A senior high schools.

“So they cross to the public schools and benefit from two things: accelerated grade placement and enhanced opportunity for Category A placement,” he explained.

He suggested that the combination of these incentives had created considerable demand for the irregular practice of moving pupils into higher classes ahead of schedule, allowing them to sit the BECE earlier than they ordinarily should.

The Africa Education Watch Executive Director further raised concerns about the financial implications of the practice, alleging that some school authorities were demanding money to facilitate irregular admissions and accelerated grade placement.

Recounting findings from research conducted around the Osino area in 2023, Mr Asare disclosed that some schools were reportedly charging parents as much as GH¢10,000 to facilitate the process.

He warned that the amount involved had since increased, partly because of changes in the administrative procedures governing admissions into higher classes.

“So because there are two fuels or two motivations, in our case, you see that the demand for the illegality is so high that the last time we did some research around the Osino area, we realised that schools were taking about GH¢10,000. That was in 2023,” he said.

He added that feedback received from monitoring officers suggested that the financial demands had increased following the introduction of a directive requiring district directorates of the Ghana Education Service (GES) to approve admissions into Form Two and Form Three.

Mr Asare acknowledged that the directive was introduced to strengthen administrative oversight and curb corruption in the admission process.

However, he argued that the measure had produced unintended consequences by expanding the number of officials involved in the approval process.

According to him, the additional administrative layers had not necessarily eliminated irregularities but had instead created a wider chain through which corrupt activities could take place, increasing the cost of facilitating such admissions.

The situation also highlights the need for the Ghana Education Service to examine how its admission approval procedures are implemented at the district and school levels.

Strengthening transparency, improving monitoring and ensuring accountability he said, among school authorities and education officials could help address some of the concerns.

Ghana News.title: 1 in 2 households spend over 75% of their budget on food – Ghana Statistical Service
Ghana News.content:
More than half of Ghanaian households spend over three-quarters of their total expenditure on food, leaving limited financial resources for other essential needs, the Ghana Statistical Service (GSS) has revealed. This significant trend emphasizes the importance of understanding the food budget Ghana.

According to the Statistical Service’s Third Quarter 2026 Mobile Vulnerability Analysis and Mapping report, 50.5% of households, representing approximately 4.69 million homes, spent more than 75% of their total expenditure on food between July and September 2026. This data underscores the critical situation regarding the food budget Ghana.

The findings highlight the pressure food costs place on household finances, with potential implications for spending on healthcare, education, housing and other basic necessities, further illustrating the challenges of managing a food budget Ghana.

Only 8% of households spent less than half of their total expenditure on food, underscoring the extent to which food dominates household spending across the country.

The report, based on interviews with 7,752 households across all 16 regions, also identifies challenges with market access, livelihoods and the ability of families to maintain adequate food consumption.

Food consumption and household vulnerability

Understanding the Food Budget Ghana

Although 93.5% of households recorded acceptable food consumption during the period, the GSS says this does not necessarily mean families are financially secure or free from food-related pressures.

About 6.6% of households, representing approximately 606,000 homes, recorded poor or borderline food consumption. At the population level, an estimated 2.69 million Ghanaians lived in households experiencing vulnerable food consumption.

The report further found that 30.1% of households, equivalent to approximately 2.79 million homes, relied on medium or high food-related coping strategies. These included relying on cheaper or less preferred food, reducing meal portions and eating fewer meals during the day.

More concerning is the finding that 11.3% of households resorted to crisis or emergency coping strategies, including selling productive assets, reducing healthcare expenditure and withdrawing children from school to meet immediate needs.

Market access compounds food affordability challenges

Beyond household spending, the report identifies access to food markets as another important factor influencing food security.

Approximately 22.6% of households, representing 2.1 million homes, reported experiencing difficulties accessing a market during the month preceding the survey.

The consequences were reflected in food consumption patterns. Households without full market access recorded vulnerable food consumption of 13.5%, compared with 4.4% among those with uninterrupted access.

The findings raise questions about the role of transportation infrastructure, distribution networks and market availability in determining whether households can consistently access food.

Northern Ghana records highest food vulnerability

The national figures also conceal significant regional disparities. The North East Region recorded the highest proportion of households experiencing vulnerable food consumption at 42.2%.

This was followed by Upper East at 30.1%, Upper West at 29.5% and Northern Region at 27.1%.

The urban-rural divide was equally significant, with rural households nearly three times as likely to experience vulnerable food consumption as their urban counterparts. The proportion stood at 10.7% among rural households, compared with 3.8% in urban communities.

Agricultural households also face food vulnerability

Despite their involvement in food production, agriculture-dependent households recorded a vulnerable food consumption rate of 15.9%, more than twice the national average of 6.6%.

The finding raises questions about the relationship between agricultural production, household income and food security, particularly for smallholder farmers whose livelihoods depend on seasonal production and fluctuating market conditions.

It also highlights the importance of addressing storage, financing, market access and post-harvest losses alongside efforts to increase agricultural production.

Limited assistance reaches vulnerable households

The report further raises concerns about social protection coverage, with only 0.9% of households, representing approximately 83,000 homes, reporting receipt of food, cash or other assistance in the month preceding the survey.

Meanwhile, 11.3% of households had resorted to crisis or emergency livelihood coping strategies.

The GSS recommends strengthening early-warning systems to identify vulnerable households, improving the targeting of social protection programmes and investing in resilient agriculture, food storage, transportation and value chains.

The findings underscore the need to address not only the availability of food but also the financial capacity of households to afford it and the systems required to ensure that food reaches consumers.
