The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (Rtd.), has called for the immediate and strategic integration of Nigerian universities into the nation’s security architecture, declaring that safeguarding Nigeria’s sovereignty and future requires an all-of-nation alliance driven by indigenous intellect, innovation and patriotic resolve.

The Minister also outlined six critical areas in which Nigerian universities must take the lead in defending and advancing the Nigerian project: Strategic Research and Policy Intelligence, Indigenous Technological Sovereignty, Capital and Executive Capacity, Peacebuilding and National Cohesion, Economic and Human Security, and Strategic Foresight.

General Musa made this call while delivering a convocation lecture titled, “The Strategic Role of Universities in Nigeria’s National Security Architecture: Challenges, Opportunities and Policy Imperatives”, at Admiralty University of Nigeria (ADUN), Ibusa, Delta State.

The Minister emphasised that contemporary national security extends far beyond conventional military operations.

Addressing the academic audience, the Minister noted that Nigeria is confronting complex and hybrid threats rooted in socioeconomic vulnerabilities and technological gaps. He added that winning the peace and securing the homeland demand the full mobilisation of the nation’s citadels of learning.

“Security is not the responsibility of the Armed Forces and other security agencies alone; it is a sacred national undertaking that requires the collective strength of government, institutions, communities and citizens. A nation may possess formidable military capabilities, yet remain vulnerable if its economy is weak, its technology is externally dependent and its intellectual capital is underutilised. Our universities must stand as pillars of strategic intelligence, technological sovereignty and national resilience,” General Musa stated.

While acknowledging systemic challenges such as inadequate research infrastructure, brain drain, weak synergy between academia and security agencies, and limited commercialisation of research, the Minister highlighted the Federal Government’s decisive investments to reverse these trends.

He cited Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) approvals of ₦4.25 billion for 158 research projects in August 2025 and an additional ₦7.5 billion for 174 research teams in June 2026 as evidence of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu administration’s commitment to funding home-grown solutions.

According to a statement by the Special Assistant on Media to the Minister of Defence, Leah Katung-Babatunde, the Minister outlined clear policy imperatives requiring Federal and State Governments to institutionalise university-security frameworks, university managements to prioritise impact-driven research and campus safety, and security institutions to commission independent academic studies while respecting academic freedom.

Turning to the graduating class, the Defence Minister urged the graduates to reject any sense of entitlement and embrace their degrees as instruments of national service.

“Nigeria is not merely waiting for you to occupy offices; your fatherland is waiting for you to solve problems,” the Minister charged. “Whether you studied computer science, agriculture, engineering, law, education or political science, your knowledge must defend our digital borders, feed our citizens, strengthen our infrastructure and uphold the rule of law. Let your competence strengthen society, let your integrity inspire confidence, and let your patriotism be demonstrated through courageous and responsible action.”

World.title: INEC Reaffirms Readiness for 2027 Polls, Successfully Conducts Mock Poll in Plateau
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Yemi Kosoko in Jos

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has reiterated its commitment to conducting free, credible, inclusive and transparent elections in 2027, following the successful conduct of a mock election in Plateau State on Saturday.

Chairman of the commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan, who monitored the exercise, said the mock poll was designed to assess the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), as well as evaluate the efficiency of the voter accreditation process ahead of the general election.

He expressed satisfaction with the conduct of the exercise and the turnout of voters, noting that the accreditation process proceeded smoothly and in an orderly manner.

Amupitan assured Nigerians that INEC was making adequate preparations to deliver a credible electoral process in 2027, stressing the commission’s determination to uphold the principles of transparency, inclusiveness and integrity.

The INEC chairman also disclosed that the commission was working closely with security agencies to ensure the safety of voters, electoral personnel and election materials during the polls.

According to him, INEC has conducted a nationwide risk assessment of polling units and shared its findings with relevant law enforcement agencies.

“We have done what we call a risk assessment of all the polling units in Nigeria, and we have identified all the polling units and shared them with the law enforcement agencies so that they can make extra preparations ahead of the elections,” he said.

“We are determined that the 2027 election will be free, inclusive, credible and transparent,” the chairman emphasised.

World.title: Tinubu Tasks Energy Commission On Local Production Of Biofuel
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

* Welcomes Nigeria’s admission into global bioenergy partnership

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has charged the Energy Commission of Nigeria with accelerating the development of the country’s bioenergy industry as part of his administration’s efforts to reduce dependence on petrol and diesel, lower energy costs and create jobs.

The president, in a release issued on Saturday by his Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, gave the charge while welcoming Nigeria’s admission as a Partner Country of the Global Bioenergy Partnership (GBEP), an international initiative hosted by the Food and Agriculture Organisation of the United Nations.

Nigeria’s admission on November 5, 2026, in Rome, Italy, follows the Federal Executive Council’s approval of the Strategic Plan of the Nigeria Bioenergy Partnership.

Since assuming office in 2023, Tinubu has taken steps to diversify Nigeria’s energy sources and reduce energy costs, including establishing the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas, expanding its mandate to include electric vehicles and constituting the Presidential Committee on Green Economic Initiatives.

Nigeria’s participation in the Global Bioenergy Partnership builds on these measures.

The president noted that with Nigeria’s vast agricultural resources, the country has no reason to overlook the economic benefits of converting agricultural waste and other organic materials into commercially viable fuels.

According to Tinubu, “Developing a domestic biofuel industry will open new markets for Nigerian farmers, create employment opportunities and stimulate manufacturing, particularly in rural communities.

“I expect the commission to translate Nigeria’s membership of the Partnership into investments, new industries and more affordable energy for Nigerians.”

The president commended the Director-General of the Energy Commission of Nigeria, Dr Mustapha Abdullahi, and his team for securing Nigeria’s admission into the Partnership and advancing the Federal Government’s energy diversification policy.

Tinubu urged the commission to work with the private sector to establish biofuel production facilities across the country without compromising national food security.

World.title: Gbajabiamila’s LMI Secures Public Service Pathways for 80 Young Nigerians
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

* Says Speaker Abbas to secure internships for fresh graduates in N’Assembly, MDAs

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Legislative Mentorship Initiative (LMI), founded by a former Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, has trained 268 young Nigerians in five years, with more than 80 of its fellows already contributing to public service across the National Assembly, State House, federal and state ministries, departments and agencies.

Gbajabiamila, who is the Chief of Staff to President Bola Tinubu, disclosed this at the graduation ceremony of the initiative’s fifth cohort and celebration of its fifth anniversary in Abuja Saturday.

He said the programme was established to prepare young Nigerians for leadership and equip them with the knowledge and experience required to strengthen public institutions.

He also revealed that the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Tajudeen Abbas, had pledged to personally facilitate internship opportunities for the latest graduates across the National Assembly and various ministries, departments and agencies of government.

According to Gbajabiamila, more than 20 LMI fellows are already working in Abbas’s office and other departments of the National Assembly, a development he described as evidence of the initiative’s growing contribution to Nigeria’s leadership development.

The former Speaker explained that the initiative was conceived in 2022, when he marked his 60th birthday, as a deliberate investment in the future of public leadership and governance in Nigeria.

He said the programme was designed to give young Nigerians early exposure to the workings of public institutions, legislative processes, policymaking and the responsibilities associated with governance, rather than waiting until they occupy positions of authority.

“By the end of today, LMI would have graduated five cohorts in five years and trained 268 dynamic and impressive fellows. Young leaders ready to hit the ground running,” he said.

Gbajabiamila disclosed that the initiative had also entered into a partnership with the Nigerian Technical Aid Corps (NTAC), formalised through a memorandum of understanding signed two days before the graduation ceremony, to facilitate the deployment of its fellows beyond Nigeria.

He expressed appreciation to the Director-General of NTAC, Dr. Buba Yakub, for supporting the initiative and facilitating the partnership.

The former Speaker described the achievements recorded by the programme as encouraging but stressed that its ultimate success would not be determined by the number of graduates or certificates awarded, but by the quality of their contributions to public institutions and society.

He said: “The real test is what our LMI Fellows do with the knowledge, exposure and opportunities they have received. It is the quality of their contributions to public institutions, the integrity with which they discharge their responsibilities and the difference they make in the lives of the people they serve.”

Gbajabiamila maintained that leadership development must be deliberate, inclusive and sustained, stressing that Nigeria could not build strong institutions without preparing competent and public-spirited young people to take up leadership responsibilities.

He noted that the five cohorts had brought together young Nigerians from different states, ethnic, religious, geographical and professional backgrounds, including persons living with disabilities.

According to him, the programme deliberately maintains gender balance and promotes inclusion to ensure that its leadership development process reflects the diversity of the Nigerian society.

Gbajabiamila, who described nation-building as a collective responsibility, acknowledged the contributions of the management team, faculty members, institutional partners and other stakeholders who had sustained the initiative over the past five years.

He particularly commended Abbas for embracing the programme and consistently providing opportunities for its fellows to interact with experienced legislators and gain practical exposure to parliamentary leadership.

He also acknowledged the contributions of the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, whom he described as a consistent supporter of the initiative and a valuable resource person for successive cohorts.

Other personalities he appreciated included the Speaker of the Parliament of Ghana and Chairman of the Conference of Speakers and Presidents of African Legislatures (CoSPAL), Alban Bagbin; Speaker of the House of Representatives of Liberia, Richard Koon; and Deputy Speaker of Nigeria’s House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu.

He also commended the Chairman of the LMI Planning and Advisory Committee and Secretary-General of CoSPAL, Dr. ‘Dapo Oyewole; the Chairman of the Leadership Advancement Foundation (LEAF), Dr. Ike Neliaku; and the Director of LMI, Ms. Solape Sonuga, for their contributions to the growth of the initiative.

The former Speaker disclosed that more than 50 professionals were engaged behind the scenes to ensure the effective planning and implementation of the programme, which, according to him, requires approximately one year of preparation.

He said the initiative had also benefited from the contributions of more than 200 faculty members who had shared their knowledge, professional experience and expertise with the fellows over the years.

Gbajabiamila, however, called for increased financial and institutional support to expand the programme, noting that sustaining its achievements would require more partnerships and resources.

“We will need more support. We will need more hands. And I dare say we will need more pockets, other than mine,” he said.

Earlier, the Director of LMI, Ms. Solape Sonuga, disclosed that the fifth cohort attracted nearly 24,000 initiated applications, out of which more than 7,000 were completed applications.

She said the figures demonstrated the continuing interest of young Nigerians in public service despite growing cynicism about governance and public institutions.

Sonuga described the initiative as a deliberate intervention to develop a pipeline of competent, ethical and committed leaders for Nigeria and Africa.

She said the programme was established on the conviction that leadership succession should not be left to chance but must be deliberately planned through systematic investment in young people.

According to her, the fellows spent three weeks undergoing intensive training and engaging with distinguished parliamentary leaders, diplomats, policymakers, development practitioners and institutional leaders.

She said the programme exposed participants to the practical workings of governance and provided opportunities for them to engage with leaders and institutions beyond Nigeria’s borders.

“The most consequential thing you will take away from this experience is not the calibre of the people you have met, but the calibre of the person you are becoming.

“Because the greatest privilege of this Fellowship is not access. It is transformation,” she said.

Sonuga challenged the graduating fellows to demonstrate intellectual courage, integrity, discipline and excellence in their respective areas of engagement, stressing that they should not wait until they occupy prominent public offices before demonstrating leadership.

She warned that Africa’s major challenge was not a shortage of ambition but the need to strengthen character, competence, commitment and conviction among those aspiring to lead.

In a special recognition segment, Gbajabiamila announced Laraba Joshua from Kebbi State as the recipient of the Oluwadamilola Agbaje Outstanding Fellow Award for Cohort Five.

The award was established in memory of Oluwadamilola Agbaje, a member of Cohort Three who died last year, to recognise fellows who exemplify the values of excellence, integrity, commitment and service upon which the initiative was founded.

Gbajabiamila described Joshua’s story as exceptional, noting that she was among the first few people from her village to attend university and had subsequently devoted herself to advocacy aimed at expanding educational opportunities for other young people.

He said her commitment to helping others access opportunities reflected the kind of selfless leadership the initiative sought to cultivate.

In her vote of thanks, the Vice-Chairperson of the LMI Planning and Advisory Committee, Ms. Adeola Olayinka, expressed appreciation to Gbajabiamila, Abbas, the management team, faculty members, institutional partners and other stakeholders for sustaining the initiative.

She congratulated the graduating fellows and reminded them that the fellowship was not the destination but the beginning of greater responsibilities in public service and nation-building.

Olayinka also disclosed that preparations for the sixth cohort would commence immediately, signalling the initiative’s determination to sustain its leadership development programme.

World.title: Nnaji Unveils Manifesto, Prioritises Open Governance, Job Creation
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Gideon Arinze in Enugu

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Enugu State, Chief Uche Nnaji, has unveiled his manifesto ahead of the 2027 governorship election, prioritising job creation, industrialisation and open governance.

Nnaji unveiled the manifesto Saturday, in Enugu during the inauguration of the party’s campaign council, pledging to generate 50,000 direct and indirect jobs through industrial development.

He said the proposed industries would create employment opportunities for young people, stimulate economic activities and help address hunger and insecurity in the state.

“What we are doing is giving a manifesto based on truth and reality, not a manifesto based on lies,” he said. “When we build these industries, we will be able to take a minimum of 50,000 youths off the streets through direct and indirect employment,” he said.

Speaking further, he said: “We want to have a society where there will be no danger to people’s lives. We want to wipe out or drastically reduce hunger in this state.”

The candidate said his administration would also promote open governance by publishing government budgets and making contract details accessible to the public to strengthen transparency and accountability.

Earlier, the PDP deputy governorship candidate, Chief Peter Ugwu, urged members of the campaign council and local government campaign leaders to take the campaign to their communities and mobilise grassroots support ahead of the February 6 election.

Also speaking, the party’s state Secretary, Chukwunonye Okereke, reiterated that the party’s manifesto was anchored on five pillars, including governance, security, economic prosperity, industrialisation and infrastructural development.

World.title: YABATECH, Al Basar Foundation Screen 2,500, Performs 421 Eye Surgeries in Free Medical Outreach
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Funmi Ogundare

Yaba College of Technology (YABATECH) has screened about 2,500 people for eye-related ailments and performed 421 surgeries as part of its six-day free medical outreach aimed at improving access to eye care for underserved communities.

The six-day outreach is coordinated by the college’s Centre for Linkages, Partnerships and Collaborations and Centre for Information, Communications and Public Relations, alongside the Directorate of Medical Services.

The Deputy Rector (Academics), Dr. Ismail Badmus, disclosed this weekend at the medical outreach programme organised in collaboration with the Al Basar International Foundation.

Badmus said the college had initially targeted screening 7,000 people and conducting about 700 surgeries but had so far screened 2,500 out of the revised target of 4,000, while 421 surgeries had been performed.

He explained that the surgeries, which focused mainly on cataracts, were being conducted at the Gbagada General Hospital, with the college’s medical services department and two other centres coordinating the exercise.

According to him, the outreach also involves volunteers from within and outside the institution, who are supporting the delivery of medical services to beneficiaries.

The deputy rector said the initiative was part of the institution’s corporate social responsibility to give back to the communities that had supported its operations over the years.

He noted that YABATECH believed its responsibility extended beyond producing skilled graduates to addressing the needs and challenges of the wider society.

“This is the fourth time we are doing it. We feel that we owe society more than the production of graduates that are built and featured. It is part of our corporate social responsibility to give back to society at large,” he stated.

He added that the college’s relationship with its host communities had made it necessary to identify with their challenges and provide assistance, particularly in areas where residents lacked access to affordable healthcare.

Badmus observed that many of the beneficiaries were aged between 40 and 70, with some unable to afford the cost of cataract surgery.

He explained that the college had expanded the scope of this year’s intervention to include glaucoma surgeries, with a target of 100 procedures.

Badmus said the decision followed the realisation that some patients who turned up for screening had neither cataracts nor glaucoma, making them ineligible for the initial surgical intervention.

He said the college had, for the first time, decided to extend assistance to members of the public with other eye-related conditions rather than turn them away without support.

According to him, “The institution is inviting members of the public to help identify and refer people who may have been missed during the exercise for possible intervention.

He, however, acknowledged that the outreach was yet to meet its initial screening and surgery targets, expressing hope that the intervention would reach more beneficiaries.

Speaking with journalists, the Regional Manager of Al Basar International Foundation, Bello Abdullahi Yuguda, explained that the intervention was designed to provide free eye care and medication to less privileged Nigerians who could not afford specialised treatment.

He stated that the foundation had set a target of conducting 700 surgeries and reaching about 4,000 people with free medical consultations, medicines and eyeglasses.

He said while more than 450 patients had undergone cataract and pterygium surgeries, another 100 patients diagnosed with glaucoma had been referred to the foundation’s hospital in Ibadan for further investigations before surgery.

This, he said, brought the number of patients identified for surgical intervention to about 550, with additional approvals secured for patients requiring retina and other complicated eye surgeries in Kano.

According to him, the foundation is committed to ensuring that beneficiaries receive quality eye care, regardless of their financial circumstances.

“Our intention for this outreach is to cater for the less privileged. Our target is to have 700 surgeries, as well as reach about 4,000 people with the distribution of medicines and eyeglasses.

“With the collaboration of YABATECH, as well as the intervention of the state and local governments, we are able to achieve this target and make the outreach successful,” he stressed.

Yuguda explained that the programme was supported by humanitarian organisations and sponsors who funded the surgeries and other medical interventions.

Some beneficiaries of the free eye-care outreach, expressed gratitude to the organisers, describing the initiative as a life-changing intervention that had enabled them to regain their sight.

One of the beneficiaries, John Isibor, thanked God and the foundation for providing the opportunity to access eye treatment that would otherwise have been beyond his financial means.

“First of all, I thank God and the foundation behind this programme. I pray that God will also surprise them and provide everything they need but cannot afford,” he said.

World.title: CNS: We Must Be Fit, Ready to Serve Whenever Duty Calls
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

* Orders personnel to make physical fitness part of their daily routine

Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Chief of Naval Staff (CNS), Vice Admiral Idi Abbas, has said that officers and ratings of the Nigerian Navy must be fit and ready to serve whenever duty calls.

Vice Admiral Abbas also ordered all personnel of the Nigerian Navy to make physical fitness part of their daily routine and sustain regular physical training across all Navy units, so that the Service will continue building individual fitness and overall operational effectiveness.

Speaking during the Fourth Quarter Route March in Abuja on Saturday, the CNS explained that the routine exercise builds the collective endurance of personnel, raises their physical fitness and strengthens teamwork among commands and establishments.

Represented by the Director of Project Implementation, Monitoring and Evaluation at Naval Headquarters, Rear Admiral Mohammed Yakubu Dahiru, the CNS said that the route march is held every quarter as part of the Nigerian Navy’s regular training programme.

He said: “It also reinforces a standard that applies to every officer and rating: we must be fit and ready to serve whenever duty calls. This quarterly exercise supports the Chief of the Naval Staff’s mission to deploy a highly motivated and professional naval force capable of safeguarding Nigeria’s maritime interests and contributing effectively to joint operations.

“Whether on patrol, responding to an emergency or supporting joint counter-terrorism and counter-insurgency operations, fitter personnel are better prepared for the demands of the mission and can sustain their performance until it is complete.”

He also spoke on ongoing operations, stating: “Our operational successes this year, particularly in Operation Delta Sentinel and across joint theatres nationwide, demonstrate why physical standards matter. Naval personnel have disrupted illegal refining sites and recovered suspected stolen crude oil, thereby denying criminal elements the proceeds of crime.

“Across our commands, bases and formations, we have rescued kidnap victims, protected critical maritime infrastructure, helped secure our waterways and taken the lead in neutralising violent extremist insurgents in ongoing counter-terrorism and counter-insurgency operations.

“Behind each of these results are personnel who can sustain long hours on duty, remain alert as fatigue sets in and work together when the pressure is greatest.”

Commending their dedication, resilience and service to the nation, Vice Admiral Abbas urged personnel to carry the same discipline, vigilance and teamwork they demonstrated into every assignment as the year draws to a close.

“While the Route March is quarterly, readiness is a daily responsibility. The standards we uphold in training are the standards we take into operations, so let us continue to hold ourselves to a level that reflects our core values of integrity, professionalism and teamwork,” he concluded.

World.title: Stakeholders Urge Men to Prioritise Family, Health, Values Above Wealth
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Business leaders, military officers, medical professionals and traditional rulers have called on men to prioritise their physical and mental health, family responsibilities and personal values while pursuing professional and financial success.

They made the call at the inaugural edition of The Marriott Conversation, organised by Etiquette, Poise & Protocol Resource (EPRA) at the Lagos Marriott Hotel, Ikeja, to commemorate International Men’s Day.

The event, themed ‘The Man, His Mission, The Legacy,’ attracted 71 participants aged between 29 and 76, while 11 others participated virtually.

The gathering featured keynote addresses, interactive sessions and panel discussions on marriage, fatherhood, financial responsibilities, emotional intelligence and mental health.

Speaking at the event, Chairman of EPRA, Mr. Olutunji Oladimeji, said the initiative was designed to encourage men to reflect on their personal lives beyond professional accomplishments and societal expectations.

“TMC 2026 was an opportunity to look beyond professional titles, financial accomplishments and social expectations, and examine the man behind these achievements,” he said.

Oladimeji expressed concern over family conflicts and the pressures associated with financial and social responsibilities, stressing the need for men to pay greater attention to their well-being.

“Our intention is to encourage personal reflection leading to a wholesome redemption, rather than conventional motivational speeches,” he added.

In his keynote address, Group Chief Executive Officer of Aradel Holdings, Dr. Adegbite Falade, highlighted the emotional and psychological pressures confronting men in their efforts to fulfil family and professional obligations.

Falade, who addressed participants through a recorded presentation, noted that societal expectations often discouraged men from acknowledging their struggles and seeking assistance.

“Strength is not always the absence of struggle. Strength is the courage to recognise struggle and to seek help before it destroys you,” he said.

He urged men to avoid pursuing financial and professional achievements at the expense of their marriages, relationships with their children and personal health.

“Success is a terrible bargain if your wife becomes a stranger and your children become spectators of your life.

“Never sacrifice permanent relationships on the altar of temporary accomplishments. It is not worth it,” Falade stated.

Speaking on the importance of building a lasting legacy, he encouraged men to invest in the character and development of their children rather than concentrate solely on material inheritance.

“An inheritance is what you leave for your children. A legacy is what you leave in your children,” he said.

Also speaking, Air Vice Marshal Albert Bot emphasised the importance of emotional intelligence in managing personal relationships, professional responsibilities and societal expectations.

Bot urged men to develop the capacity to manage anger, stress and interpersonal conflicts without undermining their relationships.

He distinguished between reacting emotionally to situations and responding constructively to challenges, noting that effective conflict management was essential to maintaining healthy relationships.

“The man you are on the inside should be bigger than the person on the outside,” he said.

The Special Guest of Honour and Eze Aro IX of Arochukwu Kingdom, Dr. Eberechukwu Oji, stressed the importance of faith, family, mentorship and accountability in helping men navigate life’s challenges.

The traditional ruler encouraged men to embrace vulnerability and seek support from trusted friends, mentors and family members when confronted with difficult circumstances.

Speaking on parenting, Oji urged fathers to instil discipline and responsibility in their children.

“The cure to entitlement is to teach a sense of responsibility,” he said.

The event also featured a session during which two elders shared their experiences on marriage, parenting and family relationships.

A retired medical professional, Pa Okungbaye, encouraged men to demonstrate commitment to their families through active participation in domestic responsibilities, effective communication and mutual respect.

Similarly, Chairman of Mind Builders Schools, Elder Bosun Falore, identified prayer, patience and presence as essential elements of successful family relationships.

Falore maintained that financial provision alone was insufficient to sustain a family, stressing the importance of emotional maturity and active involvement in the lives of spouses and children.

During a panel session moderated by Charles Okeibunor, participants examined the challenges associated with extended family financial obligations, work-life balance and mental health.

The Chief Executive Officer of Doughcrust and men’s mental health advocate, Mr. Ayokunle Okuneye, urged men to establish financial boundaries while supporting members of their extended families.

He noted that excessive financial commitments could undermine personal well-being and financial stability.

Executive Director of MoMo Payment Service Bank, Mr. Femi Aminu, also advised men to provide financial assistance within their means and avoid commitments that could expose them to unnecessary pressure.

On his part, Group Executive Director, West and Central Africa, Omnicom Media Group, Mr. Yinka Adebayo, encouraged men to avoid unhealthy comparisons and competition while pursuing their personal and professional goals.

Other panellists included the Medical Director of Divine Medicals Centre, Dr. Greg Osagie, and Executive Director, Sales, Carloha Nigeria, Mr. Joseph Omokaphue.

The panellists stressed the need for men to strike a balance between financial responsibilities and active participation in family life, noting that spouses and children required emotional support and attention beyond material provision.

The event received support from Carloha Nigeria and Gee Royal, while representatives of Unitrust Insurance, Uridium Technology, Coronation Insurance and ToriBOX also participated.

Meanwhile, EPRA disclosed plans to sustain the conversation through an initiative tagged ‘Brotherhood Code,’ which would feature online engagements, smaller gatherings and access to support resources.

The organisers also disclosed that preparations had commenced for the second edition of The Marriott Conversation.

Established in 2011, EPRA provides training in etiquette, emotional intelligence, social conduct and professional development for educational institutions and corporate organisations.

World.title: Here are all the mayors in charge of South Africa’s 8 metros
World.content:
Coalition negotiations have reshaped South Africa’s eight metros, with the DA leading just two despite winning the most votes in six. Image: X @geordinhl

The Democratic Alliance (DA) emerged as the biggest political winner in terms of votes in South Africa’s 2026 local government elections, but coalition politics has prevented it from translating that support into control of most of the country’s biggest cities.

Following two weeks of negotiations, political manoeuvring and coalition horse-trading, the leadership of all eight metropolitan municipalities has now been decided.

Political setback

The final outcome is a significant political setback for the DA, which secured the largest share of votes in six of the eight metros, but will govern only two.



The party retained control of the City of Cape Town, where leader Geordin Hill-Lewis was elected mayor through an outright DA majority.

It also secured the mayoralty in Nelson Mandela Bay, with Retief Odendaal elected through a six-party coalition.

READ | DA forms six-party coalition to govern Nelson Mandela Bay

However, the DA was shut out of power in all three Gauteng metros, despite its strong electoral performance.

Instead, ActionSA emerged as one of the biggest winners of the coalition negotiations, securing the mayoral positions in Johannesburg and Tshwane.

ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba was elected mayor of Johannesburg, while Nasiphi Moya retained the top position in Tshwane.



The ANC, meanwhile, secured control of Ekurhuleni, adding to its victories in Buffalo City and Mangaung.

The MK Party also made a major breakthrough by taking control of eThekwini, the first time it has contested local government elections.

READ | DA condemns Tshwane ANC, ActionSA ‘coalition of chaos’

Gauteng becomes the biggest coalition battleground

The political battle for Gauteng’s three metros was among the most closely watched negotiations following the elections.

The DA had hoped its electoral support would translate into mayoral control, but rival parties combined their numbers to prevent this.

ActionSA emerged with the mayoralties in Johannesburg and Tshwane, while the ANC secured Ekurhuleni.

The arrangements brought together the ANC, ActionSA and EFF, with the MK Party also involved in the broader negotiations.

There was, however, uncertainty around the MK Party’s participation in Tshwane, highlighting the fragile nature of some of the political agreements.

The result is a major development for ActionSA, which has managed to secure control of two of the country’s most important metropolitan municipalities.

For Mashaba, his election as Johannesburg mayor represents a return to the city’s top political office after previously serving in the position between 2016 and 2019.

Moya’s election in Tshwane also strengthens ActionSA’s position in Gauteng, where the party has become an important player in coalition politics.

ANC retains three metros despite losing ground

The ANC has managed to retain control of three metropolitan municipalities, although it has had to rely on coalition partners to do so.

In Buffalo City, the party lost its outright majority for the first time but secured support from the EFF, Patriotic Alliance, PAC and AIC.

Princess Faku was elected mayor, with Yomelela Tyali as deputy mayor and Bongiwe Saulie as speaker.

READ | ANC joins forces with EFF to keep control of Buffalo City

The ANC also secured Ekurhuleni through a multi-party arrangement involving ActionSA, the EFF and MK Party.

Mziyanda Mketsu was elected mayor, while EFF councillor Nthabiseng Tshivhenga secured the position of speaker.

In Mangaung, the ANC entered into an arrangement with the EFF, MK Party and smaller parties.

Vumile Nikelo was elected mayor, with EFF representative Sam Matiase as deputy mayor.

The results demonstrate that, despite losing support at the ballot box, the ANC remains a powerful force in local government negotiations.

MK Party makes its mark in eThekwini

One of the most significant outcomes of the elections was the MK Party’s capture of eThekwini.

The party, which contested local government elections for the first time, secured the mayoral position through an arrangement with the ANC.

Apostle Mxolisi Phakathi was elected mayor, while Thabani Luthuli became deputy mayor.

The ANC retained the speaker’s position, with Thabani Nyawose elected to the role.

The result gives the MK Party control of one of South Africa’s most politically and economically important municipalities.

It also represents a major shift in KwaZulu-Natal politics, where the party has rapidly established itself as a significant electoral force.

DA keeps Cape Town and Nelson Mandela Bay

The DA’s two mayoral victories came in Cape Town and Nelson Mandela Bay.

In Cape Town, Hill-Lewis secured another term with the backing of an outright DA majority.

The result makes the City of Cape Town the only metro among the eight where a single party has secured an outright majority.

In Nelson Mandela Bay, the DA needed a much broader political arrangement.

Odendaal was elected mayor through an agreement involving the DA, Freedom Front Plus, ACDP, ActionSA, PAC and UDM.

The coalition also saw ACDP councillor Lance Grootboom elected deputy mayor.

Who controls South Africa’s eight metros?

The final mayoral positions are as follows:

Metro Mayor Party Johannesburg Herman Mashaba ActionSA Tshwane Nasiphi Moya ActionSA Ekurhuleni Mziyanda Mketsu ANC Cape Town Geordin Hill-Lewis DA eThekwini Apostle Mxolisi Phakathi MK Party Buffalo City Princess Faku ANC Nelson Mandela Bay Retief Odendaal DA Mangaung Vumile Nikelo ANC

Coalition politics reshapes South Africa’s political map

The outcome of the 2026 local government elections highlights the growing importance of coalition politics in South Africa.

Winning the largest share of votes is no longer necessarily enough to secure control of a municipality.

The DA’s position in the metros is perhaps the clearest example. Despite topping the polls in six municipalities, it will lead only two.

ActionSA, meanwhile, has secured two mayoralties in Gauteng, while the ANC has managed to retain control of three metros through coalition arrangements.

The MK Party’s victory in eThekwini further demonstrates how the country’s political landscape has changed since the party entered electoral politics.

The new administrations now face the challenge of keeping their coalitions together while delivering services to residents.

For voters, the next five years will provide a test of whether the parties that successfully negotiated their way into power can govern as effectively as they campaigned.

World.title: Daniël Stevens memorial: ‘We still had so much life left to live’
World.content:
Daniël Stevens’ best friend recalled their shared love of fishing during an emotional tribute at his memorial service on Saturday. Image: Facebook/Daniël Stevens

Family and friends gathered at the Uitenhage Baptist Church in Kariega on Saturday, 28 November, to bid farewell to Daniël Stevens.

The 25-year-old died on Monday, 23 November, following an alleged assault outside Je’Vista Social Café in Jeffreys Bay.

His older brother, JC Stevens, told mourners that the family had received messages of condolences from as far as the United States, Dubai and Australia.



His best friend and business partner, Dylan, who is currently in the US, also paid tribute, expressing his anger and sadness over losing his friend.

DANIËL STEVENS’ BROTHER RECEIVES MORE THAN 1 000 MESSAGES

JC thanked those who had supported the family since his brother’s death, saying he had received more than 1 000 WhatsApp and inbox messages.

“During this time we received messages from America, from Dubai, from Australia, people we haven’t met,” he said.

He also thanked those who had contributed to the BackaBuddy campaign and travelled to attend the service.

JC recalled their childhood disagreements and how the brothers had grown closer in recent months.

“We used to fight a lot but we were on the same team,” he said.



He said he would strive to emulate his younger brother’s ability to connect with people and make everyone feel special.

‘WE STILL HAD SO MUCH LIFE LEFT TO LIVE’

Dylan, who could not attend the memorial in person, shared a letter, recalling the years he and Stevens spent living and working together.

“It breaks my heart that I am halfway across the world and cannot stand there with all of you to say goodbye in person,” he said.

“We still had so much life left to live.”

The two became friends after high school and later pursued several business ventures together.

Dylan recalled how they initially struggled to afford bread and butter for dinner. They spent many evenings at home because they had no money to go out.

“Looking back, I’m so proud that we survived those years, those tough times side by side,” he said.

“He was my friend, my brother, my teacher, my therapist and my own personal Google assistant.”

Dylan also spoke about their fishing trips, recalling how Stevens would make him walk kilometres to reach their fishing spots.

“I’m going to miss our fishing trips more than words can ever say.”

‘WHEN LIFE GOT HEAVY, YOU CALLED DANIËL’

Jessica, who recently moved from Cape Town, told mourners she had known Stevens for only two months.

He taught her to play chess, and she recalled how she managed to beat him once, despite forgetting to say checkmate.

Jessica, who does not have a brother, said she jokingly referred to herself as his adopted sister.

Another friend recalled their late-night drives and how Stevens always answered his phone when someone needed him.

“When you needed advice, you called Daniel. When you needed a talk, you called Daniel. When life got heavy and you needed to get out, you called Daniel.”

He said the two rarely took photographs together because they preferred to enjoy each other’s company.

“Now I understand how much those moments were worth,” he said.

FOUR ACCUSED REMAIN BEHIND BARS

The four people accused in connection with Stevens’ death remain in custody after appearing in the Humansdorp Magistrate’s Court on Friday, 27 November.

Three of the accused are adults, while the fourth is a 16-year-old whose identity the Child Justice Act protects.

Dylan ended his tribute with a promise to honour his best friend’s memory.

“I love you forever, brother. I will carry your spirit with me wherever I go in this world.

“And I promise I will never stop honouring everything we’ve achieved together. Rest easy until I see you again.”

World.title: Jacob Zuma appoints DAUGHTER to senior MK Party role
World.content:
Former president Jacob Zuma has appointed his daughter, Thuthukile Zuma, as acting deputy secretary-general of the uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party. Image: X/MK Party

Former president Jacob Zuma has appointed his daughter, Thuthukile Zuma, as acting deputy secretary-general of the uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party, while also directing that she be deployed to Parliament as an MP.

The appointment takes effect immediately, the party announced.

READ | DA condemns Tshwane ANC, ActionSA ‘coalition of chaos’



Thuthukile Zuma is expected to be sworn in as a Member of Parliament representing the MK Party, with the party saying her deployment is intended to strengthen its parliamentary caucus.

The announcement marks a significant development in her political career, coming shortly after she resigned from the African National Congress’ (ANC) Greater Johannesburg Regional Executive Committee.

[MEDIA STATEMENT]

PRESIDENT JACOB ZUMA APPOINTS THUTHUKILE ZUMA AS ACTING DEPUTY SECRETARY GENERAL OF THE MK PARTY pic.twitter.com/IKG4zHErpY  November 27, 2026

MK Party leadership changes

In addition to appointing his daughter, Jacob Zuma reaffirmed Sifiso Mahlangu as the MK Party’s national spokesperson.

Mahlangu will continue overseeing the party’s media relations and public messaging.

Lindiwe Mtshali will also remain in her position as acting secretary-general.



The party described Thuthukile Zuma as an experienced political activist with a longstanding record of involvement in organisational leadership.

It said she would bring political and administrative experience to her new responsibilities.

From ANC to MK Party

Thuthukile Zuma’s appointment comes less than three weeks after she resigned from the ANC’s Johannesburg regional leadership structure.



She stepped down on 10 November, ahead of disciplinary proceedings initiated by the ANC Greater Johannesburg Region.

The party had accused her of neglecting her responsibilities as a regional executive committee member, including allegedly missing meetings and failing to participate adequately in election campaign activities.

She was also accused of breaching the ANC’s social media protocols through criticism of party leadership.



Thuthukile rejected the allegations, arguing that the disciplinary process was an attempt to silence her.

At the time of her resignation, she said her departure from the regional structure should not be interpreted as an admission of wrongdoing.

Her appointment to the MK Party’s senior leadership and planned deployment to Parliament now represent a further shift in her political direction.



Zuma’s daughter to join MK Party caucus

The MK Party said Thuthukile Zuma’s arrival in Parliament would strengthen its parliamentary caucus.

The party has not specified when she will be sworn in as an MP.

Her appointment is likely to attract attention given her family ties to the party’s president and the prominent role the Zuma family continues to play in the MK Party.



The announcement comes as the party continues to adjust its leadership and parliamentary structures.

World.title: Springbok forwards shake-up: De Villiers, Hanekom in back row
World.content:
Paul de Villiers is drafted into the Springboks squad for the France clash, with Cameron Hanekom pivoting. Image: South Africa Rugby (X).

The Springboks have tweaked their back row for Sunday’s clash at Twickenham.

South Africa face France in the Nations Championship final on 29 November.

Pieter-Steph du Toit has returned home, with his replacement being confirmed.



changes TO SQUAD for Nations Championship final

Sunday’s final is a rematch from two weeks ago, when the French were victorious in Saint-Denis.

Les Bleus are top of the Northern Hemisphere standings, while the Springboks lead the Southern Hemisphere log.

Their clash at Twickenham determines which half of the world the inaugural Nations Championship title heads to.

With coach Rassie Erasmus suspended, the world champs have named an impressive squad to play in London.

South Africa Rugby confirmed two changes to Springboks forwards today (Saturday, 28 November).

Loose forward Paul de Villiers will earn his ninth cap in the 8 jersey.



Eighth man Cameron Hanekom pivots to 7 in place of the injured Pieter-Steph du Toit.

Fellow loose forward Franco Mostert will earn his cap from the replacements bench.

South Africa focusing on fundamentals

The match has arguably more significance for South Africa, who are currently on a two-match losing streak.

After the defeat to France in Paris, the Springboks fell to Ireland in Dublin a week later.

A losing bonus point saw them advance to the final, finishing just ahead of New Zealand.

One of the talking points was South Africa’s backline failing to find its feet in the north.

Manie Libbok’s return at flyhalf is an important step towards more control at crucial phases of the game.

The Springbok 10 said he was looking forward to a tough contest in London, as quoted by SA Rugby:

“My focus is just on executing the basics well and backing my teammates. The coaches have backed me, so it’s my job to go out there and do what has been asked of me. There’s always excitement going into a final, and I’m looking forward to it.”

Fixture details are as follows:

Springboks vs France – 29 November, Twickenham Stadium, London (18:40).

World.title: ‘You need to eat pap’: Pensioner’s stark warning about what the grant really buys
World.content:
Older South Africans say the Older Persons Grant leaves them choosing between a roof over their heads and a proper meal. For some, it covers neither.

Helen Titta gave one of the most striking descriptions of grant life on The South African’s Facebook page.

“A pensioner has to live in a squatter camp to be able to service in R2 400 a month, that’s without food, or you need to eat pap, no, cause it ridiculous,” she wrote.



Her comment paints a grim picture. In her view, surviving on the grant means either giving up decent housing or cutting meals down to the barest staple. Pap is a filling, affordable and much-loved meal in South African homes.

Bills come first

Other commenters said their fixed costs swallow the grant before they can think about groceries.

Henny Wybenga wrote in Afrikaans: “Wat Kan jy met R2400 doen niks krag huur kos? R5000 sal doen.”



Loosely translated, he listed electricity, rent and food. He asked what R2 400 can possibly cover and said R5 000 would be enough.

Rentia Wright said the money disappears almost instantly.

“Our pension doesn’t even last 2 days!” she wrote.



When rent and electricity are paid first, food becomes whatever is left over. For many pensioners, that is very little.

Stretching every rand

The Older Persons Grant went up by R80 to R2 400 in April.

For pensioners like Titta, that increase works out to less than R3 extra a day. That barely covers a single loaf of bread over two days.



Ansie Roos said price increases have left pensioners struggling despite their gratitude.

“We are thankful, but with all the price increases, we can’t really survive,” she wrote.

Older South Africans describe a careful daily balancing act. They buy in bulk where they can, skip meals so the food lasts, and rely on the cheapest staples to fill the gap.



Titta’s comment is blunt, but it raises a question many grant recipients are asking. The grant keeps pensioners alive. Many say it does not allow them to live well.

For older South Africans sitting down to another plate of plain pap, the difference matters.

World.title: Zimbabwe football enters a new era as VAR makes historic debut
World.content:
Zimbabwean football is set to enter a new era on Saturday, 28 November, when the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) system is used for the first time during the 2026 Chibuku Super Cup final between Hardrock and Highlanders.

The introduction of the technology at Chahwanda Stadium marks a significant development for the domestic game, which has often faced scrutiny over refereeing decisions and controversial incidents during matches.

VAR is designed to assist match officials in reviewing potentially game-changing decisions, including goals, penalty incidents, direct red cards and cases of mistaken identity.



The technology allows referees to receive additional information from video footage before making or confirming decisions.

However, the final decision remains with the referee on the field.

Its introduction could help officials correct clear and obvious errors while providing additional support during high-pressure moments in matches.

ZIFA prepares referees for historic introduction

The Zimbabwe Football Association (ZIFA) has been preparing for the historic introduction, with members of its Referees Committee undergoing VAR training last month.

The training covered how the system operates, communication between match officials during reviews and the procedures involved in reaching accurate decisions.

ZIFA president Nqobile Magwizi described the development as a major milestone, saying preparations had been completed ahead of the final.



“Everything is in place. Referees will now have additional support. If there is a penalty incident that is unclear, they can review it. If there is a goal that appears to be offside, they can check it. If there is a red-card decision that requires a second look, they can review it,” Magwizi said, according to The Herald.

Challenges and expectations surrounding VAR

The technology’s arrival could also place greater attention on the standards of local officiating, particularly how referees communicate and manage high-pressure situations.

While VAR can help identify clear and obvious errors, its effectiveness depends on proper implementation, trained officials and the availability of the necessary technical infrastructure.

The final will provide the first opportunity to see how the system operates in Zimbabwean domestic football, with its introduction potentially opening the door for wider use in local competitions.

World.title: Cape Town snags spot on world’s best cities for shopping list
World.content:
Cape Town is one of 20 cities that has been recognised as a prime shopping location. Image: THEGIFT777/ Canva

Black Friday may be over, but in Cape Town, the shopping never ends. That’s why the Mother City has earned a spot on yet another prestigious list.

The English publication Time Out just released its “World’s 20 Best Cities for Shopping” list for 2026. Based on eight categories including fashion and clothing, food and groceries, and gifts and lifestyle – as well as factors like affordability, safety and restaurants – over 24 000 people in cities worldwide were asked to rate their local shopping scene.

Here’s how the Mother City fared …



CAPE TOWN: A FASHIONABLE 15TH PLACE

Out of the 20 cities that made the list, Cape Town achieved an applaudable 15th place.

What’s impressive is that ol’ CPT beat out the likes of Barcelona, Florence and Vienna, where niche boutiques, luxury fashion houses, artisanal emporiums and vintage stores are the name of the game. And let’s not get started on the delish food! Even Bogotá and Hong Kong trail behind the Mother City.

Canal Walk is one of the gems in Cape Town’s retail crown. Image: Arnold Petersen/ Canva

According to Time Out, it comes down to Cape Town’s wide range of retailers that cater to every resident and visitor to the city. Whether it’s retail therapy central V&A Waterfront, the never-ending Canal Walk, bazaars in the Cape Flats, mall meccas like Tyger Valley or Blue Route, or factory outlet giant Access Park, there are plenty of places where you can shop ‘til you drop.

World.title: Yellow Level 4 warning for severe thunderstorms in eastern KZN
World.content:
Severe thunderstorms could bring heavy rain, flooding and damaging winds to parts of KwaZulu-Natal. Image: Pexels

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued a Yellow Level 4 warning for severe thunderstorms in parts of KwaZulu-Natal on Saturday, 28 November.

The storms could bring heavy downpours, strong winds and lightning, with possible flooding and damage to infrastructure.

SAWS expects thunderstorms to develop over the eastern parts of the province during the afternoon.



Yellow (darker) level 4 warning for severe thunderstorms

Area: KwaZulu Natal

Validity: Saturday, 28 November 2026#saws #weatheroutlook #warning pic.twitter.com/jRU8h2haLH — SA Weather Service (@SAWeatherServic) November 27, 2026

The warning remains in place from 12:00 until 22:59.

Flooding and dangerous driving conditions

The weather service warns that heavy rain could flood settlements, roads and bridges.



Fast-flowing streams and deep water could put lives at risk, while falling trees may block major roads.

Motorists should expect poor driving conditions and avoid crossing flooded roads or bridges.

Severe THUNDERstorms expected over eastern KZN

SAWS says a surface trough over central South Africa, a cold front and a ridging high-pressure system along the east coast will help bring widespread showers and thunderstorms to KwaZulu-Natal.



An upper-air trough will also support storm development.

The storms could become severe in places over the eastern parts of the province during the afternoon.

SAWS says the likelihood of significant impacts remains low, despite the warning.



Residents should monitor weather updates and take precautions as thunderstorms develop.

World.title: Prosecutors seek 25-year sentence for Canada suicide poison seller
World.content:
CANADA - Canadian prosecutors on Friday requested a 25-year prison sentence for a man who sold poison to help people commit suicide, stressing his victims were largely young and experiencing mental distress.

Former chef Kenneth Law pleaded guilty earlier this year to aiding 14 suicides in Canada, but he has admitted to selling hundreds of so-called suicide kits globally through a series of online forums.

Prosecutors had also charged him with murder but, citing a lack of evidence, agreed to withdraw the more serious accusations in exchange for Law pleading guilty to lesser offenses.

That decision drew widespread condemnation, notably from friends and family of victims who believed Law was directly responsible for killing their loved ones, but prosecutors maintained they would still seek a stiff penalty.

"An appropriate global sentence to impose in this matter is 25 years less (time already served)," Crown prosecutor Katie Doherty told the court.

Law's lawyers argued against imposing what could effectively be a life sentence for the 61-year-old.

Law told the court he understood his conduct was "categorically wrong" and that he had been "changed" by the legal process.

"I remain remorseful," he said.

Courts often use comparable cases in determining sentencing, but Doherty noted there is "no case even remotely similar to Mr Law's conduct."

The judge will decide on sentencing on February 26.

-APF

World.title: 'Every door she opened, she sought to open for others' - Ramaphosa on Mlambo-Ngcuka
World.content:
EXESI - President Cyril Ramaphosa has paid tribute to the late former deputy president Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, describing her as a woman of extraordinary strength.

In his eulogy, Ramaphosa highlighted her achievements, including becoming the first black woman to serve as Minister of Minerals and Energy, the first woman to be Deputy President and the first African to head UN Women.

He said that while these positions, in their own right, were achievements, the difference she made in them should also be recognised.

“What defines her greatness is what she did with the opportunities she was given. It is for how she used those positions to improve the lives of others. Every door that opened for her became a door through which she sought to bring others. “Every position she occupied became a platform from which she sought to advance the interests of those who had been excluded. We honour her for the difference she made. For the legacy that she left behind,” Ramaphosa said.

According to Ramaphosa, Mlambo-Ngcuka will be remembered not only as a distinguished leader of our nation, but as a comrade, a colleague, a friend and a sister.

World.title: Mlambo-Ngcuka's funeral brings historic moment for Bhisho Airport
World.content:
EXESI - Bhisho Airport in the Eastern Cape welcomed a sitting South African President for the first time in its history.

President Cyril Ramaphosa landed at the airport on Saturday morning before travelling to eXesi to attend the funeral of former deputy president Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka.

The airport also welcomed former President Thabo Mbeki before Ramaphosa’s arrival.

READ | LIVESTREAM | State Funeral of the late former deputy president Mlambo-Ngcuka

Eastern Cape Transport described the arrivals as a historic moment.

“Both dignitaries landed at this lesser-known but more than capable airport en route to Middledrift (eXesi ) to bid farewell to former Deputy President Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, who is being laid to rest today. A proud and historic milestone for Bhisho Airport and the Eastern Cape,” the provincial transport department said.

Meanwhile, Eastern Cape Premier Oscar Mabuyane said the province is ‘humbled by the responsibility of becoming her final resting place’.

He's been confirmed as an uncontested candidate.

World.title: 'We dare not fail her' - Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka's legacy honoured
World.content:
EXESI - For the Mlambo-Ngcuka family and the people of South Africa, the reality of loss is sinking in as the final farewell for former Deputy President Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka was held on Saturday.

She died at the age of 71, leaving behind a legacy of public service and championing human rights.

The official state funeral proceedings began after a family service held at the Mlambo-Ngcuka’s home in eXesi village in the Eastern Cape.

President Cyril Ramaphosa was present as the late Dr Mlambo-Ngcuka casket was carried into the funeral marquee as it began to rain.

World.title: LIVESTREAM | State Funeral of the late former deputy president Mlambo-Ngcuka
World.content:
EXESI - Family, friends and comrades have gathered to pay their final respects to Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka.

The former Deputy President will be buried in eXesi in the Eastern Cape.

President Cyril Ramaphosa will deliver the eulogy at her state funeral.

Mlambo-Ngcuka died last week following complications from a recent medical procedure.

World.title: Mourners commemorate Mlambo-Ngcuka ahead of state funeral
World.content:
EXESI - A communal prayer and memorial service for late former Deputy President Dr Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka was attended by scores of mourners on Friday.

The commemoration took place one day before the State Funeral in eXesi where president Cyril Ramaphosa is expected to pay tribute to the late luminary.

The former Executive Director of the United Nations Women passed away on Friday, 20 November 2026, at the age of 71, following complications from a medical procedure.

Mlambo-Ngcuka was remembered fondly by religious leaders and liberation stalwarts.

Tributes from the World Council of Churches, the South African Catholic Bishops' Conference mourn the loss of a pioneering leader whose life was an example of service and commitment to social justice.

Archbishop of Cape Town Thabo Makgoba recalled Mlambo-Ngcuka's dedication to the cause of literacy, saying, "Every child who learns to read is one of her tender shoots."

The service was attended by political leaders like Education Minister Siviwe Gwarube and Speaker of the National Assembly Thoko Didiza.

Gwarube and Didiza shared their memories of Dr Mlambo-Ngcuka's support for women in leadership and advocacy for education.

Mlambo-Ngcuka served in several roles of public service including Deputy Minister of Trade and Industry and Minister of Minerals and Energy.

She also founded the Umlambo Foundation to support teachers and pupils.

South Africans and the international community, have been encouraged to write messages of condolence at various locations across the country and at United Nations (UN) offices.

World.title: Door left open for veteran spinner Lyon after axing for New Zealand Tests
World.content:
AUSTRALIA - Australian selectors said they "hope it's not the end" for Nathan Lyon after he was axed Saturday for their four-Test series against New Zealand, leaving the veteran spinner's career in limbo.

Corey Rocchiccioli, who is 10 years younger than the 39-year-old, was preferred instead, one of two debutants in a 13-man squad for the first Test starting at Perth on December 9.

A 14th player will be added following the next round of the domestic Sheffield Shield for a Test that will be the first since the "Sandpapergate" ball-tampering scandal blew up again this month.

With out-of-form Marnus Labuschagne dropped, Queensland batsman Jack Clayton, 27, got the nod to replace him and will likely come in a three, allowing Steve Smith to remain at four.

Clayton has been a form player in the Sheffield Shield and won the race ahead Sam Konstas and Jake Weatherald.

It is the first time Lyon has been left out of an Australian Test squad when fit to play since his debut series in Sri Lanka in 2011.

The sixth leading wicket-taker of all time with 577 from his 145 Tests, Lyon has made no secret of his plans to keep going with tours of India and England in the next nine months.

But he has struggled with form and fitness and chairman of selectors George Bailey said it was difficult phone call telling him was out.

He urged Lyon not to rush any retirement call with a five-Test series in India on spin-friendly tracks in January-February.

"Unfortunately, he just hasn't quite had the impact over the last few games that we would have liked," Bailey told reporters. "We hope it's not the end for him. We see a path. I think he can have enormous value when you project forward to India on a tour like that with his experience. "We wanted him to take some time and not rush into any decision off the back of this."

Rocchiccioli, who has played multiple times for Australia A, leapfrogged Todd Murphy, Matt Kuhnemann and Mitchell Swepson in the pecking order as his replacement.

"Corey has been a strong performer in domestic cricket for the past few seasons and has traits that are well suited to Australian conditions," added Bailey.

Whether he plays remains to be seen with a chance that Australia could go with four seamers on a traditionally bouncy Perth wicket, with Scott Boland alongside Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood.

Clayton's debut is all but locked in after allrounders Cooper Connolly and Beau Webster, who featured in the recent South Africa series, were also left out.

"Jack is a well organised player who has performed consistently for an extended period. His game is well suited to complement the rest of the batting order," said Bailey.

Matt Renshaw and Travis Head look set to remain as openers, with Cameron Green at five, Josh Inglis keeping his place at six and Alex Carey filling out the middle order.

Australia squad: Pat Cummins (capt), Scott Boland, Alex Carey, Jack Clayton, Cameron Green, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Michael Neser, Matthew Renshaw, Corey Rocchiccioli, Steve Smith, Mitchell Starc.

-AFP

World.title: Anger after boy is crushed by truck while cycling in Syokimau
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Syokimau residents are protesting over the state of poor roads in the area. [Newton Kimaiyo, Standard]

Syokimau residents are demanding urgent action to keep heavy commercial trucks off residential roads after a ten-year-old boy was crushed to death while riding his bicycle several meters from their home.

The accident occurred on Friday at around 5.30pm along Chadi Nation Road, near Epco, involving a heavy commercial vehicle at the junction.

The boy who was cycling within his neighbourhood died at the scene, leaving residents devastated and renewing calls for the government to restrict trucks operating along roads in the residential estate.

The tragedy comes barely days after Syokimau residents took to the streets to protest against the use of estate roads by trucks transporting materials from nearby quarries and those evading cess points.

The demonstrations were met with teargas from police to residents but the residents say they will use all legal means to compel relevant authorities to act on their demands to prevent further tragedies.

Speaking at the scene, resident Juliet Karungo said the community had repeatedly warned authorities about the dangers posed by heavy vehicles using roads meant for residential traffic.

"We are in deep pain today. We have been raising concerns about these trucks operating on our estate roads and now a young child has lost his life. As mothers, we have cried. I cannot imagine what the boy's parents are going through," she said.

Engineer Eric Nzola said the tragedy highlighted the urgent need to address road safety challenges in Syokimau and neighbouring estates where residential developments have expanded rapidly.

"The county government of Machakos has let us down high density zones like Syokimau and Katani need to be safer we are calling on the government to have a serious consultative meeting and reroute this tracks that are causing havoc to residents," said Eric.

He also questioned the continued use of the estate roads despite the availability of a designated tarmac route that could serve as an alternative for the trucks.

"By 6am, our children cannot safely walk to school. Even when a school is just one kilometre away, parents would rather use school transport because they fear what could happen along the roads," he said.

The residents appealed to both the national and county governments to intervene urgently and provide alternative routes for heavy commercial vehicles.

The latest fatality has renewed questions about road safety, traffic management and the regulation of heavy commercial vehicles in Syokimau, with residents insisting that protecting lives must take priority over commercial interests.

World.title: Martha Karua: I am running for president in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Martha Karua unveiled her presidential bid under the rallying banner Simama na Mama in Limuru. [Fidelis Kabunyi, Standard]

People’s Liberation Party (PLP) leader Martha Karua has declared her intention to run for president in the 2027 General Election.

Karua, who was the late former Prime Minister Raila Odinga’s running mate in the 2022 elections, has already declared her willingness to work with the United Opposition to field a single presidential candidate against President William Ruto.

Karua opposed attempts by her opposition colleagues to settle on a flag bearer through boardroom negotiations, saying the process should instead involve research that takes the views of ordinary Kenyans into account.

"We can enter a room and pick one of us as the presidential flag bearer only to be rejected by Kenyans at the ballot. That is why we need to conduct research where Kenyans will also give their views on the best candidate," Karua told the gathering at Jumuiya Conference Center, Limuru.

She dismissed claims that the opposition was divided over its plan to field a single presidential candidate.

The meeting brought together more than 5,000 women and supporters from across the country.

Karua pledged to transform the country if she was selected as the United Opposition’s joint presidential candidate.

"I am running for president of the Republic of Kenya in 2027, and I do so with a sense of responsibility and an unwavering belief in the promise of our nation," she told the gathering.

"The road ahead is ours to walk. The future is ours to shape," she added.

Accompanied by her mother, Karua called on women to remain steadfast in their pursuit of leadership. "I walked into this moment hand in hand with my mother, carrying more than the hopes of a personal journey.

I carry the courage of generations of women who came before us, the strength of those who stand with us today, and the promise of those who will come after." She said.

With a campaign slogan dubbed "Simama na Martha" and a movement centred on "One People, One Purpose, One Term", the Iron Lady of Kenyan politics took a swipe at Ruto’s leadership style, describing it as wasteful.

"There is no need for endless trips abroad and countrywide at the expense of working for Kenyans. This is the total waste of state resources that should have been channeled to meaningful use like buying medicine in our hospital and equipping schools, " she said.

She said the presidency was about public trust, not personal privilege.

Karua, who was also accompanied by Nairobi gubernatorial aspirant Margaret Wanjiru, pledged to fight corruption.

"Let us elect leaders who are not after their stomachs. That is why we need an economy that works for everyone and not a chosen few. We also need taxation systems that do not waste," Karua said.

She said her government would reduce unnecessary expenditure and prioritise the completion of ongoing projects before starting new ones.

"We need transparency in all government-funded projects. There is no need to abandon projects every election cycle and begin new ones just because a new MP, MCA or governor has been elected. All pending projects must be completed first," she noted.

On healthcare, Karua said there was an urgent need to equip all county hospitals with cancer detection and screening machines and establish a dependable healthcare system.

She criticised benchmarking trips by the current administration, arguing that resources should instead be invested in purchasing medical equipment.

The event brought together women from diverse backgrounds whose experiences, voices and aspirations, according to the PLP leader, reflected the Kenya they had helped build over the years.

They also sought to discuss the challenges they continue to face and the future they want to shape collectively.

Karua challenged women to vie for elective seats in the upcoming elections.

"I ask Kenyans to give women a chance right from the MCA to national leadership positions.

If there is a woman who is capable just give her the chance. Women are very good managers," Karua said.

"I love this country and I have served this country in the courts, parliament and cabinet where decisions affecting millions are made. I therefore have enough experience to run the affairs of our beloved country"

On education, Karua promised that her government would disburse capitation to schools on time to give head teachers sufficient time to plan. She also pledged to provide free education from primary school to university.

She further promised to end the culture of abductions, which she said was state-sponsored through security agencies.

World.title: Wamalwa ousts Natembeya, Savula as DAP-K deputy leaders
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Democratic Action Party of Kenya (DAP-K) leader Eugene Wamalwa at the party's headquarter in Nairobi on November 26, 2026. [Benard Orwongo, Standard]

Democratic Action Party of Kenya (DAP-K) leader Eugene Wamalwa has removed Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya and Kakamega Deputy Governor Ayub Savula as the party’s deputy leaders, replacing them with Mumias East MP Peter Salasya and former Cabinet Minister Kipruto Arap Kirwa.

The changes, announced on Thursday at the party headquarters, mark a significant reorganisation of DAP-K’s leadership amid growing political differences between Wamalwa and the two ousted officials.

Natembeya’s removal follows months of disagreements with Wamalwa over the party’s leadership, political direction and ambition to expand its national influence.

The governor had in July 2026 declared his intention to leave DAP-K, arguing that he wanted to transform the party into a national political movement. He subsequently pursued political mobilisation through the TAWE Movement, before aligning himself with the Linda Mwananchi Movement.

His political realignment gathered momentum after Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna unveiled him as Chairperson of the movement’s Board of Trustees and head of its presidential campaign ahead of the 2027 General Election.

The appointments were announced on October 30, 2026, during the launch of the movement’s national headquarters in Lavington, Nairobi.

Savula’s exit, on the other hand, follows an earlier political break with Wamalwa that dates back to the November 2025 Malava by-election.

The former Lugari MP openly defied DAP-K by backing United Democratic Alliance (UDA) candidate David Ndakwa against the party’s candidate Seth Panyako. Ndakwa eventually won the seat, exposing divisions within the party’s Western Kenya political base.

On January 6, 2026, Savula publicly declared that he had moved on from DAP-K and intended to work with the government.

He subsequently formally joined UDA in February and declared his interest in the Kakamega gubernatorial seat.

He was later appointed Deputy Coordinator of President William Ruto’s Western Kenya campaign team, while UDA grassroots delegates endorsed him for a deputy party leader position, which he accepted.

The two departures have therefore left DAP-K with the challenge of rebuilding its leadership structure as political realignments gather momentum ahead of the August 2027 General Election.

Wamalwa appeared to take issue with leaders who, despite benefiting from their political parties, engage in activities that undermine the organisations.

"Let them also respect our party because you cannot bite the hand that feeds you. Heshima si utumwa," he said, in an apparent reference to the disagreements surrounding Natembeya’s political engagements.

Wamalwa had previously warned Natembeya to exercise restraint and, if he intended to join another political outfit, leave DAP-K respectfully.

He, however, dismissed suggestions that their differences were personal, maintaining that he had supported the governor’s political journey, including his successful 2022 gubernatorial campaign.

The party leader has also repeatedly called for unity among opposition leaders, warning that internal divisions could undermine efforts to challenge President William Ruto in the 2027 elections.

Beyond the changes involving Natembeya and Savula, Wamalwa said the proposed appointments of Salasya and Kirwa were part of a wider effort to invigorate the party and strengthen its leadership ahead of the polls.

World.title: Wetang'ula orders CCTV review as Sabina Chege renews missing phone
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize
