Logan said these measures are particularly important as Liberia prepares for increased offshore exploration and possible drilling activities.

The strategic plan also places emphasis on transparency and public access to information. The LPRA intends to strengthen the management of petroleum data, establish clear access rules and regularly publish information to help Liberians understand the sector and identify realistic participation opportunities.

As part of its accountability commitments, Logan announced that the Authority will begin publishing an annual State of the Petroleum Sector Report in 2027. The strategic plan will also undergo open reviews in 2028 and 2030 to assess progress and make necessary adjustments.

She cautioned against judging the Authority solely by whether commercial oil discoveries are made, noting that geological outcomes are beyond its control.

“We are optimistic about the future, but do not judge us by whether oil is found; geology is beyond our control,” she said. “Judge us by the quality of the companies we attract and by our readiness to regulate them in the interest of Liberia.”

Meanwhile, the LPRA is expected to break ground for its new headquarters in January 2027. The facility will include a modern petroleum data processing and viewing center to strengthen the Authority’s technical and institutional capabilities.

The strategic plan will be implemented in three phases. The first, covering 2026 and 2027, will focus on establishing the Authority’s operational foundation. The second phase, from 2028 to 2029, will deepen regulatory delivery, while 2030 will focus on consolidating achievements and preparing the next strategic plan.

For his part, Representative Sam P. Jallah, Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Hydrocarbon, described the strategic plan as a policy framework that establishes clear targets and measurable standards for the petroleum regulator.

He said the document sends an important signal to citizens and investors that Liberia is working toward a regulatory environment built on fairness, integrity and forward-looking policies.

“When our regulatory institutions operate with clarity and integrity, investors’ confidence rises, illicit financing declines and the ultimate beneficiaries are the Liberian people,” Jallah said.

He reaffirmed the Legislature’s support for the five-year plan, pledging constructive oversight and legislative and policy support to facilitate its implementation.

Jallah said the Legislature would also hold the LPRA accountable for meeting the benchmarks and commitments outlined in the strategic plan.

Calling on government institutions, development partners, petroleum operators, civil society and the public to hold the Authority accountable, Logan said: “Measure us by what we deliver, not by what we promise.”

She said Liberia’s return to the global petroleum exploration map must be sustained through credible regulation, ethical engagement and responsible management of the country’s petroleum resources.

World.title: Liberia: Senate Probes Liberian Dollar Shortage, Rising Commodity Prices
World.content:
Despite the Liberian Dollar’s Appreciation Against the U.S. Dollar, Consumers Face Rising Prices of Basic Goods, Raising Concerns Over Holiday Spending

Monrovia – The Liberian Senate has mandated its Joint Committees on Banking and Currency and Public Accounts to investigate the reported shortage of Liberian dollar banknotes and the persistent increase in prices of basic commodities, despite the recent appreciation of the local currency against the United States dollar.

By Obediah Johnson

The decision follows growing concerns from commercial banks, business owners and market vendors over the limited availability of Liberian dollar banknotes for everyday transactions.



At the same time, consumers across the country are questioning why the appreciation of the local currency has not translated into lower prices of essential commodities, leaving ordinary Liberians struggling with the high cost of living as the Christmas season approaches.

According to the Central Bank of Liberia (CBL), the exchange rate currently stands at approximately L$163 to US$1.

The Senate’s decision followed concerns raised by River Gee County Senator Jonathan Sogbie during Thursday’s regular session at the Capitol Building on November 26.

In a communication to the Senate, a copy of which is in the possession of FrontPage Africa, Senator Sogbie expressed concern that despite legislative authorization for the Central Bank to procure and print L$79 billion, the country continues to experience a shortage of its own currency.



“I write to bring to the attention of this August Body the growing shortage of Liberian dollar banknotes in our commercial banks and markets across the country,” he stated.

“On July 16, 2026, this Senate unanimously concurred with the House of Representatives to authorize the Central Bank of Liberia (CBL) to procure and print up to L$79 billion. However, Distinguished Colleagues, our people continue to experience an acute shortage of Liberian dollars.”

He further observed that the limited banknotes circulating in the economy are, in many instances, badly mutilated and difficult to use for ordinary transactions.

The senator said the situation is particularly troubling as Liberians approach the festive season, when many households depend on funds from their annual savings clubs, commonly known as Susu, to meet Christmas and other end-of-year expenses.

“How will our people access their money when Liberian dollars are hardly available in the banks and markets? If our own currency is missing from our country, where do we go to find it?” he questioned.

Prices Remain High Despite Currency Appreciation

Senator Sogbie also raised concerns about the disconnect between the declining exchange rate and the prices of goods and services on the local market.

He argued that although the exchange rate between the United States and Liberian dollars has improved, consumers are yet to experience corresponding reductions in the prices of basic commodities.

According to him, the continued high cost of essential goods is placing an additional burden on ordinary Liberians, particularly households already struggling to meet their daily needs.

He questioned why the appreciation of the local currency has not translated into more affordable prices at marketplaces and called for an explanation from the relevant monetary authorities.

Senate Wants Answers From CBL

As part of his communication, Senator Sogbie requested the Senate to invite the Governor of the Central Bank of Liberia and other relevant officials to provide explanations for the reported shortage of Liberian dollar banknotes.

He wants the CBL authorities to provide an update on the progress made toward the procurement and printing of the L$79 billion authorized by the Legislature.

The senator also wants the bank to explain the delay in making new banknotes available to the public and address the apparent disconnect between the appreciation of the local currency and the persistent high prices of commodities.

He maintained that Liberians deserve clear answers and relief, stressing that the Senate must exercise its constitutional oversight responsibilities to ensure that the concerns receive urgent attention.

Senator Warns of Possible Festive Season Chaos

Speaking in a brief interview with FrontPage Africa at his Capitol Building office in Monrovia, Senator Sogbie warned that the continued shortage of Liberian dollar banknotes could trigger tensions and instability in communities across the country if the situation is not addressed.

He expressed particular concern about the potential difficulties facing leaders of annual savings clubs, who are expected to distribute accumulated contributions to their members during the festive season.

The senator fears that delays by commercial banks in releasing deposited funds could expose savings club leaders to embarrassment, confrontations and possible attacks from frustrated members.

He said the improvement in the exchange rate has yet to produce meaningful benefits for consumers in terms of purchasing power, especially during the festive season.

“The exchange rate has no positive effect on our people in terms of purchasing power, especially when they are in the festive season. Our people are expected to share their yearly Susu this December, and with the high mutilated bills and shortage of the Liberian dollars, we don’t know how they are going to do it, and I don’t foresee that happening anytime soon,” he said.

Senator Sogbie also pointed to difficulties reportedly being experienced by importers in clearing their goods from the Freeport of Monrovia, warning that the situation could worsen if consumers are unable to access local currency to purchase essential commodities.

He argued that electronic transactions cannot entirely replace physical banknotes, particularly given the country’s continued reliance on cash for everyday commercial activities.

Calling for immediate intervention, the senator invoked a popular Liberian saying about the Christmas season.

“There is a common saying in Liberia that ‘when the Christmas will be good, you will know from the eve,’ and this eve doesn’t look good. Let’s not wait to celebrate the eve only to have a bad Christmas. Let us solve the problem (of scarcity of Liberian dollars and hike in prices of commodities) now; it is a local problem,” he warned.

He held the Central Bank and other relevant authorities responsible for addressing the shortage of local currency and the continued increase in commodity prices.

Savings Clubs Face Uncertainty

Meanwhile, concerns are mounting among leaders of annual savings clubs across the country over reported delays by commercial banks in releasing members’ deposits.

Commercial banks are reportedly limiting the disbursement of large amounts of Liberian dollars to individuals and organizations amid the scarcity of local banknotes.

The situation has raised fears among savings club organizers, many of whom depend on commercial banks to safeguard members’ contributions before distributing the funds at the end of each savings cycle.

For thousands of participants, the annual distribution provides an important source of money for purchasing food, clothing, paying school-related expenses and meeting other family obligations during the Christmas season.

Economic observers warn that if the situation persists, households and small businesses could face additional financial difficulties during one of the country’s busiest commercial periods.

With the Senate now moving to investigate the matter, attention is expected to turn to the Central Bank’s explanation of the banknote shortage, the status of the authorized L$79 billion printing exercise and the factors preventing currency appreciation from translating into lower consumer prices.

For many Liberians, the immediate concern is whether they will be able to access their savings and afford basic commodities as Christmas approaches.

World.title: Liberia: PPCC Boss Bodger Scott Johnson Honored for Procurement Reforms
World.content:
Citation credits him with new procurement law, US$120m in e-procurement contracts

MONROVIA – Bodger Scott Johnson, Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Public Procurement and Concessions Commission (PPCC), has been honored as a distinguished public sector reformer for his role in modernizing Liberia’s public procurement system.

A citation accompanying the recognition credits Johnson with spearheading reforms aimed at strengthening transparency, accountability and efficiency in government procurement, including the amendment of the country’s procurement law, the introduction of electronic government procurement and expanded opportunities for women-owned and Liberian businesses.

The recognition highlights three major areas of reform under his leadership: the enactment of a revised Public Procurement and Concessions Act, the expansion of the national Electronic Government Procurement (e-GP) system and institutional improvements within the Commission.



New Procurement Law

The citation identifies the review and amendment of the Public Procurement and Concessions Act as one of the most significant milestones of Johnson’s tenure.

The Act for the Amendment and Restatement of the Public Procurement and Concessions Act was approved on January 12, 2026, while the PPCC subsequently issued and published amended regulations on March 18, 2026.

Among other provisions, the revised legal framework requires government institutions to conduct procurement through an electronic system and introduces provisions on sustainable and gender-responsive procurement, as well as public-private partnerships.



The law also formally recognizes procurement as a professional discipline, establishing qualifications, certification requirements and career development pathways for procurement officers across the civil service.

The reforms are intended to strengthen the professional capacity of procurement personnel while improving compliance with established procurement standards.

US$120 Million in E-Procurement Contracts

Another major achievement highlighted in the citation is the introduction and expansion of Liberia’s Electronic Government Procurement (e-GP) system, which it describes as the most visible expression of Johnson’s reform agenda.

The system was initially piloted in six institutions: the Ministries of Finance, Health, Public Works and Education, the Liberia Revenue Authority and the PPCC.

It has since expanded in phases, providing an electronic platform for the major stages of public procurement, including procurement planning, bid submission, bid opening, evaluation, contract awards and contract management.

By digitizing these processes, the system creates an electronic audit trail that allows procurement activities to be tracked and reviewed, potentially reducing opportunities for manipulation and improving accountability.

According to the citation, more than US$120 million in government contracts has been awarded through the platform since its introduction.

Approximately 18 percent of those contracts reportedly went to women-owned businesses, reflecting efforts to expand participation in public procurement.

The citation also credits the PPCC with training more than 1,300 vendors between 2024 and 2026 in bid preparation, the use of the electronic procurement platform and procedures for filing procurement complaints.

Liberia’s e-procurement reforms have also attracted regional attention, with procurement officials from neighboring countries reportedly visiting to learn from the country’s experience. The Commission has specifically reported a study visit by a procurement delegation from Sierra Leone.

Institutional Reforms at PPCC

Beyond changes to the legal and technological framework, the citation highlights improvements to the Commission’s internal operations under Johnson’s leadership.

Before becoming Executive Director, Johnson served as Chairman of the PPCC Board of Commissioners.

Since assuming the executive position, he has overseen the renovation of the Commission’s offices, installation of dedicated e-procurement workstations and construction of a 200-seat training hall.

Other initiatives include the establishment of a procurement clinic designed to provide technical assistance to procurement officers and suppliers, alongside increased targeted and random compliance inspections of government institutions.

The compliance exercises are intended not only to identify procurement violations but also to assess institutional weaknesses and recommend corrective measures.

The citation further recognizes Johnson’s efforts to improve staff welfare, logistics and working conditions within the Commission.

Johnson holds a Master of Arts degree in Public Administration from Howard University in the United States.

Liberia’s Role in Africa’s Procurement Network

The recognition also comes as Liberia continues to engage with regional and continental efforts to strengthen public procurement governance.

Through the PPCC, Liberia participates in the African Public Procurement Network (APPN), also known by its French acronym, RACOP.

Established in 2018 in Lomé, Togo, the network brings together public procurement authorities across Africa to promote cooperation, professional development, transparency and the exchange of best practices.

The APPN provides a platform for procurement institutions to share experiences in electronic procurement, sustainable purchasing, professionalization and measures to combat corruption.

Its activities also support efforts to improve the compatibility of procurement systems across African countries, potentially making it easier for businesses to participate in procurement opportunities across the continent.

The network operates through a General Assembly, an Executive Committee, a Technical Secretariat based in Lomé and five subregional networks covering North, East, West, Central and Southern Africa.

For Liberia, participation provides opportunities for the PPCC to learn from procurement reforms implemented elsewhere while contributing its own experiences to regional discussions.

The Accountability Test

Despite the reforms highlighted in the citation, public procurement remains a critical governance issue in Liberia, where substantial portions of government expenditure pass through procurement processes.

The transition from manual to electronic procurement is widely viewed as an important step toward reducing opportunities for corruption, improving competition and strengthening public oversight.

The PPCC’s commitments under the Open Government Partnership have also identified corruption risks associated with manual procurement processes, with electronic procurement presented as one of the mechanisms for addressing those vulnerabilities.

However, the long-term success of the reforms will depend on their consistent application across government institutions, effective enforcement of procurement regulations and public access to information about government contracts.

Citizens, civil society organizations and oversight institutions will also need access to contract information to determine which companies are receiving public contracts, the value of those contracts and whether the goods, services and infrastructure being procured are delivered as agreed.

For Johnson and the PPCC, the challenge ahead will be to translate the reforms and institutional improvements highlighted in the citation into measurable improvements in public spending, competition and value for money.

World.title: Liberia: Agriculture Minister, EPA Boss Warn of Food Production Decline Under Potential El Niño
World.content:
Capitol Building – The El Niño phenomenon poses a significant threat to Liberia’s agricultural sector by disrupting traditional planting schedules and causing erratic weather patterns, including extreme droughts and heavy downpours, Agriculture Minister Dr. J. Alexander Nuetah and Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Executive Director Dr. Emmanuel Urey Yarkpawolo have warned.

By Emmanuel Weedee-Conway

El Niño, a global climate phenomenon, is driving increasingly unstable weather patterns characterized by severe droughts, intense heat waves and sudden flooding across various African regions. In Liberia, several counties are reportedly experiencing severe dryness, threatening agricultural production, food security and crop yields.



Appearing before the House of Representatives during the 13th day sitting of the Third Quarter of the Third Session of the 55th Legislature, both officials warned that the potential phenomenon could significantly affect food production, emphasizing the need for urgent measures.

Impact of El Niño on Liberia’s Cropping System

Minister Nuetah told Plenary that El Niño could disrupt Liberia’s established cropping calendar, which determines when farmers should begin planting across different regions.

He explained that if farmers plant in March in anticipation of rainfall but the rains fail because of El Niño, their crops could be destroyed. Similarly, excessive rainfall could cause seeds to rot in the soil before germinating.



He also warned that prolonged sunshine and intense heat could prevent seeds from germinating and encourage the proliferation of insects and pests.

“The intensity of the heat could also encourage the proliferation of insects and pests. These pests will not only affect crops but could also threaten other forms of life in our communities, including livestock,” the Minister asserted.

Shortened Growing Seasons and Crop Losses

Another possible impact is a shortened growing season, which could affect rice production.

Liberia has rice varieties that mature within 90 days, while others require as long as 150 days.

Minister Nuetah explained that farmers planting varieties requiring 150 days to mature depend on sufficient rainfall throughout the growing period. However, if the rainy season becomes shorter, rice plants could fail to produce grains during the booting and flowering stages because of insufficient water.

This could result in empty rice panicles and little or no harvest.

“When this happens, food insecurity could become a serious concern in communities and counties that depend heavily on rice production. In some areas, we could also experience flooding because rainfall may exceed the expected intensity. For instance, farmers who have already planted swamp rice could experience flooding when excessive rainfall occurs, potentially submerging and destroying their crops.”

He warned that severe El Niño conditions could cause rice yields to decline by approximately 30 to 50 percent for crops planted during the affected period, threatening food security, particularly in rural communities dependent on rice farming.

Effects on Cassava, Maize, and Vegetables

The Agriculture Minister said cassava, maize and vegetables could also be affected.

He pointed out that excessive rainfall could cause planted cassava stems to rot before germinating, while insufficient rainfall and intense heat could damage vegetables and increase pest attacks.

“For example, when farmers cultivate pepper and rainfall becomes insufficient, the crops may suffer even when farmers attempt to provide additional water. Due to the intensity of the heat, pest attacks could increase, causing significant damage to the crops.”

He emphasized that El Niño could have serious implications for Liberia if appropriate measures were not taken.

Implications for Rice Imports and Food Prices

Minister Nuetah caveated that the consequences could extend beyond domestic agricultural production, particularly if major rice-producing countries were also affected.

“Liberia is a rice-consuming country, and we import more than 60 percent of the rice consumed locally. If El Niño severely affects agricultural production in Asia and other major rice-producing countries, we should expect a reduction in rice supplies and potentially higher rice prices in Liberia.”

He intoned that Liberia’s dependence on imported rice makes the country vulnerable to disruptions in international food production and supply chains.

He also warned that farmers could lose their seeds when crops fail because of unfavorable weather conditions, leaving them without planting materials for subsequent farming seasons.

Consequently, the Agriculture Minister asserted the government would need to provide replacement seeds to affected farmers.

“We could also experience further food shortages in communities and across the country if the phenomenon severely affects major food-producing countries around the world. Because Liberia depends significantly on food imports, limited international supplies could lead to increased prices.”

The Way Forward

To address the potential impact of El Niño, Minister Nuetah outlined five major intervention areas.

Pillar One: Strengthening Early Warning Systems

The first recommendation focuses on strengthening early warning systems and providing timely information to farming communities.

He proposed establishing a national task force comprising the Ministry of Agriculture, Liberia Meteorological Service, Ministry of Transport, Central Agricultural Research Institute (CARI), National Disaster Management Agency (NDMA), Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), World Food Programme (WFP) and EPA.

The task force, he said, would meet weekly to monitor developments and provide updates on the phenomenon.

He also recommended regular agro-meteorological bulletins and timely planting advisories to guide farmers on appropriate planting periods.

Although Liberia already has a cropping calendar, he noted that changing climatic conditions could disrupt established planting schedules, requiring farmers to receive updated information and guidance.

Pillar Two: Building a Resilient Seed and Crop System

The second pillar recommends developing a resilient seed and crop production system to minimize the effects of El Niño.

Minister Nuetah called for a gradual shift from long-duration crop varieties, particularly rice, to varieties that mature within approximately 90 days.

He identified NERICA 4 and NERICA 14 as suitable rice varieties for upland cultivation and recommended improving farmers’ access to varieties that mature within 90 to 100 days, including a new variety known as C2.

For cassava production, he urged the country to prioritize drought-resistant varieties to help farmers maintain expected harvests during periods of high temperatures and insufficient rainfall.

Pillar Three: Expanding Irrigation and Water-Harvesting Systems

The Minister called for increased support for smallholder farmers through expanded access to irrigation facilities, including solar-powered irrigation systems and boreholes capable of supplying water to farming communities and households.

He also recommended investing in water-harvesting technologies to ensure water availability during the dry season.

“We need to develop a strategy that will enable the government to invest in water-harvesting technologies. Such investments will help us manage water resources more effectively and support agricultural production over the coming years.”

Pillar Four: Promoting Climate-Smart Agricultural Practices

The fourth pillar focuses on training at least 100,000 farmers in improved farming techniques, including mulching, which helps conserve soil moisture.

He also recommended training farmers in intercropping, the cultivation of different crops on the same land, and conservation agriculture, particularly minimum tillage, to protect soil structure and productivity.

Pillar Five: Strengthening Pest and Livestock Disease Prevention

The fifth pillar emphasizes strengthening pest surveillance and preventing livestock diseases across the country.

“The Ministry of Agriculture and the Central Agricultural Research Institute have technicians with the capacity to conduct surveillance activities across the counties to identify areas where disease outbreaks are likely to occur,” he said.

Financial Requirements and Implementation

Minister Nuetah estimated that approximately US$25 million to US$35 million would be required to implement the proposed interventions.

He accentuated that the funding would support agricultural production across approximately 25,000 hectares of lowland areas, strengthen farmers’ technical capacity and provide education on the phenomenon and measures to minimize its effects.

EPA Warns of Increasingly Severe Conditions

For his part, EPA Executive Director Emmanuel Urey Yarkpawolo informed the body that the El Niño phenomenon was occurring more frequently, with increasingly severe impacts.

He attributed the situation partly to climate change, noting that rising ocean temperatures were contributing to unstable environmental conditions.

Dr. Yarkpawolo recalled that early this year, the EPA began tracking developments using satellite technology provided by the United States. The agency has also established a website to monitor daily wind movements and other weather-related developments.

He explained that some parts of the world were experiencing increasing dryness and heat waves, while others faced heavier rainfall, sometimes followed by prolonged drought.

Climate Conditions in Liberia

Turning to Liberia, Yarkpawolo disclosed that EPA monitoring conducted between November 1 and November 10 and 12 revealed significant dry conditions across the country.

He revealed that 14 counties were experiencing severe dryness, with Lofa County appearing to be the only exception.

According to the EPA’s findings, Sinoe County recorded the highest level of dryness at 71 percent, followed by Grand Kru at 38.5 percent, Grand Gedeh at 37.5 percent, Grand Bassa at 36.8 percent, River Cess at 36.4 percent and River Gee at 33.3 percent. Maryland was also among the affected counties.

He further disclosed that approximately 1.17 million people across the seven heavily affected counties were exposed to these conditions, based on the 2022 national census figures.

Yarkpawolo also warned that prolonged heat and dry conditions could expose agricultural areas to increased heat stress, negatively affecting crop production and farming livelihoods.

EPA’s Early Warning and Public Awareness Measures

The EPA Executive Director said the agency had established an early warning system and a dedicated website to monitor environmental developments.

He also disclosed that the agency had developed public awareness messages, including jingles in simple Liberian English, to help citizens understand the prevailing conditions and potential risks.

“Additionally, we are issuing press statements and making radio announcements to inform the public about the prevailing conditions and the possible consequences. Our responsibility at the EPA is to protect the environment and inform the public about developments affecting it. As part of that mandate, we monitor emerging environmental threats, issue early warnings, and provide information to the government and the country as a whole,” Yarkpawolo stated.

House Decision

Following presentations by Minister Nuetah, EPA Executive Director Yarkpawolo, an official from the Meteorological Department of the Ministry of Transport and NDMA Executive Director Ansu Dorley, Plenary instructed its Committees on Agriculture, Lands and Environment to investigate the matter and report with possible recommendations within two weeks.

World.title: Liberia: C190 Coalition Engages House on Ratification of ILO Convention Against Workplace Harassment
World.content:
MONROVIA – A coalition of nine trade unions, civil society organizations and government institutions has called on the Government of Liberia to ratify and implement the International Labor Organization (ILO) Convention 190 (C190), aimed at ending violence and harassment in workplaces.

By Emmanuel Weedee-Conway

In a formal petition submitted to the House of Representatives on Thursday, November 26, the Coalition for the Ratification of ILO Convention 190 Liberia urged lawmakers to take legislative steps toward the adoption of the convention, which recognizes everyone’s right to a world of work free from violence and harassment.



The coalition said workers across Liberia, particularly women, marginalized groups and people engaged in vulnerable forms of employment, continue to experience sexual harassment, intimidation, threats, bullying, exploitation and other forms of workplace abuse.

The group noted that ILO Convention 190, adopted in 2019, together with Recommendation 206, provides an international framework for preventing and addressing violence and harassment across workplaces and work-related environments.

To demonstrate the magnitude of the problem, the coalition referenced findings from national and international reports documenting persistent gender-based violence and harassment in Liberia.

The C190 Coalition also pointed to a January 2026 legal analysis by the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), which highlighted the discrimination, harassment, sexual abuse and exploitation faced by women working in the informal sector, particularly market vendors and domestic workers, who often have limited access to legal protection.



It also cited an August 2025 OHCHR compilation of United Nations information for Liberia’s Universal Periodic Review, which documented 3,204 reported cases of gender-based violence in 2023 and called for stronger measures against gender discrimination, sexual harassment and gender-based violence in workplaces.

Additionally, the coalition referenced a 2025 Afrobarometer survey indicating that 36 percent of Liberians surveyed believe women often or always experience sexual harassment in public spaces, including markets, streets and public transportation.

Citing figures from the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection reported by the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), the coalition said Liberia recorded 3,381 cases of gender-based violence in 2024, with women and girls accounting for approximately 85 percent of survivors.

The coalition clarified that the figures reflect the broader national gender-based violence situation and are not exclusively workplace-related incidents.

It pointed out that consultations with workers across different sectors had revealed concerns about sexual harassment, unwanted physical contact and sexual demands linked to employment.

The coalition further identified underreporting as a major challenge, explaining that many survivors remain silent because of fear of dismissal, retaliation, stigma and discrimination.

“Limited awareness of what constitutes GBVH, coupled with a lack of safe and confidential reporting channels, further discourages survivors from speaking out. As a result, many forms of harassment remain normalized or overlooked in workplaces and society.These challenges underscore the need for stronger laws and policies, safe reporting mechanisms, protection against retaliation, access to support services, and effective accountability measures,” read the petition.

Against this backdrop, the coalition argued that ratifying Convention 190 would provide Liberia an opportunity to strengthen its legal and institutional frameworks, improve worker protection and ensure accountability for acts of violence and harassment.

As part of its recommendations, the coalition called on the House of Representatives to refer its communication to the appropriate legislative committees, particularly those responsible for labor, human rights and gender equality, while transmitting it to the Executive Branch for review and appropriate action.

The Coalition also urged lawmakers to support the ratification of the convention and consider adopting a resolution expressing the Legislature’s commitment to its implementation.

The group further recommended the initiation of a national tripartite dialogue involving the Government, employers, workers’ organizations and civil society to develop a roadmap for ratification and implementation.

Other recommendations include revision and strengthening national laws and policies to address workplace violence in both formal and informal employment, establishing confidential reporting mechanisms, protecting survivors against retaliation and ensuring accountability for perpetrators.

The coalition also called for increased investment in public education, awareness campaigns and data collection to improve prevention, monitoring and responses to workplace violence and harassment.

The Coalition for the Ratification of C190 Liberia comprises the Solidarity Center, United Worker Union of Liberia, Federation of Informal Workers of Liberia, WONGOSOL, BLESSING-Liberia, Health Education and Sustainable Empowerment, Inclusive Development Initiative and the National Parent Teacher Association of Liberia.

The Ministry of Labor and the National Commission on Persons with Disabilities are listed as honorary members supporting the promotion of decent work and safe, violence-free workplaces.

Among other things, the coalition urged the Government to take concrete steps toward ratifying and implementing Convention 190, emphasizing the need to protect the rights, dignity and safety of all workers in Liberia.

Receiving the petition, the Chairperson of the House Committee on Claims and Petitions, Montserrado County Electoral District #8 Representative, Prince A. Toles, promised to transmit the document to plenary for onward discussion on the matter.

“I want to thank you for assembling here in a more peaceful manner to put forth you issue. I can promise you that having received this, I will put it on the floor of plenary and this will form part of our discussion next Tuesday,” Rep. Toles assured the petitioners.

World.title: Seven nabbed in sugar theft case
World.content:
Police in Kalulushi have apprehended seven suspects along the Kalulushi-Sabina Road for allegedly stealing 50-kilogram bags of sugar that were being transported from Ndola to Kipushi.

Copperbelt Police Chief Edwin Kaluba confirmed the development to the media.

Mr Kaluba told the media in an interview that thieves took advantage of the accident involving a Volvo truck which was carrying the consignment.

He said the incident occurred on November 25, 2026 at around 01::00 hours and was reported the same day at 02:00 hours.

He said police conducted an operation yesterday and they managed to recover about 140 X 50kg bags, 07 X 90kg bags and about 14 reparked 50 and 25 kg bags of sugar value not yet ascertained.

He identified the seven as Seven (7) suspects as Innocent Mwamba aged 60 of farm number 375 Bwafwano, Davies Mkandawire aged 59 of house number 1404 Kitwe ,Mary Kunda aged 45 of house number 35/06 Kitwe West.

Mr Kaluba said the others are John Langani aged 32 of house number E248 Chibote, Enoch Zimba aged 35 of Garnarton Kitwe,

Deliveries Nkandu aged 30 of house number 540 Kitwe west and Moses Mulenga aged 22 of house number 281 Chibuluma.

He said they are in custody and will appear in court soon.

World.title: Police in Lundazi hunt for defiler
World.content:
Police in Lundazi have launched a manhunt for a 31-year-old man who is alleged to have defiled his nine (9) year old sister-in-law in Lundazi’s Chipyola Compound.

The minor was being kept by the suspect who happened to be the husband to the victim’s sister.

The incident happened on November 22, 2026 around night time.

Eastern Province Police Commissioner, Robertson Mweemba has confirmed the matter.

It is alleged that the suspect woke up in the night under the pretext of wanting to drink water and went to the kitchen where the minor was sleeping.

“The suspect left his bedroom and went to the kitchen where water was kept, the same place where the girl was sleeping and promised to buy her a drink before defiling her,” Mr Mweemba said.

Police say the suspect again returned to the kitchen, promising to give the girl a K5 if she did not disclose it to anyone and proceeded to having carnal knowledge of her.

It was when the sister to the girl discovered a white discharge coming from her private parts the following morning, when she was bathing her, the matter came to light and was reported to the police

“No arrest has been made as the suspect is on the run,” Police say.

World.title: Farmers in Lusangazi told to preserve livestock pasture
World.content:
Farmers in Lusangazi District have been urged to establish and preserve livestock pasture to protect their animals from potential feed shortages that may arise due to El Niño weather conditions.

District Fisheries and Livestock Coordinator Bridget Mulenga says farmers should take advantage of the pasture distribution programme to improve feed availability and prepare for changing weather patterns.

Ms Mulenga said climate change, coupled with increasing pressure on land from cultivation and human settlements, was reducing grazing space and making it necessary for farmers to plan alternative sources of animal feed.

She said farmers should establish pasture early and preserve surplus feed for use during the dry season when natural grazing becomes limited.

“Climate change is affecting our seasons and the way we farm. At the same time, land is being used for cultivation and homes, which can leave livestock with less grazing and feed. We need to plan ahead and establish pastures so that feed is available when animals need it,” Ms Mulenga said.

She encouraged farmers receiving pasture and forage seed to understand the different varieties, their establishment requirements and benefits to livestock production.

Ms Mulenga cited velvet bean as one of the forage options discussed with farmers and urged community livestock facilitators to share the knowledge with other farmers.

She further cautioned farmers against neglecting animal feeding, saying poor preparation could leave livestock vulnerable to weakness, illness and death.

“We should also help farmers see the value of keeping different types of livestock and engaging in fish farming. Livelihoods may include cattle, goats, poultry, pigs and fish,” she said.

Meanwhile, District Fisheries and Livestock Officer Brian Hapeya said proper pasture establishment, harvesting and storage were important measures in helping farmers maintain livestock condition during periods of inadequate rainfall.

Mr Hapeya said good feeding practices also helped animals maintain their condition and withstand illness.

He urged farmers to make productive use of the distributed pasture and share the knowledge with other livestock keepers in their communities.

Headman Masili, whose name is Jonathan Tembo, called on farmers to complement the distribution exercise by ensuring their animals had adequate feed and water, particularly during the dry season.

He said community leaders and farmers should work together to translate the knowledge received into practical livestock management activities.

World.title: Chaplaincy key for peace and security – IG
World.content:
Inspector General of Police, Graphel Musamba says collaboration between law enforcement alongside defence and security chaplaincies is key in enhancing the peace and security of the nation.

Mr Musamba says partnerships reaffirm the shared commitment to the spiritual and moral well being of personnel, recognising that national security is a collective responsibility that requires unity of purpose and coordinated effort.

Speaking in Lusaka yesterday during the induction ceremony of 68 chaplains drawn from the Zambia Police Service and Special Division, he said such partnership reflects effective teamwork among Government security institutions.

Mr Musamba said chaplaincy plays a vital role in assisting command structures through moral guidance.

The Inspector General described the induction which was done collectively with defence and security as an important milestone in efforts to strengthen spiritual functions in the Police Service.

Mr Musamba said spiritual and moral development remains an essential pillar of the Zambia Police Service

“My office recognizes that the effectiveness of our offices is not measured by their physical fitness, professional knowledge or operational competence. It is equally determined by their character, values, emotional well-being and sense of purpose,” he said.

Speaking at the same event, Zambia Army, Director General for Religious and Moral Services, Brigadier General Shadreck Mwale urged the inductees to practice what they preach by holding on to high moral standards.

General Mwale said the chaplains should have characters that be fit their calling stating that their moral fiber should make a difference in society.

He urged them to be composed and have control over their emotions as they discharge their duties.

“If you are to stand on firm ground as a man or God you must have control over your emotions. Many have failed because their emotions have controlled them,” General Mwale said.

And Zambia Police Service, Head of Chaplaincy, Kondwelani Sakala said chaplaincy goes beyond just conducting church services but is about having an impact in the lives of officers.

Archbishop Sakala said chaplains owe their responsibility to men and women in uniform.

“It is about being present in the lives of our officers and their families; providing spiritual guidance, counselling, encouragement and moral direction, especially during moments of difficulty, loss and uncertainty. We are called to care for the people behind the uniform,” he said.

The Theme for the induction ceremony which was inspired by Acts 20:28 is dubbed: “Shepherds in Uniform: Called to Watch Over God’s Flock.”

World.title: Two SOTTI graduates earn scholarships to China
World.content:
Two former students of Solwezi Trades Training Institute (SOTTI) have been awarded Chinese government scholarships to undertake a one-year specialised training programme in Computer Numerical Control (CNC) machines at Tianjin Light Industrial Vocational Technical College in China.

The beneficiaries, Oscar Mwansa and Grace Chinjenge, both graduates in Heavy Equipment Engineering, are expected to acquire advanced skills in electric vehicle maintenance and Artificial Intelligence (AI), which will enhance their technical expertise and contribute to Zambia’s growing technological needs.

SOTTI Principal Ethel Mbewe says the sponsorship demonstrates the continued commitment of the Chinese government to promoting international educational cooperation and strengthening technical and vocational skills development.

In a telephone interview with the Zambia News and Information Services (ZANIS), Ms Mbewe said the partnership between SOTTI and Tianjin Light Industrial Vocational Technical College has continued to produce positive results since its establishment.

She disclosed that six SOTTI students have so far benefited from the sponsorship programme, with four having graduated and two others expected to complete their studies in September 2027.

Ms Mbewe said the partnership also extends to capacity building for instructors, noting that in May 2026, 20 lecturers and 10 students from SOTTI underwent training in the effective application of Artificial Intelligence at the Chinese institution.

She emphasised that investing in instructors has a multiplier effect on skills development, as trained lecturers are able to transfer specialised knowledge to generations of students.

“through technical attachments, instructor exchanges and specialised competency-based training, SOTTI faculty members would be better positioned to impart advanced skills to more than 100 learners annually”, she said.

Meanwhile, scholarship beneficiary Grace Chinjenge has expressed gratitude for the opportunity, pledging to work hard and make the most of the training programme.

Ms Chinjenge said she would share the knowledge and experience gained in China upon her return to Zambia, while promoting cultural exchange and mutual understanding with fellow students.

She expressed confidence that the programme would lay a strong foundation for her professional development and contribute to strengthening relations between Zambia and China.

World.title: Extend prosecution, arrests of GBV cases suspects beyond the perpetrator
World.content:
A local NGO in Mwinilunga 𝙳district of North-western province says prosecution of Gender Based Violence (GBV) cases should not only concentrate on the perpetrator but must extend to everyone directly or indirectly involved.

Safrina Foundation says the fight against gender-based violence is affected when law enforcement and prosecution largely focuses on the perpetrator leaving behind people who may have either aided the crime, shielded the perpetrator or those attempting to have the matters withdrawn.

Executive Director Credy Aloyo told the media in an interview 𝚝𝚘𝚍𝚊𝚢 that a number of GBV cases are only reported when the perpetrator, the victim and their relatives fail to cover the offense as result of settlement differences on matters which must only be settled in the courts of law.

Ms Aloyo said that it is therefore critical that charges are placed and arrests effected on both the perpetrator and everyone who is involved stating that this would be a more effective way in deterring would be offenders.

She said as the globe observes 16 days of activism against Gender Based Violence, stakeholders must move away from addressing GBV issues from roundtable discussions and meetings and take practical steps in sealing existing gaps that still give room to criminals to perpetuate their acts of violence against women and girls.

“Arresting and prosecuting all those involved directly or indirectly in GBV cases will send a strong signal in communities and people will be afraid to associate themselves with any GBV cases as people will be aware that they will be picked up as accomplices” Said Ms Aloyo.

She urged the prosecution and the judicial system in general to adopt strategies and evidence gathering mechanisms that will secure convictions particularly in GBV cases involving high profile and influential people.

Ms Aloyo explained that measures must equally be put in place to prevent the ability by high profile and influential people with the financial muscle to Buy-Off the victims, witnesses and in some cases members of the prosecution with the aim of tempering and compromising evidence against them.

Meanwhile Ms Aloyo has encouraged actors in the fight against gender-based violence and violence against women and girls to coordinate, combine resources and support each other if the battle against this vice should be won.

She has further called for provision of adequate facilities that provide safety and confidentiality for victims of Gender Based Violence and implementation of empowerment programs which are critical in reducing the vulnerability of women and girls.

“You see girls and women must be economically empowered, they also must be empowered with knowledge and education, which is key in reducing their vulnerability to issues such as Gender Based Violence” she said.

The 2026, 16 days of activism against gender-based violence running from 25th November to 10th December is being observed under the theme; “Unite to End Violence Against Women and Girls: Ensure Justice, Protect Survivors, End Impunity”.

World.title: Two family members found with a case to answer
World.content:
The Zambezi Magistrate Court has found two family members, Maureen Kambazhi and Precious Kambazhi with a case to answer in the ongoing indecent assault trial involving a young girl.

Delivering the ruling yesterday 27th November, Magistrate Shila Mweene placed the duo on their defence after the prosecution closed its case, stating that a prima facie case had been established against them.

Maureen Kambazhi and Precious Kambazhi are jointly charged with indecent assault on a female, contrary to Section 137(1) of the Penal Code, Chapter 87 of the Laws of Zambia.

Particulars of the offence are that between September 29 and September 30, 2025, in Zambezi District, the two accused persons, while acting together with other persons unknown, unlawfully and indecently assaulted the young girl by stripping her naked, tying her hands and legs, and pouring water into her private parts.

The case, which sparked widespread public outrage after a video of the incident circulated on social media last year, stems from a dispute over an alleged K1,067 cash shortfall at a bar owned by one of the accused, where the victim worked.

Both accused had previously pleaded not guilty when they first appeared before the court in December 2025.

Following ruling, Magistrate Mweene adjourned the matter to November 28, 2026, for mention, and set January 29, 2027, for the accused persons to open their defence.

World.title: Traditional leaders elated with World Bank project
World.content:
The traditional leadership and the government in Kaoma District have welcomed the World Bank’s Climate Risk and Vulnerability assessment for the Adaptation project in the Refugee camp and host communities.

The program being funded by the World Bank seeks to establish climate Vulnerability gaps in refugee settlements and host communities in order to protect the environment and enhance development.

The team stressed the Bank’s long-term partnership with the government in implementing various infrastructure development projects which include road construction, schools, health facilities as well as climate change resilient programs in refugee resettlements and host communities in the country.

This was disclosed during a courtesy call paid on Kaoma District Commissioner Kashina Sheba and the traditional leadership at both Barotse Royal Establishment’s Naliele palace and Lukena palace of the Nkoya Royal Establishment, by a team of climate change technocrats and consultants from the World Bank led by the Lead Consultant Professor Felix Kalaba.

“The Bank has been an important cooperating partner in the Republic of Zambia in matters of development such as infrastructure of roads, schools, clinics and hospitals. And now the idea is what are the gaps that exist in the systems of governance, to help the refugees and host communities to collectively work together to protect the environment especially on climate change impact challenges”, he said.

During the courtesy calls at both palaces, Prof Kalaba recognised the vital role played by traditional leaders in enhancing development in their chiefdoms including in the fight against climate change hence the need for concerted efforts to ensure a well-protected environment against degradation and high climate change impacts such as droughts and floods.

He thanked the royal establishments for their parental care, support, love and mutual relationship with the displaced people in the district.

“The Bank appreciates the role of traditional leaders in delivering development and this is why we said we are not just going to end with the government systems. And we will appreciate your feedback on how you see the refugees and host communities, to get your views on how your people have been impacted by climate change and some of the things that need to be done to address these challenges”, Prof. Kalaba noted.

Barotse Royal Establishment Induna Yutanga Akalemwa Mukelabai welcomed and commended the World Bank for the good and timely Initiative when the country is impacted by climate change with the El Nino being experienced this year which has resulted in low rainfall.

He stated that the programme will be of great help to the people of Kaoma especially the refugees and its host community and later assured the BRE’s support to the program and commitment to the fight against climate change.

And Chief Mutondo Webby Mulubisha of the Nkoya people expressed gratitude to the gesture shown by the world bank to the refugees and the host community, stressed cooperation and reaffirmed the royal establishment’s support and commitment in the chiefdom and entire Kaoma.

Chief Mutondo noted the importance of stopping the indiscriminate cutting down of trees and the need for planting of trees in open areas in order to protect the environment and reduce climate change effects.

“In the first place, I feel greatly honored by your visit in the sense that climate change is real, we have to face it squarely, So as you have come, we can put up our heads together so that we can see what we can do for our brothers and sisters who are disadvantaged, the refugees. The issue of deforestation is a dreadful scenario, we must stop it and on the other side, planting of trees is a deliberate intervention in this case”, stated Chief Mutondo.

Meanwhile, Kaoma District Commissioner Kashina Sheba also thanked the World Bank for its continued partnership with the government and in supporting the displaced people as well as the host community in Kaoma and Zambia at large.

The World Bank is undertaking the climate risk vulnerability assessment adaptation project in three refugee camps and host communities which include in Kaoma’s Mayukwayukwa settlement camp, Matapala in Nchelenge and Maheba in Kalumbila districts respectively.

In Kaoma, the team interacted with the district administration, council, forestry and agriculture departments as well as the traditional leadership, Mayukwayukwa settlement camp and the host community in order to assess climate change challenges and impacts in the refugee camp and host community.

World.title: Kenya: DCI to Help Investigate and Dismantle Doping Networks
World.content:
Nairobi — The Directorate of Criminal Investigations will work with the Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya to identify and dismantle networks involved in doping.

This follows the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between the two agencies to strengthen intelligence sharing and coordinated investigations.

DCI Director Mohamed Amin says the partnership will support efforts to protect athletes from exploitation and promote fair competition.

ADAK Chief Executive Officer Peninah Wahome says closer cooperation with law enforcement agencies is critical in tackling doping-related offences and protecting Kenya's sporting reputation.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The growing list of sanctions has raised concerns about the extent to which doping has penetrated Kenya's once-celebrated distance-running fraternity.

The situation is equally concerning at the domestic level. The Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya (ADAK) currently lists 65 provisionally suspended athletes on its active register, with additional cases involving prohibited substances such as EPO and CERA, as well as alleged anti-doping rule violations, reported in October and early November.

The concern is that repeated high-profile doping cases could leave future Kenyan performances under unnecessary suspicion, even when achieved through legitimate means.

Kenya also faces questions about the effectiveness of its anti-doping enforcement mechanisms.

Kenya remains in Category A, the highest-risk classification under World Athletics' anti-doping framework, while its anti-doping programme has previously faced intense international scrutiny over funding and institutional capacity.

The recurrence of sophisticated doping cases, particularly those involving blood manipulation and EPO, suggests that expanding testing alone may not be enough to address the problem.

As AIU Chief Executive Brett Clothier acknowledged on Thursday, Kenya has made progress in strengthening its anti-doping structures over the past five years, but significant challenges remain.

"The Kenyan authorities have made a lot of progress in the fight against doping in the last five years, but these cases highlight that there is still a long way to go. The Kenyan government is aware of the current situation and has committed to further strengthen the Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya and take action to address the criminal networks that facilitate doping within the country," Clothier said.

He added that the AIU would discuss the details of those commitments with the Kenyan government in the coming months.

Against this backdrop, the proposed Anti-Doping (Amendment) Bill, 2026, currently undergoing public participation in the Senate, could become a significant milestone in Kenya's efforts to confront the crisis.

Close 

The proposed legislation seeks to strengthen the legal framework for combating doping by targeting not only athletes who use prohibited substances but also individuals and networks involved in supplying and facilitating their use.

Among the proposed measures are fines of up to KSh5 million and prison sentences of up to five years for medical practitioners, coaches and other individuals found culpable of supplying banned substances.

The Bill also proposes enhanced enforcement powers for ADAK compliance officers.

If enacted and effectively implemented, the legislation could mark a shift in Kenya's anti-doping strategy, moving beyond the punishment of individual athletes towards dismantling the networks that enable doping.

World.title: Mozambique: Banning a Film of People Saying They Are Powerless Stresses What They Are Saying
World.content:
The treason trial of Venancio Mondlane is claiming to ask who is responsible for the violence in the post-election demonstrations. The answer from ordinary people filmed in demonstrations and interviews is in the banned OMR film “Isn’t this our country?” (Nao e nosso pais este aqui?) The 45 minute film is particularly good in recording both the power people felt in the demonstrations, their disempowerment facing the damage done to their lives by mining, and the powerlessness faced by young people with no jobs and no future.

The powerlessness was stressed by the 9 October 2024 general elections, with widespread fraud. (I was in Maputo reporting that election for CIP, and the fraud was so great no one knows who actually won.) Ten days later, on 19 October, Elvino Dias, the official lawyer for opposition candidate Venancio Mondlane, was gunned down in Maputo. On 21 October Mondlane held a press conference at the site of the murder, calling for protests, and he and the journalists were teargassed by the police. That propelled the demonstrations, but in protests from 21 to 25 October police killed 24 people. That created a wave of anger, and demonstrations took on a different tone. The film shows that the response was attacks on symbols of party and state power – burning Frelimo offices and police stations.

The film makes clear how the subsequent demonstrations and actions were decided locally in cities and towns across the country. It also makes clear the anger of ordinary people at what they see being done to them, and about their lack of power to respond.



The film does not hide the reality, and shows at least two people actually being killed by police, including journalist Mano Shottas shot livestreaming a protest on Facebook in Ressano Garcia.

Showing of the film in Mozambique is blocked by a state agency saying it was filmed without a licence, when the law specifically applies only to commercial filming and not research institutes like OMR (Rural Observatory). But it is obvious why Frelimo is anxious that it not be shown during the treason trial – it tells a very different story from the one being told in the courtroom. It gives Mozambicans a voice in their own country. (I am out of Mozambique and was allowed to see this excellent film. There is a subtitled version.)

For Portuguese readers, the two OMR people responsible for the film, Joao Feijo and Rita Chiure, have also written two important research papers going into these issues more deeply, Observador Rural 172 and 169 https://omrmz.org/observador-rural/

Mozambique Times (Independent newsletter with journalist in the courtroom) https://bit.ly/Moz-trial-MozTimes;Mozambique Insights has commentary in English www.mozambiqueinsights.com

World.title: South Africa: Joburg Women Lead March Against Pie Act Amendments
World.content:
Under the bill, people arranging an occupation without the owner's consent could face jail time or a R2-million fine

On Friday, over a hundred people, mostly women, marched through the streets of Johannesburg to the Provincial Legislature, opposing the draft amendment to the Prevention of Illegal Eviction from and Unlawful Occupation of Land Act (PIE Act).

The march was organised by the Inner City Resource Centre, Rivoningo Women's Forum and Voices Against Eviction.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The PIE Act was passed in 1998 to repeal apartheid era laws. Under the draft amendment bill, published for public comment earlier this year, it will be an offence to take payment for arranging an occupation, or to "incite, arrange, organise or permit any person to occupy land without the consent of the owner". The penalty is a fine of up to R2-million, up to two years in prison, or both.

March organiser Monica Hasamu said the group had submitted a memorandum to the Gauteng premier in August, calling on MPs and party chief whips to oppose the amendments.

The provincial government was given 30 days to schedule a meeting with a delegation of the housing rights groups listed in the memorandum. But this did not happen.

"The government should ... consult us before carrying on with its plans to amend the PIE Act, before it criminalises communities who have been actively building Joburg for years," said Hasamu.

The group's memorandum said many families who have lived in inner-city Johannesburg buildings since 1994 are now being labelled "hijackers" or "treated as criminals".

Marchers demanded an end to unlawful evictions, demolitions and displacement of poor and vulnerable residents across Gauteng. They also want the government to upgrade abandoned and neglected buildings and informal settlements.

Zamekhile Phakathi, who has lived at Frazer House with her four children since 2021, was one of more than 100 residents who were evicted from a building in Hillbrow. They were assisted by the Socio-Economic Rights Institute to secure the emergency shelter.

"We may be evicted considering that our case is still in court. The government should listen to us before making amendments to the PIE Act," said Phakathi.

Fahmida Edries from Happy Valley settlement in Eldorado Park said she moved to the settlement a year ago. Their shacks have been demolished several times.

Close 

"We want the government to give us services and build RDP houses. Amendments to the PIE Act to promote evictions are out of the question," said Edries.

World.title: Nigeria: Kano Govt Dismisses Kwankwaso's EFCC Allegations Against Governor Yusuf
World.content:
The Kano State Government dismissed allegations by former Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso accusing Governor Abba Yusuf of instigating the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to investigate him.

The Kano State Government dismissed allegations by former Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso that Governor Abba Yusuf instigated the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to investigate him.

In a statement by the Commissioner for Information and Internal Affairs, Sunusi Bature, the state government said Governor Yusuf was not involved in Mr Kwankwaso's case with the anti-graft agency.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"The government wishes to state categorically that Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf has absolutely no involvement in Kwankwaso's dealings with the EFCC. Senator Kwankwaso has had engagements with the anti-corruption agency long before the emergence of the present administration in Kano State.

"It is therefore wrong, misleading and politically motivated for him to associate Governor Yusuf with an issue that predates the current government," the statement said.

The government described linking Governor Yusuf to the investigations as "wrong, misleading, and politically motivated."

Earlier on Friday, Mr Kwankwaso--who is running as the 2027 vice-presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC)--accused his former political protégé of abusing their 43-year relationship by weaponising state institutions against him and his political allies.

Responding to claims of interference in opposition affairs, the state government also distanced Governor Yusuf from ongoing court cases involving the NDC.

It stated that the legal proceedings stemmed from internal disagreements within the party and have nothing to do with the state administration.

"It is becoming increasingly clear that Senator Kwankwaso is attempting to use Governor Yusuf as a convenient target to attract public sympathy and political relevance ahead of the 2027 general elections," the statement read.

The administration urged the former governor to focus on resolving the internal challenges within his political camp rather than blaming the state government for his political difficulties.

"The government also rejects Kwankwaso's attempt to link Governor Yusuf with the internal crisis and court cases involving the NDC. These are internal party matters arising from disagreements within the NDC, and the Kano State Government has no involvement whatsoever in the legal proceedings.

Close 

Reiterating that Governor Yusuf was elected to deliver governance rather than engage in endless political disputes, the statement warned that voters in Kano are well-aware of current political developments.

"You cannot win public sympathy through blackmail and unfounded allegations," the government stated, adding that those relying on such tactics should prepare for the verdict of the electorate at the polls in 2027.

The statement added that Governor Yusuf remains focused on development and the welfare of the people of Kano State.

World.title: Nigeria: Widow Demands Prosecution of Police Officers Linked to Dead Husband's Disappearance
World.content:
The widow's lawyers also demanded the release of the duplicate investigation file and payment of the N2 million damages awarded to their client by the Federal High Court in Abuja.

The widow of businessman John Anozie has asked the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, and the Attorney-General of the Federation, Lateef Fagbemi, to prosecute police officers implicated in her husband's death, accusing both institutions of failing to act despite a court judgment and the transfer of the investigation file to the AGF.

The Nigeria Police Force (NPF) forwarded the original investigation file on Mr Anozie's death to the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF) four months ago, but the officers implicated in the case are yet to be prosecuted.

His widow, Nnenna John-Anozie, has now written to the IGP and the AGF, demanding action.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Ms John-Anozie made the demands in separate letters dated 17 November and written on her behalf by her lawyers, Providence Law Firm.

Both letters were received by the respective offices on 19 November, according to receipt stamps on copies PREMIUM TIMES obtained.

In the letter to Mr Disu, the lawyers demanded the immediate release of the duplicate investigation file, the handover of the implicated officers for prosecution and payment of the N2 million damages awarded to their client by the Federal High Court in Abuja.

They asked the police to "immediately release the certified true copy of the case file" containing the investigation records on Mr Anozie's abduction and death.

They also demanded that the police "immediately hand over the culpable and indicted officers" to the AGF for prosecution.

The officers named in the letter are retired Assistant Superintendent of Police Anthony Obiozor Ikechukwu, Sergeant Uzochukwu Emeana, John Eze and Oriole, also known as T-Boy.

The lawyers also demanded payment of the N2 million damages awarded to Ms John-Anozie by the court.

In a separate letter to Mr Fagbemi, the lawyers asked him to intervene by directing the police to produce the implicated officers for prosecution and commence proceedings against them.

They also urged the AGF to direct the IGP to comply with the outstanding aspects of the court judgment, particularly releasing the duplicate case file and paying the damages.

The lawyers asked the AGF to ensure that "the prosecution of the culpable individuals" commenced so justice could be served.

The letter to the IGP indicated that the lawyers had previously drawn the police's attention to the Federal High Court judgment through letters dated 14 October 2025, 26 May 2026 and 21 July 2026.

They said the latest correspondence became necessary because the outstanding court orders had not yet been fulfilled.

The letters came about four months after the police informed the Federal High Court that they had forwarded the original investigation file to the AGF for review and possible prosecution.

'Passage of time has deepened pain'

On 13 July, Nnenna's lawyer told the court that the police had located the file and released it for photocopying. He, however, said he did not know why the police had not forwarded it to the AGF as of that day.

Judge Binta Nyako said she was considering whether to transfer the contempt proceedings to another judge because she had become "so involved" in the matter.

However, on 24 July, the court announced that the case file had been forwarded to the AGF. The judge subsequently retained the case.

The police filed a Notice of Compliance showing that the original case file had been forwarded to the AGF.

The documents showed that the file contained the police investigation report, crime diary extracts, witness statements, statements from the implicated police officers, police wireless messages and records of investigation activities.

It also contained legal advice and subsequent correspondence on the advice.

The Commissioner of Police, X-Squad Section of the Force Criminal Investigation Department, originally forwarded the file to the IGP on 8 June 2020 for prosecution.

A letter dated 15 July 2026 from the Directorate of Legal Services said the case file had been forwarded to the AGF for "perusal, legal inputs and possible prosecution".

The AGF's office acknowledged receipt of the file on 20 July.

The police's compliance with that part of the judgment was a significant development in a case that had remained stalled for years. However, the transfer did not resolve the other issues covered by the judgment.

The outstanding orders included releasing a certified true copy of the duplicate case file to Ms John-Anozie, arresting and handing over the principal suspects for prosecution, and paying the N2 million in damages awarded to her.

Four months later, Ms John-Anozie said the AGF's office had yet to act on the file.

"The Office of the Attorney General of the Federation has, to date, taken no action on the case file reportedly forwarded to it," she said.

She said she had "therefore been placed in the extraordinary position of having to pursue a case concerning" her dead husband while being "denied access to the very investigative records generated in that case."

She added: "And so, after nine years of petitions, investigations, court orders, panel proceedings, legal representations and litigation, the questions with which this journey began remain the same:

"The passage of time has not diminished the pain; it has deepened it."

What the law says

The Administration of Criminal Justice Act provides a timeframe for the Attorney-General of the Federation to act after receiving certain police case files.

Section 376(1) provides that: "Where an offence for which the Magistrate Court has no jurisdiction to try is preferred against a defendant, the police shall at the end of investigation submit the original case file to the office of the Attorney-General of the Federation."

Section 376(2) further provides that: "The Attorney-General of the Federation shall, within fourteen days of receipt of the police case file, issue and serve his legal advice indicating whether or not there is a prima facie case against the defendant for which he can be prosecuted."

The Federal Ministry of Justice says its Department of Public Prosecutions "provides legal advice to law enforcement agencies and conducts public prosecutions on behalf of the Attorney-General of the Federation".

The long search for justice

PREMIUM TIMES, in an investigation, documented Ms John-Anozie's long search for her husband and the repeated failure of police authorities to comply with court orders and directives from the #EndSARS Judicial Panel of Inquiry.

Her husband disappeared in June 2017 after officers attached to the defunct Special Anti-Robbery Squad travelled from Awkuzu, Anambra State, to his home in Lekki, Lagos. The police later claimed he died in custody but failed to produce his body.

Close 

Ms John-Anozie approached the National Human Rights Commission and the #EndSARS panel to seek answers. The panel's proceedings were adjourned more than 12 times because police officers failed to appear and produce the investigation file.

Other courts also ordered the police to produce her husband or his body, but the police failed to comply.

In 2023, she petitioned the police to reopen the investigation. When they failed to provide information, her lawyer, Vincent Adodo, sought the records under the Freedom of Information Act.

The police did not respond, prompting her to approach the Federal High Court in Abuja.

On 24 September 2025, Judge Binta Nyako ordered the police to release the investigation records, hand over the implicated officers for prosecution and pay her N2 million in damages.

The police failed to release the documents within the seven days the court allowed.

Ms John-Anozie subsequently commenced contempt proceedings against the then IGP, Kayode Egbetokun.

Mr Egbetokun later left office and was replaced by Olatunji Disu, whose administration pledged to end police impunity and ensure officers are held accountable.

During the contempt proceedings, the court was informed that the investigation file had been forwarded to the AGF.

However, Ms John-Anozie said she had not yet received a copy of the file, and the police had also failed to comply with other outstanding aspects of the judgment.

The AGF and the police spokesperson did not respond to requests for comment.
