World.title: South Africa: NHI Survives First Two Constitutional Challenges
World.content:
The court rejected a medical schemes industry challenge and dismissed a Western Cape government challenge

The Constitutional Court has rejected two constitutional challenges to the National Health Insurance Act.

The Board of Healthcare Funders argued that Parliament had failed to provide enough information about the costs, funding and operating model of NHI. The court rejected this, finding that meaningful public participation did not require perfect information.

The Western Cape government's challenge to the public participation process in the National Council of Provinces was dismissed. The majority found that residents had a reasonable opportunity to influence the process, even if their proposed amendments were not adopted.

In a dissenting judgment, Justice Steven Majiedt said the NCOP process had serious flaws in how it had considered provincial submissions, including that Gauteng's report never reached it.

The National Health Insurance (NHI) Act has survived the first two of what is expected to be many legal challenges in the months and years to come.

While the Act has not yet come into operation, it was signed into law in May 2024, following a public participation process involving oral and written submissions in all nine provinces, which were then considered by the National Assembly and the National Council of Provinces (NCOP).

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The issue of meaningful public participation was central to the two challenges, which came before the Constitutional Court in May.

Medical schemes challenge

In the first challenge, the Board of Healthcare Funders, which represents 65 medical schemes and administrators, argued that full meaningful participation was not possible because Parliament had not provided information on the costs and funding of the basket of services or on the proposed operating model.

Parliament, the board contended, had approached the whole issue with a "closed mind".

Handing down the ruling on Friday, Justice Steven Majiedt said the court had unanimously dismissed this argument.

He said the Bill was introduced in the National Assembly in August 2019, kicking off a process which lasted nearly four years, including hearings in all nine provinces. It resulted in 961 oral and nearly 339,000 written submissions.

Majiedt said the court held that while the Constitution required that members of the public and interested parties were given enough information to make public participation "meaningful", it did not require it to provide "perfect information".

"Moreover, implementation of the NHI scheme will stretch over decades and will depend on resources available. Reliable costing is not yet possible, and the basket of services is to be determined incrementally," he said.

The evidence also did not show that Parliament had a "closed mind".

Western Cape challenge

The second challenge was raised by the Western Cape Premier, also on the issue of public participation but specifically in the National Council of Provinces (NCOP).

On this application, the court was divided. The application was dismissed by a six-to-five majority. Majiedt penned the minority judgment.

The minority, he said, had found that the public participation process in the NCOP was unreasonable and unconstitutional, especially in light of the fact that the Act seeks to fundamentally change how health care is funded and accessed.

"It will affect virtually every person in the country in matters of health, dignity and, at times, survival.

"There was a need for an exacting public participation process."

The NCOP's Select Committee on Health and Social Services was supposed to consider reports from every province.

While most of the provinces had expressed support for the bill, this was subject to their proposals and amendments. The select committee, however, had just "mechanically treated these mandates as votes in favour of the bill," the minority found.

By the time the committee had considered the Western Cape report, it was already too late to influence deliberations. The Western Cape's submissions, in a 635-page report, were considered at a separate 35-minute meeting.

The Gauteng report was never put before the NCOP. The minority said no explanation had ever been given for this, and the NCOP had done nothing to obtain the report.

"The views of the residents of the most populous province never reached the legislature," said Majiedt.

But the majority judgment, penned by Justice Jody Kollapen, dismissed the application.

The judges noted that the bill had given rise to opinions so sharply divided and ideologically diverse that persuasion was unlikely.

The voices of Gauteng residents had been heard, they said, through written submissions and via members of the select committee who attended the provincial hearings.

Close 

The judges said failure to influence a process could not be used to challenge it if the concerns raised had been considered.

They had conducted a detailed analysis of the committee's meeting, and it was clear that it had a "common understanding" of all concerns and had considered them.

"The fact that proposed amendments were not adopted shows at most that the committee was not persuaded that the bill required amendment. All that reasonable public participation guarantees is a reasonable opportunity to influence the outcome. It does not guarantee that the outcome will change."

The majority found it inappropriate to subject a legislative public participation process to a formulaic or forensic audit.

"If that standard were adopted, virtually every challenge to a public participation process would collapse into a substantive review of the legislation itself."

The court made no order on costs.

Direct quotes in this article are from Majiedt's summary of the judgment, not from the written judgment itself.

Read the judgment here

World.title: South Africa: Father Launches Silent Campaign Against Gun Violence After Son's Death
World.content:
After losing his 31-year-old son to gun violence a month ago, Lavender Hill resident Mark Nicholson has launched a silent campaign calling for urgent action against shootings in his community.

On Sunday at 5.30am, Nicholson walked through Lavender Hill with friends and family. They held posters and wore T-shirts bearing the face of his son, Keenan.

On Friday morning, Nicholson stood at the Lavender Hill robots on the M5 in a white shirt with Keenan's picture on it. He held the same poster: "Where are the guns coming from that are killing our children?"

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Keenan was among five people killed in a shooting after gunmen opened fire at a house in Lavender Hill on Saturday, 24 October.

Western Cape police commissioner Lieutenant General Sizakhele Dyantyi visited the crime scene in Blode Street the following morning. In a SAPS statement, Dyantyi said it couldn't be normal for people to be "killed in such numbers" in their communities.

"Police resources were deployed to the area in an effort to bring those responsible for the murders and attempted murders to book," the statement said. SAPS did not answer whether any arrests have been made.

The silent campaign follows a 100km walk Nicholson undertook from Malmesbury to Moorreesburg between 22 and 24 November in memory of people who have lost their lives to gun violence.

Although the walk left his legs and feet sore, he said "every step was for every murder caused in South Africa".

Tyrin Basil Landsman, co-owner of Tyrin's Tour and long-time friend of Nicholson, helped transport Nicholson's family to Moorreesburg after the 100km walk.

Landsman said he was happy to be part of Nicholson's journey and to offer whatever support he could.

"We believe in the importance of community, standing together and supporting people who are doing something meaningful," Landsman said.

Firearms were used in 732 of the 1,109 murders recorded in the Western Cape between July and September 2026, the highest number of any province. The province also accounted for 208 of the country's 261 gang-related murders.

Nicholson said he wants to meet with SAPS and law enforcement officials to discuss ways to make their community safer. He said he was hoping to meet with the Steenberg station commander next week.

"I will campaign every second of the day until I am heard; nothing will stand in my way," he said on Friday while standing at the robots.

World.title: Zelenskyy compares Putin to Hitler as Trump pushes to end Ukraine war: 'He's an aggressor and a killer'
World.content:

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy compared Russian President Vladimir Putin to Adolf Hitler on Thursday amid President Donald Trump's ongoing efforts to end the war between Russia and Ukraine.

"Of course, it's up to President of the United States, but it's strange. He's (Putin) an aggressor and a killer. He can't be a friend. It just cannot be," Zelenskyy told the British Broadcasting Company (BBC) during an interview that aired Thursday.

"It's the same that somebody say about Hitler during the Second World War, that he's a good friend. No, he is not a friend," Zelenskyy continued.

Trump used the word friend to describe Putin while meeting with the Russian president during a trilateral summit in China on Nov. 19.

ZELENSKYY PRESSES US FOR EXPANDED RUSSIA TALKS AS KUSHNER ANNOUNCES BREAKTHROUGH

Trump entered a room where Putin was waiting and said, "Who is he? He's my friend," before shaking Putin's hand. He later posted a photo to Truth Social of the pair shaking hands with the caption "My Friend."

Zelenskyy further criticized the United States, claiming the U.S. was sending Ukraine signals similar to those he had been getting from Russia.

"We need more progress. This is what we need. We need American position to be American position. We don't need signals, I mean, that are from the United States, which we can get from Russia," he told the BBC.

"It's not about Russia or not Russia," he added. "They have to put pressure on the situation. The situation is … Russia is [the] aggressor. So that's why they have to do it. That's why they are mediators. It's not about comfortable talks. It's about a strong country who can pressure because this country has power and respect."

KUSHNER ENTERS UKRAINE PEACE TALKS AS TRUMP EYES SECURING SAFEGUARDS AGAINST ANOTHER RUSSIAN INVASION

Zelenskyy also expressed frustration that the U.S. has focused much of its foreign policy bandwidth on the Middle East during the Iran war rather than on Europe.

"It's a pity they made a focus on the Middle East and they helped them more, but it's their choice," he said.

The war between Russia and Ukraine has been raging for nearly five years. Starting when Russian troops invaded eastern Ukraine, the war has now racked up well over 1 million casualties between Russia and Ukraine, according to the Center for Strategic & International Studies.

MIKE WALTZ WARNS KREMLIN FACES 'UNSUSTAINABLE' LOSSES APPROACHING WWII SCALE AS TRUMP SEEKS DEAL

A recent report from Russian news outlets estimated that Russia has lost at least 700,000 troops. CSIS estimates that Russia's casualty numbers are double those of Ukraine's.

Despite the apparent mismatch in casualties, Russia now holds portions of Ukrainian territory and may be poised to keep them after the war's conclusion, a possibility Trump acknowledged.

TRUMP RUSSIA DEAL COULD FUEL PUTIN'S WAR, EX-NATO COMMANDER WARNS AS ZELENSKYY SAYS 'NYET'

"They're gonna end up with a little bit different shaped Ukraine," Trump told Ross Douthat of CBS' "60 Minutes."

Trump also told CBS that he believed the war is going to end soon.

He also told reporters on Thursday that he's pushing each side to make a deal.

"We want to make a deal. We want to stop the killing," Trump said.

"I could walk in and say, ‘I don’t like you!’ and then we have the same problem that we have with Zelenskyy and Putin. The biggest problem with that settlement is the fact that you have two leaders that really hate each other," the president added.

World.title: Broadcast networks use airport immigration arrest to attack ICE, just like usual
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

When it comes to illegal immigration, no one should be turning the channel to the broadcast news networks for a "mainstream media" presentation. It is better to imagine it under the title "Abolish ICE Theater."

That was on flagrant display in January with the aggressive law-enforcement presence in Minneapolis, when two protesters were killed in confrontations with officers in January. A Media Research Center study found the network newscasts did over two hours of coverage in a 10-day period and were 93% negative toward ICE. The actual criminal acts of illegal immigrants were a tiny fraction of the coverage: 13 seconds on ABC, 16 seconds on CBS and 89 seconds on NBC.

That pattern has continued, as if the sides here weren’t about immigration law, but about President Donald Trump. ICE receives the same severely negative coverage the president gets, while illegal immigrants receive the sympathetic coverage constantly delivered to the anti-Trump side, whatever the circumstances.

ANTI-ICE PROTESTERS AT SEATTLE-TACOMA AIRPORT FORCE SECURITY PRESENCE DURING BUSY HOLIDAY TRAVEL

On Nov. 21, ICE agents came to a jet bridge at the Seattle airport to detain Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, a Mexican national who had reportedly overstayed his visa by more than 10 years. In the altercation, his daughter, Sofia Hernandez Mejia, also a visa overstayer, allegedly hurled hot coffee on the officers. The illegal immigrants were reportedly going to board a flight from Seattle to Los Angeles.

This led to 19 minutes and 53 seconds of anguished agitprop on the Big Three networks. These are the same networks that routinely ignore ICE arresting rapists, child abusers and murderers. Those stories are typically left on the cutting-room floor (or its digital equivalent).

PEARL JAM DECRIES ICE'S 'SYSTEMIC ABUSE' AFTER 'HEARTBREAKING' SEATTLE AIRPORT ARREST

The good vs. evil narrative was established in the lingo used by the network journalists. On Sunday’s "World News Tonight," ABC anchor Linsey Davis warned, "ICE officers are once again facing scrutiny over their tactics. This, after an arrest operation at Seattle Tacoma Airport on Saturday. Video shows the confrontation and chaos as a man and woman were arrested by ICE."

On "NBC Nightly News," anchor Hallie Jackson began: "To the new fallout tonight after a chaotic confrontation caught on camera between ICE officers and two people boarding a plane." Reporter Dana Griffin repeated: "Tonight, outrage over a distressing ICE encounter caught on camera. Masked officers seen on a jet bridge trying to detain two people boarding an Alaska Airlines flight."

BORDER DEM POISED TO WIELD ICE PURSE STRINGS REJECTS SOCIALIST ‘DEFUND’ PUSH

Both shows quoted Washington’s Democrat Gov. Bob Ferguson. On ABC, he was "just so sad that our country has come to this place. You know, that we have an agency that just conducts itself in such a cruel way and such a heartless way." On NBC, he proclaimed, "It is time to abolish Donald Trump's ICE." It’s Trump’s police, not federal police.

ICE agents were "distressing people" with "chaotic" results. They were "cruel" and "heartless." The illegal immigrants were just "two people." Any protesters interfering with or obstructing agents, or people reportedly throwing hot coffee at them, are somehow not responsible for "chaos" or "distressing video." Only one side of these disputes is always guilty. The other side is always virtuous, no matter what the immigrants have done.

BROADCAST BIAS: MEDIA SKIP MAMDANI’S ‘GENOCIDE’ COMMENT BUT LOVE HIM BASHING ICE

The theater continued on Monday. ABC anchor David Muir repeated: "Tonight, the disturbing images of a father and daughter arrested by ICE at the airport in Seattle." Correspondent Aaron Katersky echoed: "This is the chaotic, traumatic arrest on an airport jet bridge of a daughter and her father."

NBC repeated the line about "distressing video" and reported the aliens "are being held inside a Tacoma, Washington, ICE processing center after video of their chaotic arrest sent shockwaves online."

WHITE HOUSE BRINGS RECEIPTS AFTER MEDIA CLAIMS NONCRIMINAL ICE ARRESTS ‘SOARING’: ‘FALSE NARRATIVES’

The "CBS Evening News" joined the action, as anchor Tony Dokoupil said: "We turn now to that ugly scene as passengers boarded a flight from Seattle to Los Angeles this weekend. ICE agents appeared on the jet bridge and dragged a father and his adult daughter out the side door as they screamed for help." The governor trashed ICE again: "ICE is completely and totally out of control. And today we are confronted with yet more evidence of this."

This led to 19 minutes and 53 seconds of anguished agitprop on the Big Three networks. These are the same networks that routinely ignore ICE arresting rapists, child abusers and murderers.

There was nothing really new in the second night of reports, except for adding the daughter’s American citizen husband for more defense lawyering. It just looked like the narrative needed another round of promotion, for people who were too busy watching football to catch the Sunday night news.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

The nature of this pro-Democrat narrative became more obvious on Monday’s "PBS NewsHour," when anchor Geoff Bennett asked New York Times immigration reporter Hamed Aleaziz: "What does accountability look like at this point? What consequences, if any, could follow from the [Department of Homeland Security] inspector general's findings?"

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

He doesn’t mean "accountability" for those breaking our immigration laws. No, there’s going to be hell to pay for enforcing the law. Aleaziz explained: "Obviously, we have a Congress coming in, Democrats taking control of the Senate and the House. They have already said that ICE and DHS is going to be a main target of their investigation." Democrats will be "putting a target" on ICE, he said – just as the networks have been doing.

World.title: Does ‘man flu’ really exist? Here’s what an emergency room physician says
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

When a minor cold knocks a man onto the couch for days, it’s often dismissed as a classic case of the "man flu" — but is there real science behind it?

Dr. Stephanie Widmer, a New York City emergency medicine physician, medical toxicologist and Fox News medical contributor, confirmed that the "man flu" is not a real medical diagnosis.

"It is very interesting that ‘man flu’ is becoming a very commonly used term," she told Fox News Digital.

MEN AND WOMEN WHO SMOKE MARIJUANA MAY EXPERIENCE DIFFERENT EFFECTS, STUDY SUGGESTS

But the question remains: Do men actually get "sicker" or experience more severe symptoms than women when they have a cold or the flu?

While some evidence already points to biological differences in how men's and women’s immune systems respond, the doctor noted that the issue "deserves a little bit more attention" from researchers.

"At the end of the day, there is no evidence ... that men have more severe symptoms, suffer more, or experience more pain or discomfort when it comes to the flu, colds or other respiratory viruses and viral illnesses," she said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

There is some data, however, suggesting that men may be hospitalized more or may experience worse mortality after a flu infection than women, according to Widmer.

"But again, that doesn't mean they are necessarily experiencing more severe symptoms," she said. "It doesn't prove that the man flu does exist, so to speak."

While some theorize that women tolerate illness better because the biological capacity for childbirth gives them a naturally higher pain threshold, Widmer noted that this hypothesis has not been scientifically proven.

CLICK HERE TO 

"I'd like to think that's true," she said. "Women have babies. We can endure a lot of pain, but … [it’s not] backed by science."

Research from the National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health, published by the National Institutes of Health in 2022, found that acute pain tolerance is more consistent over time in women than men, while men showed higher pain tolerance in sporadic sessions.

Another 2022 study, published in the Journal of Psychosomatic Research, debunked the "man flu" theory, titling the paper "Man flu is not a thing."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The research analyzed the symptoms of men and women with sinus infections, finding that there was no difference in initial physical severity. Women felt worse at the start, but recovered faster than men.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Although a certain gender difference was found both in the clinician [and] patient-rated ARS symptoms, the hypothesis of a ‘man flu’ should be disregarded," the authors stated.

World.title: Mamdani eyes 2028 kingmaker role as expert warns socialist movement could gain power even in defeat
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's efforts to shape the 2028 Democratic presidential field could help socialists build lasting political influence, even if their preferred candidate ultimately loses the nomination, according to political analysts.

"The 2026 midterm bluenami showed us that the Democrat party is shifting far left, and Mamdani is hoping to capitalize on that momentum," Nicole Huyer, senior research associate for the Heritage Foundation's Institute for Economic Policy Studies, told Fox News Digital.

"What’s really interesting, is that Mamdani seems to be thinking beyond individual candidates for 2028, and more toward building an organized political infrastructure for socialists," she added.

Mamdani, a self-described Democratic socialist, stunned the political establishment in 2025 when he defeated former Gov. Andrew Cuomo in New York City's Democratic mayoral primary before winning the general election, marking a major victory for the socialist movement.

The New York City leader recently held private meetings with top union leaders as part of a broader effort to encourage labor-aligned and leftist candidates to launch White House bids in 2028, Axios reported Nov. 8, citing four anonymous sources.

MAMDANI MAKES BEHIND-THE-SCENES MOVES TO SHAPE 2028 DEMOCRATIC PRESIDENTIAL RACE

Mamdani has argued that progressive Democrats cannot afford to let their midterm gains slip away, according to the report.

"He’s making sure that whoever the candidate is in 2028 will have a strong Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) and progressive movement backing them," Huyer continued. "Basically translating all of the victories socialists saw in 2026 into a coalition capable of winning nationally in 2028."

Even if Democratic socialists fail to secure the party's 2028 presidential nomination, the campaign itself could help build a stronger movement for future elections, according to Stu Smith, investigative analyst at City Journal.

"We will see whether DSA and its allies can turn this vision into reality, but even a failed campaign could prove galvanizing," Smith told Fox News Digital. "Many of DSA's current leaders were politicized through Bernie Sanders's presidential campaigns."

"Even if a more moderate Democratic nominee ultimately emerges, it may prove to be a Pyrrhic victory if the effort helps cultivate a new generation of DSA talent that continues to shape left wing politics and public policy in ways that diverge from traditional American political norms," Smith added.

MAMDANI CONFIDENT THERE'S A PATH FOR A PROGRESSIVE CANDIDATE TO THE WHITE HOUSE IN 2028

Huyer went on to say that certain policies favored by some Democratic socialists, such as steep wealth taxes and rent control, could "be devastating" to the U.S. economy.

"Socialism may be gaining ground ideologically and culturally due to messaging success, but the socialist economic agenda remains completely destructive," she said.

The DSA’s "Workers Deserve More" platform proposes enacting "aggressive wealth taxes on the richest individuals and corporations" to spend on public goods and infrastructure projects.

SOCIALISTS LAUNCH RADICAL PLATFORM TO ABOLISH THE US SENATE IN BID TO FUNDAMENTALLY TRANSFORM AMERICA

Several DSA chapters across the U.S., including Los Angeles, Atlanta and Chicago, have recently issued "Run AOC Run" resolutions to urge Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to launch a 2028 White House bid, City & State New York reported.

More progressive candidates may potentially shift the 2028 Democratic primary field to the left, but they could also split the vote and create an opportunity for a more moderate candidate to win, the Manhattan Institute's Director of Public Opinion Matthew Shor told Fox News Digital.

"On the one hand, a larger number of progressive candidates could push the field toward policies favored by the party’s most committed activists," Shor stated. "But on the other hand, too many progressives could split the vote in that lane and let a moderate circumvent them en route to the nomination. As much as any faction wants to influence the conversation, they would much rather win the nomination."

The DSA’s platform also calls for abolishing the Electoral College and replacing the U.S. president and Supreme Court "with an executive and judiciary chosen by and subordinate to Congress."

Several Democratic socialists secured major wins in this year's midterms.

Six DSA-endorsed candidates won their House races in the 2026 midterms: Melat Kiros in Colorado; Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez in New York; Donavan McKinney in Michigan; Angela Gonzales-Torres in California; and Chris Rabb in Pennsylvania, Fox News Digital previously reported.

Still, Democrats embracing far-left candidates in the next election cycle could help the GOP to "regain political momentum" they lost in the 2026 midterms, Wayne Winegarden, senior fellow in business and economics at the Pacific Research Institute, said.

MAMDANI-BACKED SOCIALIST WINS NYC HOUSE SEAT AS DSA EXPANDS ITS REACH IN CONGRESS

"While many progressives may run [in 2028], the Democrats have large majorities in Congress because moderate candidates won in places that have voted Republican for years," Winegarden told Fox News Digital. "Democrats have a strong chance to maintain control over Congress and win the Presidency if they demonstrate they are governing effectively from the center and nominate candidates for President who would govern as such."

"Should the Democrats embrace the progressive left, they will create a pathway for Republicans to regain political momentum," he added.

When reached for comment on Nov. 10, Mamdani’s office referred Fox News Digital to remarks he made at a Nov. 9 press conference.

"And when it comes to these meetings, I [have] sought and continue to meet with labor leaders precisely because they have been on the front lines of delivering for those working people and the importance of ensuring that the crises that affect working people are at the centerpiece of any of the politics that come from now until 2028," Mamdani told reporters.

World.title: Big Ten playoff panic, SEC upset threats and a $26 million Deion Sanders question await on rivalry Saturday
World.content:
The final weekend of the college football regular season is already underway, and Saturday could lead to a conundrum within two of the biggest conferences.

By Sunday morning, the Big Ten could be asking how many College Football Playoff bids it has left, the SEC could be arguing about a three-loss Tennessee team and Colorado could be doing some very expensive math.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

If you’d told us before the season that USC-UCLA would have playoff implications, most of us would’ve assumed the Trojans were the ones trying to lock up a spot.

SEC THREATENS THE NUCLEAR OPTION AS LSU’S REBELLION PUTS CONFERENCE FUTURE AT RISK, RJ LUIS PLANS TO SUE

But, since there has been nothing predictable about the 2026 season, it's fitting that the Big Ten conference needs a smooth weekend to avoid a chaotic ending that could see the Bruins joining Indiana as teams missing the playoff.

In the SEC, it's business as usual with the Georgia Bulldogs leading the charge, as Texas follows closely behind in terms of playoff rankings.

On Friday night, even though Texas A&M was pesky, the Longhorns clinched a spot in the conference title game and will play Georgia next week in Atlanta for the final SEC championship.

But, there is no semblance of LSU and Ole Miss in the postseason conversation, rather replaced by a team like Tennessee.

That's right, Lane Kiffin and Pete Golding are both missing the CFP, while Alabama can secure its spot in the postseason behind freshman quarterback Keelon Russell against the pesky Auburn Tigers in the latest edition of the "Iron Bowl."

A $17 MILLION BILL FOR AN AD WHO NEVER ACTUALLY STARTED? MICHIGAN'S TREV ALBERTS MESS GETS UGLIER

In the Big 12, it was all about Utah and BYU getting out of the weekend unscathed. Thanks to the Utes destroying West Virginia on Friday night, they will walk into the conference title game against Texas Tech undefeated.

There is a chance they could get three teams into the postseason, if the Red Raiders win the Big 12 title game against Utah, with BYU potentially grabbing that final spot.

Entering this final Saturday, also known as "Rivalry Week," we might also see a number of head coaches roaming their current sidelines one last time before switching jobs over the next few weeks.

And, there seems to be a lot of interesting noise coming out of Boulder around Colorado head coach Deion Sanders.

Here we go, Big Ten, it comes down to UCLA and Oregon (Or Iowa)

The postseason hopes for UCLA could rest on the hip of quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who was carted off the field last weekend after a nasty hit against Michigan, which also came on the same day that Bob Chesney lost his first game as Bruins head coach.

After losing to Washington last week, it's Indiana that is also hoping for some sort of chaos within the Big Ten, especially when you consider that the Hoosiers only way of securing a CFP spot is by playing for a conference title next week, along with beating Purdue today.

BIG TEN FACES ONE-BID NIGHTMARE IN CFP RANKINGS AS SEC EYES FOUR BIDS AND BIG 12 COULD THRIVE

So, can the Big Ten snag at least two spots in the CFP? Sure, but it would be easier for the conference if UCLA won on Saturday against USC, and then potentially sustain their second loss next weekend in the conference championship against Oregon.

I think it's also fair to say that Lincoln Riley needs to win this game against UCLA if he is going to comfortably return in 2027. I would also emphasize that there are two schools within the state of Texas paying close attention to this one on Saturday.

If the Ducks, who started the season 4-3, can beat Washington on Saturday, Dan Lanning would be one win away from a CFP berth that looked unattainable just five weeks ago.

And, we can't forget about the Iowa Hawkeyes, who destroyed Nebraska on Friday afternoon to finish the regular season 10-2. Heck, I could make a valid argument that Kirk Ferentz deserves to be coaching in the CFP without playing for the Big Ten title.

IOWA'S KIRK FERENTZ THREATENS TO FIRE COACHES IF THEY MENTION STYLE POINTS WITH GREAT OLD-SCHOOL STATEMENT

But, there will be plenty of questions answered throughout the day, with the Big Ten needing to stay away from the chaos that has engulfed them over the past month.

SEC madness on the way? There's potential in Tuscaloosa and Nashville

If you want to see a conference sweating bullets, have Vanderbilt upset Tennessee on Saturday night and watch the arguments for a potential 9-3 Vols' still deserving a spot in the postseason.

After defeating LSU last weekend, and leaving Lane Kiffin with his fifth loss of the regular season, Josh Heupel is one win away from leading this Tennessee team to a postseason berth without a functioning quarterback position.

Can Vanderbilt spoil it for their in-state rival? The Dores would love nothing more behind freshman quarterback Jared Curtis, though the Vols defense is one of the nastiest we've seen in college football this season.

LANE KIFFIN TAKES THE SIDE EXIT AS TENNESSEE SENDS LSU HOME AND MOVES TO THE DOORSTEP OF CFP

As for No. 5 Alabama, it's a visit from the Auburn Tigers that will be its final hurdle of the regular season.

Unfortunately for the Tide, it will have to get through the "Iron Bowl" before they start discussing postseason plans, and this game almost always brings some sort of chaos with it.

Sure, Alabama might be fourteen-point favorites, but the 7-4 Auburn Tigers are hoping to wreck their in-state rival's Thanksgiving weekend.

Just remember, anything can happen on rivalry weekend, and there is bound to be some sort of havoc unfolding on Saturday afternoon in the SEC.

That could even be something as small as Arkansas handing LSU its sixth loss of the season, which would not go over well in Baton Rouge.

Is Deion Sanders coaching his final game at Colorado?

There have been plenty of awkward moments around Boulder over the past four seasons behind Coach Prime, but 2026 is just uncomfortable to watch.

Will he go or will he stay? These have been the compounding questions that continue to be asked around campus over the past month. The press conferences have been intense, and a bit confrontational.

But, does Colorado have the entire $26 million needed to fire Deion Sanders?

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Maybe not, but after missing a bowl game for the second year in a row, the Buffaloes are not getting any better as more time passes and it might be time to take out a small loan.

Entering today's season finale, Deion is 20-28 over his four years in Boulder. Even though he has undoubtedly reignited the fire at Colorado, it's clear that this program might need to try something new.

We will find out after today's game against UCF, but there is a chance this is the last time we see Coach Prime roaming the Buffs sidelines.

It's wild to think the 2026 regular season has already come to an end. It feels like we were just sitting in a Baton Rouge courthouse waiting for a judge to decide on whether two players could be rostered by LSU.

Oh, and the ongoing fight between the SEC and the Tigers doesn’t seem to be dying down any time soon, with an expulsion vote possibly coming next week.

As for the college football playoff, things will become much more clearer Sunday morning, as one final chance at chaos presents itself.

World.title: Zelenskyy questions Trump’s ‘strange’ reference to Putin as a ‘friend’
World.content:
KYIV, Ukraine — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed frustration with the U.S. stance toward Russian leader Vladimir Putin, in the latest sign of deepening tension between Kyiv and Washington, as new questions emerged about Europe’s future financial commitments to Ukraine.

Zelenskyy said in an interview with the BBC broadcast Friday that he wants the U.S. to apply more pressure on Putin to stop his invasion of Ukraine, which began almost five years ago and grinds on despite President Donald Trump’s efforts to broker a peace deal.

The Ukrainian president described Trump calling Putin “my friend” at a recent summit in China as “strange” because the Russian leader is “an aggressor and a killer.”

“He can’t be a friend,” Zelenskyy told the British broadcaster in Kyiv, likening the statement to someone calling Adolf Hitler a friend during World War II.

The White House did not respond to a request for comment on Zelenskyy’s remarks. But Trump on Thursday defended his reference to Putin. “We want to make a deal. We want to stop the killing,” he said.

“I could walk in and say, ‘I don’t like you!’ and then we have the same problem that we have with Zelenskyy and Putin,” he said. Speaking to reporters at Mar-a-Lago, he added: “The biggest problem with that settlement is the fact that you have two leaders that really hate each other.”

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Zelenskyy was “insulting his counterpart,” showing that the Ukrainian leader “is not willing to follow the path of (a) peace settlement.”

The International Criminal Court has issued an arrest warrant for Putin for war crimes, accusing him of personal responsibility for the abductions of children from Ukraine. The Trump administration has imposed sweeping sanctions on the court as part of its campaign to dismantle the tribunal over investigations into the U.S. and its allies, including Israel.

The Kremlin has said that Russia also does not recognize the ICC and considers its decisions “legally void.” Peskov in 2023 called the court’s move against Putin “outrageous and unacceptable.”

Zelenskyy’s comments were broadcast a day after Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law and a U.S. envoy trying to mediate an end to the war, complimented Putin on being a “grandmaster” of politics and weeks after Kushner’s partner in peace efforts, Steve Witkoff, described Putin as a “humanitarian.”

Moscow’s invasion has killed hundreds of thousands of troops and thousands of Ukrainian civilians. It also brought heavy sanctions on Russia and diplomatically isolated Putin in the West before Trump resumed relations.

At the same time, Zelenskyy has complained that the Pentagon is not delivering to Ukraine paid-for Patriot missiles that could stop Russia’s ballistic missiles and that SpaceX’s military-grade version of the Starlink satellite internet service, which is the backbone of Ukraine’s drone operations and communication, isn’t working properly.

Europe has in the past vowed to stay the course in helping Ukraine fend off Russia’s invasion. But European Union leaders on Thursday failed to reach consensus after fraught talks over a new $49 billion loan for Ukraine’s economic and military needs next year.

Elections in the EU over the next 12 months could amplify the influence of parties reluctant to send more money to Ukraine and may fray the continent’s support.

The grinding aerial bombardment between Russia and Ukraine has escalated recently.

Russia launched close to 300 aerial attacks a week through Nov. 20 on Ukraine’s civilian infrastructure, according to the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project, or ACLED, which tracks violence.

Frequently asked questions What is Black Friday? Black Friday is one of the biggest shopping events of the year when retailers slash prices on products across categories. It happens the day after Thanksgiving, and while it used to be dedicated to in-store shopping, more shopping now happens online. What should I buy on Black Friday? The best products to buy on Black Friday include tech, toys, small home and kitchen appliances, clothes and shoes, subscriptions and experiences and gift cards and sets. Retailers tend to focus on products that people usually want to gift loved ones (or themselves) ahead of the December holidays. What’s the difference between Black Friday and Cyber Monday? There’s not much of a difference between Black Friday and Cyber Monday anymore. Black Friday, the day after Thanksgiving, was once dedicated to in-store shopping, while Cyber Monday, which happens the Monday after Thanksgiving, was dedicated to online shopping. But in recent years, the line between the two holidays has blurred. Retailers start their sales earlier, host them for longer and discount items in stores and online throughout November, so there’s little distinction. When do Black Friday sales end? Black Friday sales technically end tonight, November 27. However, Cyber Monday is coming up, so most deals are still available over the weekend. That said, you shouldn’t wait to shop — the longer you do, the more likely items on your wish list will sell out. Can you return Black Friday purchases? Yes, you can usually return Black Friday purchases, which often carry the same return policy as items you buy any other time of year. However, there are exceptions, so read the fine print or ask a customer service representative if you’re unclear.
