NEW DELHI: Haryana Police on Saturday used water cannon to disperse Congress workers protesting outside Meta's office in Gurugram over allegations that the company was censoring opposition voices and favouring Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), according to Reuters.The protest, led by the Congress youth wing, is part of a growing confrontation between the opposition party and Meta, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, in India, its largest market by users.Congress has accused the company of restricting opposition content and alleged that its actions were benefiting the ruling BJP.On X, the Congress youth wing claimed that its workers were hit with water cannon and drenched with âfilthyâ water during the demonstration. It accused the government of using force against protesters demanding freedom of expression. A few supporters were detained by police but were later released, according to a Reuters witness.Meta has maintained that it restricts content in India in accordance with local laws. The company has not publicly commented on the protests. However, during a closed-door meeting with Congress, it conveyed that it remained neutral towards all political parties, according to people familiar with the matter.Congress has argued that the restrictions could put it at a disadvantage ahead of state elections next year, when Facebook and Instagram are expected to play a key role in political campaigning.

World.title: A wall across the sea: Inside Gujarat's ambitious Kalpasar project
World.content:
Gujarat is planning to build a 60.13-km barrier across the Gulf of Khambhat to create a freshwater reservoir

What exactly is Gujarat planning to build?

Government's fresh push and the Netherlands connection

What Gujarat stands to gain from Kalpasar

Can the Gulf of Khambhat be turned into a freshwater reservoir?

A freshwater dream, but at what cost to the sea?

Kalpasar's biggest test: Turning ambition into reality

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Imagine building a massive wall across the sea, stretching for kilometres, with powerful tides crashing against it, strong ocean winds sweeping across its surface and an entire marine ecosystem thriving beneath it. Now imagine turning the vast stretch of seawater trapped behind that wall into a freshwater reservoir.What sounds like an extraordinary engineering challenge is at the heart of Gujarat's ambitious Kalpasar project, which proposes building a dam across the Gulf of Khambhat. But can such a massive structure withstand the forces of the sea, and what happens to the marine ecosystem when nature's tidal movements are restricted?The proposed Kalpasar project envisages constructing a 60.13-km-long barrier, including a 26.7-km stretch across the Gulf of Khambhat, to create a freshwater reservoir spread over approximately 1,600 square kilometres.The project aims to use runoff from the Sabarmati, Mahi and Dhadhar rivers, supplemented by water conveyed from the Narmada, while also developing road and rail connectivity across the structure.With an estimated cost of Rs 1.33 lakh crore in a 2026 project filing, it is among Gujarat's most ambitious infrastructure proposals.However, turning a tidal stretch of the Arabian Sea into a freshwater reservoir presents a complex set of engineering, hydrological and environmental challenges.The Kalpasar project is not simply a conventional dam built across a river. It envisages a massive barrier across the Gulf of Khambhat, creating an enclosed water body that would eventually function as a freshwater reservoir.The proposed structure is designed to incorporate water-regulating mechanisms to control the movement of water into and out of the reservoir.River water flowing into the enclosed area would gradually help replace the saline water, while regulators would play a crucial role in managing water levels and preventing unwanted seawater ingress.The project also envisages a road and rail corridor along the barrier, potentially connecting the Saurashtra region with mainland Gujarat. This makes Kalpasar a combination of water-storage infrastructure and a major transport project.However, the exact engineering configuration, including the regulator design, construction methodology and operational arrangements, needs to be established from the latest detailed project report rather than assumed from earlier proposals.After decades of studies and delays, the Gujarat government has renewed efforts to move the Kalpasar project towards implementation, turning to the Netherlands for technical expertise in tackling the engineering challenges of building a massive barrier across the sea.The project gained fresh momentum during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to the Netherlands in May 2026, when India and the Netherlands signed a Letter of Intent on technical cooperation.PM Modi also visited the Dutch Afsluitdijk, a 32-km-long barrier that separates the Wadden Sea from the freshwater IJsselmeer lake, to understand the country's experience in water management and coastal engineering.The collaboration took a further step on September 24, 2026, when the central water commission, Gujarat's Kalpasar department and Dutch knowledge institutions Deltares and Delft University of Technology (TU Delft) signed two tripartite memoranda of understanding (MoUs).According to the ministry of jal shakti, the partnership will bring Dutch expertise in hydraulic and hydrological modelling, coastal and structural engineering, salinity management, sediment movement and climate resilience into the project's planning and design.A team of Indian officials had also visited the Netherlands in July to study flood-protection infrastructure, sluice and pumping systems, barrier technologies and ecological solutions.The Centre informed the Rajya Sabha on July 27 that the Detailed Project Report (DPR) was at an advanced stage of finalisation. The government has also proposed an integrated hybrid renewable energy capacity of around 2,470 MW on reclaimed land that is presently submerged during high tide, with the generated power intended to support, among other uses, the pumping of freshwater for irrigation in Saurashtra.The DPR is expected to incorporate engineering measures and salinity-management strategies to address the risk of seawater ingress.At the heart of the Kalpasar project is Gujarat's ambition to address the water needs of its drought-prone Saurashtra region.The proposed reservoir is expected to use runoff from the Sabarmati, Mahi and Dhadhar rivers, supplemented by water conveyed from the Narmada.The project envisages irrigation benefits across large parts of Saurashtra, where water scarcity has long affected agriculture and regional development. By providing an additional source of freshwater, the state hopes to reduce dependence on groundwater and existing water-transfer arrangements.However, Soumya Dutta, an environmentalist and co-convenor of the South Asian People's Action on Climate Crisis (SAPACC), questioned whether the water would actually reach farmers, citing the experience of the Sardar Sarovar project.âMost of the water from the Narmada has gone to industries rather than agriculture. Farmers in Saurashtra and Kutch have not received the water, while industries in Sanand and other areas have benefited from the supply,â Dutta told TOI.He argued that large water infrastructure projects have often been promoted in the name of farmers, while industries have also benefited from the resulting water supply. Citing the Sardar Sarovar project, he questioned whether Kalpasar would deliver on its stated promise of providing water to agricultural communities.Beyond water security, Kalpasar is also being projected as a major connectivity and energy infrastructure project.The proposed road and railway links across the gulf could significantly reduce travel distances between Saurashtra and mainland Gujarat, improving access to markets and industrial centres.According to the Centre, the proposed corridor could reduce the travel distance between Bhavnagar and Surat by approximately 179 km, from 356 km to 177 km.The project also envisages around 2,470 MW of hybrid renewable energy capacity, combining solar and wind power. Together, these components are intended to make Kalpasar more than a water-storage project, with the potential to reshape the region's agricultural, industrial and transport landscape.However, the extent to which these benefits can materialise will depend on the project's final design, water availability and economic viability.One of the biggest questions surrounding Kalpasar is how the government plans to convert a large stretch of seawater into a freshwater reservoir and maintain its quality over the long term.The proposed reservoir is expected to use runoff from the Sabarmati, Mahi and Dhadhar rivers, supplemented by water conveyed from the Narmada. However, the challenge lies in gradually flushing out the seawater trapped within the enclosed area and preventing salinity from returning.The process would depend on the volume of freshwater entering the reservoir, the efficiency of water regulators, seepage through the seabed and barrier, and evaporation. The balance between freshwater inflows and saline water entering the reservoir would be crucial in determining how much usable water can ultimately be stored.Dutta warned that restricting freshwater flows could also increase the risk of saline water entering coastal land and groundwater, potentially affecting agricultural fields and freshwater sources."Freshwater flow from upstream creates pressure underground and keeps saline water from moving inland. But if you stop the freshwater flow, the saline water has higher pressure and saline intrusion takes place," he said.Citing a study he said he had conducted downstream of the Sardar Sarovar Dam on the Narmada, Dutta said freshwater wells in areas around Bharuch had become more saline after the flow of freshwater declined.He warned that a similar situation could emerge around the proposed Kalpasar project, affecting not just agricultural land but also freshwater wells, tube wells, ponds and other water bodies.Water quality is another concern. Rivers feeding the proposed reservoir pass through several urban and industrial areas, raising questions about pollution and the suitability of their water for drinking and irrigation. The government would also need to account for seasonal variations in river flows, particularly during years of weak monsoons, when freshwater availability could decline.Dutta also flagged the possibility of pollutants accumulating within the enclosed reservoir instead of being carried out to sea."Instead of letting it flow out into the sea and spread over a much larger area, you are creating a much smaller enclosed water body where pollution and toxic substances will accumulate," he said.The proposed reservoir's storage capacity alone, therefore, would not determine its usefulness. Its long-term success would depend on whether the project can maintain acceptable salinity levels and ensure a reliable supply of freshwater for Saurashtra's drinking, agricultural and industrial needs.While the Kalpasar project promises to transform Gujarat's water security, restricting the natural movement of seawater across the Gulf of Khambhat could have far-reaching ecological consequences.The gulf is a dynamic marine environment where powerful tidal movements regulate water circulation, sediment transport and the health of coastal habitats. Altering these natural processes through a massive barrier could change the ecological conditions that sustain marine life along the coastline.One of the major concerns is the potential impact on marine biodiversity. Changes in tidal patterns and salinity could affect fish migration, breeding grounds and the availability of suitable habitats for marine organisms.Dutta warned that restricting the natural exchange of freshwater and seawater could disrupt the ecological balance of the gulf, affecting the variety of marine life it supports."If you are blocking that, you are keeping one part as freshwater ecology and isolating the saline-water ecology. The mixing and the variety of life goes down," he said.He explained that estuaries support different forms of biological life because they contain varying levels of salinity, ranging from freshwater to brackish and more saline conditions. Restricting this natural mixing, he argued, could reduce the diversity of life sustained by these interconnected ecosystems.Mangroves and intertidal mudflats along the gulf could also be affected by changes in water levels, sediment deposition and the natural exchange of seawater. These ecosystems play an important role in supporting coastal biodiversity and protecting shorelines.The movement of sediment is another critical factor. The Gulf of Khambhat receives sediment from several rivers, while its strong tidal currents redistribute it across the coastline.Restricting this circulation could alter sediment deposition, potentially changing coastal erosion patterns and affecting nearby estuaries and wetlands. The extent and location of these changes would need to be established through detailed hydrodynamic and sediment modelling.The potential consequences could extend beyond the marine ecosystem to fishing communities dependent on the gulf.Changes in fish habitats, breeding cycles and fishing grounds could affect fish availability and traditional livelihoods. The project's environmental assessment will therefore need to examine not just the immediate area around the proposed barrier but also its wider impact on the gulf and surrounding coastline.Questioning the economic and environmental rationale behind such a massive infrastructure project, Dutta argued that decentralised water-storage systems closer to agricultural areas could offer a less expensive alternative."Creating a network of distributed water storage and distribution systems would have been far less expensive and far less destructive," he said.He suggested that such systems could be managed through local institutions, including gram panchayats and zila parishads, giving communities greater control over water distribution.He also pointed out that since the proposed reservoir would be located downstream, water would have to be pumped to farms further inland, adding to the project's energy requirements and operational costs.Despite renewed government efforts and technical cooperation with the Netherlands, the Kalpasar project faces several hurdles before it can move towards implementation.The final Detailed Project Report will be crucial in establishing the project's engineering design, construction methodology, water-management mechanisms, financial requirements and long-term operational costs.The project will also require the necessary environmental and statutory clearances, backed by detailed assessments of its impact on marine biodiversity, coastal ecosystems, fisheries and surrounding communities.With an estimated cost of Rs 1.33 lakh crore in a project filing submitted in May 2026, it is among Gujarat's most ambitious infrastructure proposals.Ultimately, Kalpasar's viability will depend on whether Gujarat can overcome the engineering challenges of constructing a massive barrier across a tidal gulf, maintain a dependable freshwater supply and address the environmental risks.For now, the project represents an ambitious attempt to reshape the Gulf of Khambhat, but translating that vision into reality will require scientific evidence, technical certainty and careful environmental assessment.

World.title: JD(U) extends full support to delimitation, women's reservation proposals
World.content:
The Janata Dal (United) on Saturday announced its full support for the proposed Constitution amendment bills on delimitation and women's reservation, calling them a significant step towards strengthening Indian democracy.

In a post on X, JD(U) working president Sanjay Kumar Jha said the proposal envisages a 50 per cent increase in the existing strength of the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies, while paving the way for 33 per cent reservation for women in these bodies.

"The Janata Dal (United) fully supports this proposal," Jha said, describing it as an important initiative to expand Indian democracy.

He said the proposed increase in the number of seats would broaden people's representation and create greater opportunities for women's participation in the decision-making process, reported by news agency PTI.



Jha also urged political parties to set aside their differences and extend support to the bills, calling for a constructive role in ensuring their passage in parliament through a broad consensus.

Meanwhile, the BJP-led Centre is preparing to introduce a fresh constitution amendment bill in the Lok Sabha on Monday.

The legislation seeks to implement 33 per cent reservation for women by increasing the number of seats in the Lok Sabha, state assemblies and Union Territory legislatures by 50 per cent.





It also proposes to freeze the revised seat allocations and constituency boundaries until 2051.

The constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, proposes to increase the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from its existing limit to 850 members. This would include up to 815 representatives from states and 35 from Union territories.

The legislation also seeks to raise the maximum strength of state legislative assemblies from 500 to 650 members.

According to the bill's statement of objects and reasons, the proposed changes aim to implement one-third reservation for women, including those belonging to scheduled castes (SCs) and scheduled tribes (STs), in the Lok Sabha and state and union territory legislative assemblies through a delimitation exercise.

World.title: President Murmu clears key procedural step for tabling of revised Delimitation Bill in Parliament
World.content:
NEW DELHI: President

on Saturday recommended that the Lok Sabha consider the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, under Article 117(3) of the Constitution, completing a key procedural requirement ahead of Parliament's sitting beginning November 30.

According to a Lok Sabha Secretariat bulletin, the recommendation followed a communication sent on November 27 by Union minister of state for law and justice and parliamentary affairs Arjun Ram Meghwal to the Lok Sabha secretary-general.

Article 117(3) requires the President's recommendation before either House of Parliament can pass a Bill that, if enacted and brought into operation, would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India.

The development comes a day after the Union Cabinet approved a revised legislative package comprising the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, and the accompanying Union Territories Laws Amendment Bill.

The government is expected to withdraw the pending Bills introduced in April, which failed to secure passage after the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha, and introduce the revised drafts on Monday.





Revised package proposes 50% increase in seats

The revised package proposes a uniform 50 per cent increase in the number of Lok Sabha and state Assembly seats across states and Union Territories.

Under the proposal, the Lok Sabha's maximum strength would increase from 550 to 850, while the maximum strength of state Assemblies would rise from 500 to 650.

The package also proposes redrawing constituencies within each state based on the latest published Census figures, which would be the 2011 Census, rather than waiting for the 2026-27 Census.

The distribution of seats among states would remain frozen until 2051.

Another key provision concerns the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state Assemblies. The proposed Delimitation Commission would redraw constituency boundaries in time for the quota to take effect ahead of the 2029 general elections.

The Lok Sabha is scheduled to meet from November 30 to December 3, while the Rajya Sabha will reconvene separately on December 2.

The revised Bills are expected to be introduced during the sitting, replacing the legislative proposals that failed to clear the Lok Sabha in April.

The earlier Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill sought to expand the strength of the Lok Sabha and facilitate the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures. It failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the House.

World.title: Flex boards backing Shafi Parambil surface in Oommen Chandy’s home turf Puthuppally
World.content:
Notwithstanding a directive from the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) against public statements and activities that could trigger factional disputes, the war of words over the political legacy of late Chief Minister Oommen Chandy is showing no signs of abating.

In a significant development, flex boards backing Shafi Parambil, regarded as a contender for the KPCC president’s post, surfaced in Puthuppally on Saturday, adding a new twist to the factional battle.

The boards feature Mr. Parambil standing alongside Oommen Chandy, with the inscription ‘Oommen Chandy School of Politics’. They also carry the message, ‘Continuing to move forward, having won the hearts of the people’, along with the Congress symbol.

Similar boards backing Mr. Parambil, Vadakara MP, have appeared in various parts of the State following senior Congress leader Rajmohan Unnithan’s recent criticism of him. Their appearance in Puthuppally, however, assumes particular significance, as the constituency, now represented by Chandy Oommen, is the home turf of his late father and ‘A’ group patriarch Oommen Chandy.

Frosty relationship

Family members of the late leader, including his wife Mariyamma Oommen, had publicly endorsed Mr. Unnithan’s remarks against Mr. Parambil. The boards, which appear to be aimed at countering the criticism, could place Chandy Oommen, the late leader’s son and a sitting legislator, in a politically awkward position. The ‘A’ group is already on the defensive following the family’s support for Mr. Unnithan’s comments.

Another significant aspect is the strained relationship between Chandy Oommen and the faction associated with Mr. Parambil. “Since the beginning of his political career in the Congress, Mr. Oommen has maintained a distance from the group comprising Mr. Parambil and Rahul Mamkootathil. Though Mr. Mamkootathil is no longer with the Congress, the distance between Chandy Oommen and Mr. Parambil persists. The latest development is likely to sharpen the confrontation between factions backing the two leaders,” a leader said.

World.title: Plan approach paper reflects Keralam UDF govt.’s Sangh Parivar agenda: Pinarayi Vijayan
World.content:
The recently-published approach paper for Keralam’s 15th Five-Year Plan reflects a “Sangh Parivar agenda” and signals the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government’s intention to surrender public wealth to market forces and corporates, Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan said here on Saturday (November 28, 2026).

Addressing a press conference here, Mr. Vijayan demanded the UDF government to withdraw the approach paper as it signals the destruction of the achievements made by Keralam. The UDF should clarify whether the approach paper reflects its politics and also whether the UDF as a whole approves of the document, he said.

Shift in focus

The paper, in effect, writes the obituary for people’s development on which Keralam has so far placed emphasis, Mr. Vijayan said. “The approach paper signals a complete withdrawal from a focus on social development and welfare and offers market forces and corporates the opportunity to plunder the State’s resources,” he said.

The plan process itself is being surrendered to the private sector. This would push the ordinary people, who should be lifted up as a result of the planning, to the margins. While the Centre replaced the Planning Commission with the NITI Aayog, the UDF government in Keralam is confining the State Planning Board to the role of an advisory panel.

“The UDF government in the State has surrendered to the BJP and the Central government. Keralam has a non-BJP government that implements BJP policy. In such a situation, the national leadership of the Congress party should explain whether this is the right approach,” he said.

Allocations

With emphasis on pleasing the private sector and corporates, the allocations to agriculture, social justice, welfare of scheduled castes, scheduled tribes, minorities and backward classes, health and education will be drastically cut, the Opposition leader said.

Also Read : KPCC steps in to quell infighting over ‘A group’ and Oommen Chandy’s political legacy in Keralam

Mr. Vijayan also slammed the approach paper proposal on small modular reactors as an option for nuclear energy generation in the long run. “Successive governments have, on various occasions, said no to this proposal. It (the approach paper proposal) will have serious implications,” he said.

World.title: Defence objects to admission of documents in Abhimanyu murder trial
World.content:
The defence raised an objection during the trial of the case related to the murder of Abhimanyu, a Students’ Federation of India (SFI) activist of Maharaja’s College, under way at the Ernakulam District and Sessions Court contending that it had not been provided copies of certain documents produced by the prosecution.

The defence argued that copies of the investigating officer’s application seeking the appointment of a tahsildar to conduct an identification parade and the District Collector’s order appointing the official had not been furnished to it. It further contended that these documents were not included in the list of material records.

Examination of witnesses

The objection was raised by advocates B. Raman Pillai and Anil Mohammed during the examination of the then Kanayannur tahsildar as a witness. Subsequently, copies of the documents were provided to the defence. The defence also demanded that the records should not be admitted as evidence since they were neither included in the list of documents nor supplied to the accused earlier. The examination of witnesses will continue on November 30.

The Kerala High Court had upheld the Ernakulam District and Sessions Court’s decision denying a plea for in-camera proceedings by the accused in the Abhimanyu murder case.

The case

Abhimanyu, a second-year BSc Chemistry student and SFI college unit secretary, was fatally stabbed on July 2, 2018, during clashes between activists of the SFI and the Campus Front, the student wing of the Popular Front of India (PFI), reportedly following a dispute over graffiti. The murder triggered widespread protests and reignited debate over political violence on college campuses.

The trial in the Abhimanyu murder case has been proceeding without interruption before the Ernakulam Principal Sessions Court since October 15, after the Kerala High Court in July directed that it be completed within four months, acting on a petition filed by Abhimanyu’s mother, Bhoopathy. Principal Sessions Judge K.K. Balakrishnan is presiding over the trial, while G. Mohanraj is appearing as the Special Public Prosecutor.

World.title: Bird flu: Animal Husbandry Department tightens preventive measures in Coimbatore
World.content:
The Animal Husbandry Department has stepped up preventive measures in Coimbatore district after H5N1 (avian influenza) was confirmed in a dead pond heron found along Sanganur stream at Siddhapudur. ICAR–National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) confirmed bird flu in a sample from the bird.

The Forest Department and local bodies have been requested to alert the Animal Husbandry Department in the event of death of birds in unusual circumstances. The department has put up 12 checkpoints at inter-State border as a preventive measure. Veterinary doctors have been instructed to visit farms in person and carry out inspections.

Likewise, the department will also keep a tab on the health of migratory birds at waterbodies, Regional Joint Director of Animal Husbandry Department Chitra said. Poultry farmers have been instructed to immediately report any unusual bird deaths or disease symptoms to the department, she said.

In the city limits, the department is coordinating with the Coimbatore Corporation to maintain and strengthen biosecurity measures.

World.title: Rare cancer diagnosed in infancy: 5.5-month-old undergoes limb-saving surgery
World.content:
In a challenging medical procedure, doctors have successfully performed limb-saving surgery on a 5.5-month-old girl diagnosed with a rare form of soft-tissue cancer, infantile fibrosarcoma. The surgery helped preserve the baby’s left leg, which was at risk of amputation due to extensive tumour involvement.

The procedure was performed at Manipal Hospital, Old Airport Road, where the infant was treated under the hospital’s Limb Saving Programme after months of chemotherapy and consultations with multiple medical teams.

Cancer detected shortly after birth

Born on April 1, 2026, the infant was admitted to intensive care within hours of birth due to infections. During her recovery, her mother noticed a small lump below her left knee. Subsequent investigations confirmed infantile fibrosarcoma, a rare cancer that primarily affects infants.

Chemotherapy was initiated on the 11th day after her birth, despite her fragile health. Over the following months, the baby experienced multiple complications, requiring prolonged intensive care and tube feeding.

After three months of chemotherapy, the tumour began to shrink. However, its extensive involvement of vital structures in the leg posed a significant challenge, with amputation emerging as a likely treatment option. The family subsequently approached the hospital, where the case was taken up by the team led by Srimanth B.S., lead consultant, Orthopaedic Oncosurgery.

Rare soft-tissue tumour

Explaining the complexities of the case, Dr. Srimanth said infantile fibrosarcoma generally develops during the first year of life. Although it can grow rapidly and affect surrounding tissues, its spread to distant organs is uncommon.

He said advances in chemotherapy and molecular testing had expanded treatment options for such cancers. Identification of genetic alterations, including NTRK gene fusions, could help doctors use targeted medicines to shrink tumours and make limb-preserving surgery possible in selected cases.

The surgery presented several challenges, as doctors had to remove the tumour completely while preserving the nerves and blood vessels essential for the functioning of the leg. Complicating matters further, only one of the three major arteries supplying blood to the lower leg remained functional.

Using high-resolution imaging, surgical magnification and microsurgical techniques, the team successfully removed the tumour while preserving the critical structures and maintaining blood supply to the limb.

Challenges in the surgery

Prashant Puranik, lead consultant, Reconstructive Oncology and Microsurgery, said performing limb-saving surgery on an infant of four to five months was particularly challenging, given the risks associated with the child’s age, previous chemotherapy and neonatal complications. Preserving the nerves and blood vessels, while minimising blood loss and operating time, was crucial. The paediatric anaesthesiology team played a key role in managing the high-risk procedure.

The baby was discharged four days after the procedure. A subsequent histopathological examination confirmed clear surgical margins, indicating that the tumour had been completely removed.

She is currently under regular medical follow-up, with doctors monitoring her growth, limb function and development, besides keeping watch for any signs of tumour recurrence.

World.title: Six hero stones dating to Vijayanagara period discovered in Doddaballapura
World.content:
Six hero stones dating back to the Vijayanagara period (15th or 16th century) have been discovered in Linganahalli in Doddaballapura, about 40 km away from Bengaluru, by officials of the Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage. According to the officials, they were found dumped on the premises of a private multinational company and had remained unnoticed for many years due to a lack of awareness and information among people.

Speaking to The Hindu, M. Kavyashree, Deputy Director, Bengaluru division, Department of Archaeology, said, “These hero stones were dumped on a private property. When the department heard the information from locals in the village, we rushed and spoke to the property manager. After they agreed, all six stones were recovered and carried in a tractor as they are huge. They have been temporarily installed at a nearby Muzrai Department temple. We will soon install a board and a fence to protect them.”

Elaborating on how they differentiate between hero stones dating back to the Vijayanagara period and other periods, she said, “We differentiate them on the basis of attire, weapons, ornaments, style of the carving on rough stone, etc. In these stones, the warriors to whom these hero stones are dedicated are wearing headgear, holding daggers, bows and arrows. The top knot of the turban is pointed towards the right, with big earlobes wearing huge earrings. There is also a dagger at one of the warrior’s waists in one of these hero stones. The thighs of the warriors carved on the stone are bigger in comparison to the hero stones of the Chalukya or Kadamba period.”

She further highlighted that three out of the six hero stones have devakanne or celestial maidens. “These devakannes or maidens escorted warriors to the heavens after they died fighting in wars. Hero stones depict the afterlife journey of warriors,” she added.

Ms. Kavyashree said that such stones should be preserved not just to commemorate the warriors they are dedicated to, but because they also provide valuable insights into the cultural and social fabric of society, religious practices of those times, and the clothes and ornaments that warriors or devakannes (celestial maidens) wore.

World.title: Consumer organisations seek passenger-friendly changes to railway reservation rules
World.content:
Two consumer organisations have urged the Railway Board to review the recently introduced reservation rules and procedures and adopt measures to protect the interests of passengers, particularly senior citizens and those with limited digital access.

In a representation dated November 28, the Southern Railway Users’ Federation of Tamil Nadu and Puducherry and Citizens’ Voice Coimbatore (CVC) welcomed measures to prevent misuse of the reservation system but said the changes should not inconvenience genuine passengers.

They sought continued access to opening-day reservations through Passenger Reservation System (PRS) counters and a compassionate refund mechanism for cancellations due to emergencies such as hospitalisation, death of a close family member and natural calamities. They proposed a refund of 25% to 40% of the fare for verified cancellations made up to two hours before departure.

The organisations also sought prominent display of chart-preparation timings and SMS alerts on final reservation status. To prevent confusion over journeys booked around midnight, they suggested an additional confirmation mechanism displaying the actual date and day of departure.

On Reservation Against Cancellation (RAC) fares, they proposed charging passengers the reserved seating fare initially and collecting an additional berth charge of about ₹85 only from those subsequently allotted exclusive berths. They also sought affordable reserved seating facilities if RAC was discontinued.

The representation further called for periodic reviews of reservation policies based on passenger feedback, booking trends, waiting-list movements and cancellation patterns. It was addressed to the Union Railway Minister and the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Railway Board.

World.title: Right to protest: Many detained as demand grows to scrap Freedom Park restriction in Bengaluru
World.content:
Over 200 protesters who attempted to march from Maurya Circle towards the Vidhana Soudha on Saturday (November 28) were detained by the Bengaluru City Police, as civil society groups stepped up their demand for the withdrawal of the 2021 police order restricting protests in the city to Freedom Park.

The march, organised by Horatada Hakkigaagi Janandolana (Campaign for the Right to Protest), was also held in solidarity with Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs), who have begun an indefinite strike demanding a monthly pay of ₹15,000. Defying the restrictions, the protesters sought to assert their right to protest at any site of injustice or outside the office of the authority concerned, rather than being confined to a designated protest venue.

The campaign has been demanding that the Karnataka government withdraw the 2021 order and restore the earlier 2009 order, which did not restrict demonstrations to a single venue.

Activists argue that the restrictions prevent people from taking their problems directly to the authorities responsible for addressing them. They have also argued that the 2021 restrictions were imposed through a State government order, and not mandated by the High Court, leaving the government free to withdraw or amend them.

The march brought together trade unions, Dalit organisations, groups representing slum residents, student unions, women’s rights organisations, environmental groups, and other progressive organisations. Their representatives underlined how restricting protests to Freedom Park could render struggles over everyday issues ineffective by preventing people from taking their demands to the places where decisions are made.

For residents of slums, the Slum Janara Sanghatane said, it made little sense to be confined to Freedom Park when demanding the repair of a borewell or resisting a sudden and unlawful eviction. Similarly, Fridays for Future and the Bangalore Environment Forum argued that opposition to the proposed Hebbal short tunnel required residents to be able to mobilise at the site where the project was to come up.

The trade unions said the right to protest had been central to their struggles against contractualisation, for the regularisation of workers and for fair wages. The All India Central Council of Trade Unions (AICCTU) said such demands would not have reached the government without sustained street agitations.

The Congress leadership’s decision to march beyond Jantar Mantar during its protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Delhi was cited by protesters in Bengaluru to question the party’s position on the right to protest. They asked why the Congress could take its protest beyond a designated site in Delhi, while its government in Karnataka continued to restrict demonstrations to Freedom Park. The protesters said the government could not apply “double standards”.

World.title: ‘Beacon of light’: PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir speak with astronaut Zeeshan Ali aboard China’s space station
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir held a phone call on Saturday with Pakistani astronaut Zeeshan Ali, who is aboard the Shenzhou-24 mission .

On Wednesday, Ali became the first Pakistani in orbit and also the first foreign astronaut to board China’s Tiangong space station, marking a historic milestone in Pakistan’s space ambitions and Beijing’s efforts to expand its space diplomacy.

On Saturday, the premier and the military chief spoke with Ali from the headquarters of the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (Suparco) in Islamabad.

Speaking first during the call, which was aired on media channels, PM Shehbaz noted he was accompanied by CDF Munir, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and China’s Ambassador Jiang Zaidong.

“Zeeshan, today is a great day for all of us sitting here and 240 million people of Pakistan, and I extend my warmest felicitations to you on becoming the first Pakistani astronaut to orbit the Earth,” the premier told the astronaut, asking him to also convey his warm greetings to the Chinese crewmates.

Reciting a couplet of Allama Iqbal, he said: “My dear Wing Commander Zeeshan, your success has ignited a renewed spirit of ambition in a generation eager to push boundaries, explore new frontiers, and take our nation to greater heights through hard work, sincerity of purpose, untiring efforts, and unwavering determination.”

Speaking next, CDF Munir told Ali: “We are really proud of you and proud of the armed forces that one of us has gone into space and achieved this great accomplishment.”

The field marshal said Ali’s presence aboard China’s space station was a “proud testament to our time-tested strategic partnership”.

“Truly, our friendship with China is beyond compare. And we always say higher than the Himalayas, deeper than the oceans, sweeter than the honey, and now boundless as the universe,” CDF Munir remarked.

Responding to them, Ali said it was a great honour for him to “represent Pakistan 400 kilometres above the Earth, orbiting at 7.9 kilometres per second; to represent Pakistan not only as the first astronaut to orbit the Earth, but [also as] the first international astronaut to enter the Chinese space station”.

“I am truly grateful for your kind words and the good wishes of the entire nation. Everything is going very well over here and according to the plan,” the astronaut added.

The payload specialist affirmed he was doing his best to perform his “duties and the scientific research work as per the expectations of the entire nation”.

Speaking again, PM Shehbaz remarked that while Islamabad’s ties with Beijing were already described as “higher than the Himalayas and deeper than the ocean”, they have now “soared beyond the skies”.

“This landmark mission comes as our two great countries celebrate 75 years of our diplomatic relations; what could be a more befitting tribute for this enduring friendship?” the prime minister said.

He extended his gratitude to China’s President Xi Jinping, noting his “leadership and steadfast commitment to Pakistan-China friendship have taken our all-weather strategic cooperative partnership to unprecedented heights”.

“Our iron brother China has given Pakistan the honour of being the first foreign partner in its space programme. This unparalleled gesture shall forever remain etched in the hearts and minds of the people of Pakistan,” the premier highlighted, saying “Thank you, China” in Chinese.

‘Excel in science and technology,’ Ali tells youth

In remarks addressed to the Pakistani youth, Ali urged them to “promote education and to excel in science and technology”.

“I hope that the next generation of astronauts, engineers, and scientists will travel even farther into space and explore further for the betterment of humanity.”

The astronaut then also thanked President Xi for sending a “congratulatory note exclusively for us at the Tiangong space station for the successful launch of this joint flight mission of Shenzhou-24”.

PM Shehbaz hailed Ali’s “extremely sincere and enthusiastic words”, asserting that his message would serve as a beacon of light for Pakistan’s youth and “breathe a new spirit into the promotion of science and technology among them”.

The prime minister then extended his congratulations to the Suparco chairman and his team, as well as the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) and its members.

PM Shehbaz further said Ali represented the “beginning of Pakistan’s manned missions into space”.

“The knowledge you bring back will open a very important chapter in Pakistan’s pursuit of excellence in science and technology and other related fields.”

The premier also noted emphasised Pakistan’s belief that the “outer space should serve peaceful purposes and the collective well-being of the entire humanity around the globe”.

“The experiments you are conducting alongside your talented Chinese brothers are not just for Pakistan; they will enrich the collective scientific knowledge of the international community,” he emphasised.

The prime minister wished the astronaut best of health throughout his stay in space and a safe and sound return home.

“Please convey to your Chinese brother astronauts the warmest wishes of the people of Pakistan for their good health as well as the success of this wonderful mission. The entire Pakistani nation is eagerly awaiting your safe return home after your great success story.”

Experiments planned onboard Tiangong

The 40-year-old pilot, who is the first Pakistani in orbit , is working as a payload specialist and is set to stay at the station for 5 to 10 days. He also learnt Chinese songs and poetry, practised calligraphy and played table tennis.

Reaching the Tiangong space station on Wednesday, the Shenzhou-24 crew — comprising Chinese commander Tang Hongbo, flight engineer Wu Yi and Ali — was greeted with hugs by the three astronauts of the Shenzhou-23 mission already aboard the station.

“As the first foreign crew member to board the China Space Station, I am incredibly excited. China Space Station here I come!” said Ali in Chinese, according to Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.

The spacecraft had docked with Tiangong three hours and 38 minutes after a Long March-2F rocket carrying it lifted off from China’s Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre at 8:18am Beijing time (5:18am Pakistan time) under a pink sky.

The spacecraft separated from the carrier rocket about 10 minutes after liftoff and entered orbit, the Chinese space agency said. According to Suparco, docking took place at 11:56am Beijing time (8:56am Pakistan time).

During the mission, Pakistani scientific payloads will be deployed in the Wentian and Mengtian laboratories aboard the Tiangong station, according to Suparco.

The experiments include cultivating microalgae as a potential source of food and oxygen for future space missions and studying the effects of spaceflight on quinoa seeds.

The CMSA said the crew would conduct around 90 experiments during the mission. Its objectives also include an orbital rotation with the Shenzhou-23 crew, routine operations and maintenance of the station, and further space science research involving various payloads.

‘Carrying hopes of 250m Pakistanis’

In April, Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud were chosen from Pakistan to start training in China.

Suparco and CMSA signed a cooperation agreement in February 2025, under which two Pakistanis were to train in China, with one joining a mission on the Tiangong space station operated by Beijing.

Eventually, Ali was chosen to join the Chinese mission.

Speaking at a press briefing in Jiayuguan on Tuesday, Ali said he was “deeply grateful” to the Chinese government for helping “us realise our dream of going into space”.

He said he arrived at the Astronaut Centre of China a few months ago, carrying with him the hopes of 250 million Pakistani people.

Ali said he believed that “what comes after this flight matters more than the flight itself”.

“This mission is not a finish line; it is a launch pad. And I hope the next chapter of China-Pakistan space cooperation will grow from one astronaut, one flight to multiple joint flights, to the Moon, Mars and beyond.”

On Wednesday, PM Shehbaz congratulated the nation on Ali’s departure for the Tiangong space station, saying Pakistan had begun its journey “beyond the stars”.

He described the mission as a journey not just for one astronaut but for 240m Pakistanis, particularly the younger generation and scientists.

World.title: Bilawal recalls past differences between PPP and PML-N, says elders learned from their 'mistakes'
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Saturday recalled past differences between his party and the PML-N over the discontinuation of projects initiated by each other, saying leaders from both sides had “learned from their mistakes”.

He made the remarks while addressing the foundation-laying ceremony of a Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation (SIUT) hospital in Rahim Yar Khan.

The Bhutto scion has been on a visit to Punjab for the past few days, touring multiple cities in the province’s south. Amid the ongoing debate on new provinces, he has stressed that the proposed south Punjab province had secured a political consensus through democratic means, with the Senate and the provincial assembly backing the idea.

Speaking on Saturday, Bilawal thanked Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for allowing federal funds to be channelled to the Sindh government at his request. He said the provincial government subsequently worked with SIUT to develop the project plan, thanking its founder Dr Adib Rizvi.

The PPP chairman emphasised the importance of ensuring continuity in development projects, irrespective of which government was in power, saying this was essential to serving the public.

Bilawal thanked Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz of the PML-N — which PPP supports in the Centre — for not creating hurdles in the project.

“If this project is moving forward, one reason is that the Punjab chief minister created no hurdles in it,” he said.

Bilawal stated that he wanted to continue the “same tradition” set by Maryam Nawaz of not obstructing projects initiated by other parties for the public good.

“We should also learn from the mistakes our elders made, and which they themselves have learned from. This was an issue between the PPP and the PML-N. Our elders initially made some mistakes, but later learned from them,” he said.

He recalled that in the past, the PPP would form a government only to be “ousted” a few months later, after which the PML-N would come to power and projects initiated by the PPP would come to a halt.

Similarly, Bilawal said, former prime minister Nawaz Sharif would be removed from office, allowing the PPP to return to power, whereupon it would focus on its own projects instead of continuing initiatives started by the previous PML-N government.

And the cycle would repeat, he added, noting that the public’s problems would continue to increase.

The Bhutto scion then recalled the 2006 Charter of Democracy that his mother Benazir signed with Nawaz, wherein they decided to accept each other’s mandate.

Bilawal went on to note that afterwards, PPP and PML-N did not conspire to bring down the other’s government nor halt the other party’s projects. He maintained that this was the only way to serve the public.

Bilawal urges avoiding ‘greatest injustice to the people’

Reiterating his stance that ordinary citizens wanted politicians to focus on issues such as rising inflation and unemployment, Bilawal stressed the need to ease the public’s financial hardships amid the ongoing economic crisis triggered by the conflict in the Middle East.

He again underscored the need to set aside political differences, “abandon the politics of political revenge”, and unite to solve people’s issues, as that is what the public expected.

The PPP chairman stressed that the government should make all decisions with mutual consensus and democratic and constitutional means.

“There are 24 hours in a day, and if in those 24 hours, you think ‘I have to target my political opponent, someone associated with another political party, that we must seek revenge against them’, then we will be doing the greatest injustice to the people of Pakistan.”

Responding to a query, Bilawal said he did not want to speak on politics as that would divert the attention away from the hospital project.

At the outset of his address, the PPP chairman contended that his efforts had always been aimed at providing world-class healthcare facilities to people at their doorstep.

He said the SIUT hospital will comprise two phases, with efforts to ensure that construction for the second phase begins as soon as the first is completed.

Explaining the contours of the hospital’s construction stages, Bilawal said the first phase would have 50 beds, with facilities for dialysis, lithotripsy and laboratory tests, including ultrasound and X-ray.

SIUT is a major tertiary care institution known for providing quality healthcare free of cost. In the Sindh government’s budget for this financial year, an estimated Rs250 million each were proposed for SIUT hospitals in Rahim Yar Khan, Gujjar Khan, Sargodha, Dera Ismail Khan and Kot Addu.

World.title: Death toll in Baloch Colony building collapse rises to 13 as rescuers recover four more bodies, locate fifth
World.content:
KARACHI: Rescue workers on Saturday recovered four more bodies from the rubble of a six-storey building that collapsed near Karachi’s Baloch Colony area and were in the process of recovering a fifth, taking the death toll to 13.

On Wednesday, three people were killed and 14 others injured when the under-construction building — reportedly being constructed illegally on a residential plot — collapsed. Another body was recovered on Thursday, taking the death toll to four. On Friday, four more bodies were recovered, taking the toll to eight.

Rescue 1122 spokesperson Hassaanul Haseeb Khan said that during the operation, one body was recovered at around 4:20am and two more were extricated from the debris around 8:30am. The fourth body was recovered in the afternoon.

A later rescue statement said that another body — the 13th in total — had been located in the debris and efforts to recover it were under way. Four bodies now remain missing.

Khan added that the rescue teams had now initiated “fast track” operations from all four sides. He said searching and debris removal operations had also been expedited.

He hoped that the operation would likely be completed on Saturday night and the team would extricate the remaining bodies from the debris.

Videos shared by Rescue 1122 from the site showed members of the Urban Search and Rescue team using heavy-duty bolt cutters to cut through rebar and recover bodies, while clearing rubble with various tools.

Commissioner’s office submits report to CM

The Karachi Commissioner’s Office has submitted a report to the chief minister on action taken against illegal and unauthorised buildings in the city, stating that 516 buildings have been sealed as part of an ongoing crackdown, as of Nov 27.

According to the report, action was taken against 262 buildings under construction in various districts. Of these, 158 were sealed, while notices were issued to 12 buildings. Construction work was found to have been halted at one site during an inspection.

In Korangi district, 41 of the 48 buildings were sealed, while notices were issued to seven. In Keamari, 12 of the 19 buildings were sealed and notices were issued to five, while construction work was found to have stopped at one site. The report also recorded 12 buildings in West, 21 in Malir, 64 in Central, 61 in South and 37 in East. Of these, eight buildings in Malir, five in Central, 55 in South and all 37 in East were sealed.

Karachi Commissioner Syed Hassan Naqvi has directed deputy commissioners to continue action against illegal and unauthorised constructions and ensure that those violating building regulations are dealt with in accordance with the law.

Man rescued alive after 54 hours

A day earlier, emergency services rescued a man alive from beneath the rubble, two days after the building collapsed.

Rescue 1122 said that 28-year-old Muhammad Adil was rescued alive from the rubble. It said that the search operation for any other individuals feared trapped was underway.

Khan termed the rescue a “breakthrough”. He added that rescue operations were ongoing to search for other survivors from the debris.

He said the rescued man told them that two other persons who might be alive were in touch with him. However, Khan said the rescuers conducted a search in the identified area but could not locate them.

Khan added that heavy machinery was also being used to remove debris, but that whenever a human body was spotted in the debris, the team stopped the machine operations and initiated manual work with extra care to recover the body.

Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah expressed gratitude that the man trapped under the rubble survived for 54 hours, describing it as a “miracle”, according to a statement issued from his office.

According to the statement, the chief minister directed rescue agencies and the Karachi commissioner to accelerate the ongoing rescue operation and deploy all available resources.

Murad also praised rescue workers for their tireless efforts and directed officials to ensure the survivor receives the best possible medical treatment.

Sindh Local Government Secretary Waseem Shamshad, who also served as director general of the Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA), was removed from both posts on Thursday on the directives of CM Murad following the incident.

The CM ordered sweeping action over the incident while chairing a high-level meeting, further issuing directives for the removal of East Deputy Commissioner Nasrullah Abbasi, as well as Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) East Zubair Sheikh, over “negligence”, a statement issued by the CM Office said.

In addition to the removal of the three officials, CM Murad further issued directives for the suspension of 16 SBCA officials and the initiation of an inquiry against them.

He directed the police to “immediately” arrest the building’s owner, Salman Tahir, and the builder, Zeeshan.

Moreover, he instructed that the building’s architect and structural engineer be included in the incident’s investigation to determine whether the construction complied with approved plans, building regulations and safety standards.

14 ‘illegal’ buildings in KAEHS to be demolished

The KDA’s Additional Deputy DG Farhan Kaiser visited the site on Thursday and told the media that their first priority was to remove the debris. He said that under the directions of the Sindh CM and LG minister, “illegal buildings” were being sealed across the metropolis.

He said that so far, 14 buildings had been sealed in the KAEHS after the building collapse and would be demolished in a second phase of the operation.

Kaiser added that it was the responsibility of the residents to report illegal buildings in their respective areas, and vowed to take action against the builders and owners of these buildings.

Members of the Chief Minister Inspection Team (CMIT), Bilal Memon and Anwar Shar, visited the scene and collected samples of the material used in the construction of the building for investigation purposes.

Rehabilitation secretary Rafiq Mustafa Shaikh, SBCA DG Abid Saleem, Rescue 1122 DG Brig. (retd) Wajid Sibghatullah Mahar and Rescue 1122 COO Dr Abid Jalaluddin Shaikh also visited the site and supervised the rescue operation.

FIR registered

A first information report (FIR) of the incident was registered at the Tipu Sultan police station on Wednesday, on the complaint of an official of the Sindh Local Government Department.

The FIR, seen by Dawn, invoked Sections 302 (intentional murder), 119 (public servant concealing design to commit offence), 427 (mischief causing damage), 337-H(1) (hurt caused by rash or negligent act), 109 (abetment) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code.

The building’s four owners — including Salman Tahir whose arrest the Sindh CM has ordered — its builder, architect, structural engineer and its contractors have been nominated in the FIR.

According to the FIR, the complainant alleged that poor-quality material was being used in the construction of the building. He claimed that the suspects, in collusion with the officials of various government departments, had been involved in constructing additional structures and not complying with the building’s approved plan.

This was why the building collapsed around 1pm, the complainant alleged.

Police have arrested four of the suspects, including one of the owners, Saad Tahir, and three contractors, who were produced before the judicial magistrate (south) today.

The judge granted police a five-day physical remand of the suspects.

World.title: CDA seals Fazl’s Islamabad residence after 'foreign' owner's CNIC cancelled
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Saturday sealed the Islamabad residence of Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman after the identity card of the property’s legal owner was cancelled.

The move comes amid continuing tensions between the JUI-F and the federal government.

A notice affixed on the property gate on Thursday said the building has been sealed by CDA’s Building & Housing Control “on account of cancellation of ownership”.

A CDA notice affixed on a gate of JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s residence in Islamabad on Nov 28, 2026. — via Kashif Abbasi

CDA’s Building & Housing Control swung into action a day after the deputy director for CDA’s Estate Management-I ordered sealing of the property due to the change of title being cancelled.

In an order dated Nov 27, the deputy director for CDA’s Estate Management-I noted that the owner, Amanullah, son of Muhammad Younus, had been “identified as a foreign national and his Pakistani Computerised National Identity Card (CNIC) had accordingly been cancelled”.

“In exercise of the powers delegated by the Authority to the member (Estate) and after consideration of the available record and observance of the prescribed process, the change of title granted in favour of Mr Aman Ullah s/o Muhammad Younas, […] has been CANCELLED with immediate effect,” read the order, available with Dawn.

It directed the director general of the CDA’s Building & Housing Control Department to seal the property, adding that he could seek assistance from CDA formations and the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) administration, if required.

“Consequential legal action shall be taken by Directorate of Estate Management-1,” it added.

The CDA order noted that the focal person for Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) Illegal Foreigners’ Repatriation Plan (IFRP), in a letter dated Nov 25, also confirmed the cancellation of Amanullah’s Pakistani CNIC “following verification by Nadra and requested initiation of appropriate legal proceedings in respect of immovable properties reportedly acquired by him in Islamabad”.

CDA highlighted that Amanullah had been given an opportunity of hearing as a show-cause notice was issued to him on Nov 25 to appear personally before the CDA member for Estate on Nov 26 and explain why the change of title in his favour should not be cancelled.

The CDA said Amanullah could not be found at the “subject property for personal service of the notice, whereupon the notice was duly pasted at the premises of the subject property” to communicate the proceedings to him.

However, Amanullah allegedly failed to appear before the CDA Estate member on Nov 26, nor “did he avail himself of the opportunity of hearing to rebut the allegations or produce any valid identity document or prior written permission of the competent government” for acquiring the property.

CDA had also issued notice against the same property on Oct 30 for placing a generator outside and for alleged illegal/unauthorised construction.

‘Violation of prescribed transfer requirements’

According to the CDA order, the matter regarding Amanullah’s nationality and identity credentials was brought to its notice through “official communications received from various government agencies”, including the Office of the District Magistrate, the focal person for IFRP, ICT and the National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra).

It noted that as per a Nadra letter, Amanullah had originally obtained his CNIC on the basis of his parents’ CNIC, whereas “discrepancies had been observed in the family record, including the existence of two CNICs of his late father, Muhammad Younas”.

The order said that subsequent verification by Nadra established that the identity document furnished by Amanullah “for the purpose of obtaining change of title in respect of the subject property was not a valid Pakistani CNIC and had been cancelled by the competent authority, thereby rendering the mandatory identity requirement for processing the change of title unfulfilled”.

It stated that under Chapter 6 of the CDA Property Manual, which requires producing a valid CNIC, furnishing an invalid identity document constituted a “material violation of the prescribed transfer requirements and vitiates the administrative process through which the change of title was obtained”.

The CDA also cited Section 3 of the Foreigners Act 1946, which empowers the government to regulate the acquisition of property by foreigners, stating that a 1984 order under it provided that no foreigner shall “acquire land or any interest in land or landed property in Pakistan except with the previous permission in writing of the federal government or of the provincial government”.

“No such permission has been produced or placed on the record of the Authority in respect of the subject property,” the order maintained.

Consequently, the CDA’s Estate Wing initiated proceedings to cancel the change of title granted in Amanullah’s favour, the document added.

Police deny arrest of Fazl’s son; workers in KP held

Separately, Islamabad police denied the JUI-F’s claim that Fazl’s son Maulana Asjad Mahmood had been arrested.

In a statement, a spokesperson for Islamabad police declared such reports circulating on social media as “baseless and false”.

“Islamabad police clarifies that neither has Maulana Asjad Mahmood been arrested, nor has any action been taken in this regard,” read the statement.

The police urged the public not to “believe rumours” and not to share unverified reports.

The clarification came hours after the JUI-F claimed that Asjad had been arrested.

In the late afternoon, Senator Kamran Murtaza had shared a picture, saying he was present with his lawyers at Pak Secretariat police station and alleging he was not being allowed to meet Fazl’s son.

Around 6pm, however, Murtaza posted that Asjad had been “released”.

In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Swabi, police detained several leaders and workers, including the party’s Vice President Maulana Fazli Ali and former provincial minister Ghafoor Khan Jadoon.

Spokesperson for the district police, Liaqat Ali, told Dawn that the arrested workers were confined in a police lockup.

JUI-F leaders had announced holding a protest at Karnal Sher Khan Chowk against the government’s actions, but were arrested before they could proceed.

Other arrested leaders included Swabi General Secretary Noorul Islam Khan, Information Secretary Qaiser Shah, Swabi Tehsil Emir Mufti Abdul Samad, Topi Tehsil Emir Maulana Taj Nabi Khan, General Secretary Javed, Razaar Tehsil Emir Maulana Anwar Zeb, Chhota Lahore Tehsil Emir Maulana Mushtaq Hussain, General Secretary Hafeezur Rehman and Advocate Rashid Sohail.

Further, a first information report (FIR) was lodged on Saturday regarding Jamia Qasimul Uloom in Multan, which named Fazl’s other son, Maulana Asad Mahmood.

In the FIR, the complainant alleged that Asad and others forcibly entered the building after the former was removed as the madrasah’s administrator.

The complainant alleged that Asad was “aggrieved” by the decision and “began interfering in the affairs of the madrasah through various persons and diverse channels”.

The complainant, the son of the new administrator, alleged that last night three people, Qari Moosa Sial, Qari Noorul Haq and Mufti Kaleemullah, entered the madrasah at the instigation of Asad and Mufti Aamir Mehmood and vandalised the premises.

According to Multan police, a dispute between “two parties concerning the administrative affairs and other matters” of the madrassah was under consideration in a court of law.

Police said that in the presence of the district administration, the officials “ensured compliance with the court orders and fulfilled all necessary legal requirements”.

“The Multan police clarifies that all operations are conducted within the scope of the law, without any discrimination. Citizens are advised to refrain from believing or spreading unverified reports,” police said.

The JUI-F had also claimed that scores of party activists and workers were arrested and booked across Punjab and KP on Thursday and Friday as the party staged protests at various locations.

One such first information report (FIR) was filed at Ghallanai police station in Mohmand district over a protest staged on Friday.

The party’s district chief Mufti Mohammad Arif Haqqani, 16 other leaders and more than 200 unidentified people were nominated in the case.

The FIR accused the protesters of blocking the main Peshawar-Bajaur Road to all kinds of traffic for nearly two hours.

Others named in the case included former Upper Mohmand nazim Hafiz Taj Wali, former Bazai nazim Maulana Bismillah Jan Rahimi, Arshad Bakhtiar, Qari Fazal Khaliq, Rohail Khan, Umairullah Khaksar, Maulana Gulab Noor, Samiullah and Qari Syed Alam Qari.

PPP condemns sealing of property

Meanwhile, PPP Secretary General Humayun Khan visited Fazl’s residence in Islamabad to express solidarity with the JUI-F chief. Speaking outside the residence, he said the manner in which the property was sealed and Maulana’s family evicted was inappropriate and condemnable, particularly the treatment of women and children.

Khan said PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari had directed him to visit the residence and express solidarity with the JUI-F chief. He urged Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to order an impartial inquiry into the matter, adding that Fazl was the head of a political party.

The senior PPP leader added that the country needed stability and urged the government to focus on the problems facing farmers and the underprivileged, particularly unemployment.

Fazl-govt rift

Fazl had criticised the Centre for imposing governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and making the then-PTI provincial government non-functional. The JUI-F chief also accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments despite his efforts to mediate between the PML-N and PTI governments.

Tensions escalated when Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights, resulting in the veteran politician and key federal ministers exchanging harsh remarks .

In recent weeks, PPP Chairman Bilawal-Bhutto Zardari — a key ally of the ruling PML-N — has voiced his support for Fazl and condemned the “government’s actions” against him.

Last week, police and Federal Constabulary (FC) personnel deployed to protect Fazl and other members of his family were withdrawn from the residences they guarded in Islamabad and Dera Ismail Khan.

A JUI-F spokesman had confirmed the withdrawal, alleging that Fazl’s Islamabad residence had been cordoned off by capital police and that security personnel had harassed visitors. He also claimed that the party’s Central Secretariat in Islamabad had been besieged by police.

An Islamabad police official, however, said only one police guard had been withdrawn.

The JUI-F chief’s son has also come under scrutiny from the anti-graft watchdog, with the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) summoning former federal communications minister Asad Mahmood over alleged irregularities in 4,252 appointments at Pakistan Post during his 2022-23 tenure. Mahmood skipped two consecutive summonses issued for Nov 10 and 14, according to a NAB source.

The JUI-F staged protests in parts of Sindh and Balochistan on Nov 7 against a “coordinated character assassination campaign” targeting Fazl.

Party leaders and workers condemned the alleged drone surveillance of his residence and the circulation of footage on social media, demanding an impartial investigation and action against those responsible.

On Tuesday, Fazl claimed he had been put under an hours-long “state siege” to prevent him from attending a multiparty conference hosted by the Lahore High Court Bar Association.

On Thursday, authorities barred the JUI-F chief and eight other leaders of his party from entering, residing or remaining in Sargodha — where the JUI-F planned to hold a rally that day — for 30 days. Despite the restriction, Fazl said in a video message that he was setting out for Sargodha.

The next day, hours after Fazl claimed that he was under arrest, Lahore Capital City Police Officer Bilal Siddique Kamyana denied that the politician had been taken into custody.

Additional input by Imran Gabol, Muqaddam Khan and Fauzee Khan Mohmand.

World.title: Indian police disperse protest outside Meta offices with water cannons
World.content:
Police in the northern Indian state of Haryana used water cannons to disperse activists from the main opposition Congress party protesting outside Meta’s offices over allegations that the company is censoring opposition voices.

Activists from the youth wing of the Congress party have staged massive protests outside Meta offices, accusing the company of acting in the interests of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party, in what has become one of the Facebook and Instagram parent’s biggest challenges in its largest market by users.

Meta says that it restricts content in India in accordance with local laws.

The company has not commented publicly on the protests, but in a closed-door meeting with Congress has conveyed that it remains neutral towards all political parties, according to people familiar with the matter.

The opposition party’s youth wing has sued Meta and the Indian government, seeking to strike down a rule that has sharply expanded content restrictions by requiring automated sweeps to remove copies of posts flagged in individual takedown orders.

Congress’ youth wing posted on X that its party activists were hit with water cannons and drenched with “filthy” water by police during a protest outside Meta’s office in Gurugram, accusing the government of using force against demonstrators demanding freedom of expression.

Police detained a few party supporters, but they were later released, a Reuters witness said.

Congress, the main opposition party to Modi’s government, says the content restrictions put it at a disadvantage ahead of state elections next year, when Facebook and Instagram are expected to be key campaigning platforms.

World.title: PTA says submarine cable fault fixed, internet services return to normal
World.content:
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) on Saturday announced the restoration of the SEA-ME-WE 5 (SMW5) international submarine cable system following the repair of a fault, saying internet services across the country had returned to normal.

On November 18, PTA said that a fault had been reported in the SEA-ME-WE 5 (SMW5) international submarine cable system, approximately 11 kilometres from Pakistan’s coast.

In a statement today, the regulator said the cable was now fully operational and the fault had been rectified through coordination between Transworld Associates (TWA) and the international SMW5 consortium.

It said technical teams had worked round the clock to repair the fault and restore connectivity. Meanwhile, temporary rerouting of internet traffic through alternative international links had helped minimise disruptions during the outage.

The PTA confirmed that internet services had returned to normal operating capacity following the restoration of the cable.

Submarine cables are a critical part of international telecommunications infrastructure, carrying data between countries and continents. Faults in these systems can affect internet speeds and connectivity, particularly when traffic has to be redirected through alternative routes.

Currently, seven submarine cables provide internet connectivity to Pakistan: Asia-Africa-Europe 1 ( AAE-1 ), South East Asia-Middle East-West Europe 4 (SMW4) and India-Middle East-Western Europe (IMEWE), operated by PTCL; and South-East Asia-Middle East-Western Europe 6 (SEA-ME-WE 6), South East Asia-Middle East-West Europe 5 (SMW5) and Transworld Associates 1 (TWA-1), operated by Transworld Associates.

Cyber Internet Services operates the seventh cable named Pak­istan and East Africa Connecting Europe (PEACE).

In July this year, a fault in the same SMW5 cable system had caused widespread connectivity issues in Pakistan. The PTA subsequently announced that the fault had been repaired on July 3, following its detection on July 1.

World.title: Afghanistan school blast kills 7 students, injures up to 99
World.content:
An explosion near a school in Afghanistan’s northeastern Kunar province killed seven students and injured up to 99 others on Saturday, a spokesperson for the Afghan Taliban Interior Ministry said.

Preliminary reports indicated the explosion originated at a depot storing explosives belonging to mining companies near the school, spokesperson Abdul Mateen Qani said in a statement.

Kunar province, which borders Pakistan, is home to a number of mining operations.

The blast occurred in the Andarsir area of Asadabad district, Qani said, adding that authorities were investigating and would release further details once they had completed their inquiry.

The blast, caused unintentionally, occurred in a house near Shagai Middle School as explosives were being prepared for for mining and rock blasting, Sami-ul-Haq Haq Bayan, head of Kunar’s department of information and culture, said.

Citing medical officials, he said seven bodies had been received at a provincial hospital and 97 people had been injured.

The Kunar official warned the casualty toll could increase and the exact circumstances of the explosion were not immediately clear.

In August, an explosion at an education centre in the Afghan capital city Kabul injured at least 42 children, according to the United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan.

A Kabul hospital that admitted at least 35 of the injured students said all patients were between the ages of 10 and 14.

World.title: Govt seeks flat Rs3.04 per unit fuel cost adjustment for Oct-Dec
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The government has asked the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) to allow a flat additional fuel cost adjustment (FCA) of Rs3.04 per unit for three months — October to December — as an equalised, forward-looking monthly FCA (FFCA) to avoid major price shocks.

Acting on the government’s directives, Nepra has called an emergency public hearing for Tuesday (Dec 2) to approve the FCA, which will be applicable from December’s electricity bills.

The government had announced last week that the additional FCA would be capped at 83 paisa per unit. When contacted, a Power Division spokesperson said the comparison was with September’s FCA of Rs2.37 per unit.

“The ministry has requested an FFCA of Rs3.04 per kWh, applicable for the period from October to December 2026,” Nepra said in its public hearing notice.

The ministry’s petition stated that an additional FCA of Rs2.88 per unit had been requested for October over the reference rate already charged to consumers, for which a public hearing had been completed. The additional FCA for November was estimated at 92 paisa per unit, while that for December was estimated at Rs5.13 per unit. The average for the three months was thus calculated at Rs3.04 per unit.
