Tech.title: These Galaxy Z Fold 8 Tweaks Will Help You Take Full Advantage of Its 2 Screens
Tech.content:
I’ve used and reviewed at least a dozen phones this year, but I keep coming back to the Galaxy Z Fold 8. This foldable phone brings me a strange sense of joy that hasn’t diminished even a few months after its launch (and despite the arrival of a popular rival). I like its symmetrical, thin and lightweight design, but it’s the customizable software experience that’s kept me hooked.

Out of the box, the Galaxy Z Fold 8, like other phones, is quite rigid software-wise. The home screen layout on the cover display is locked to a four-column grid, its camera settings aren’t configured to maximize their potential and you might not know about the multitasking improvements.

Thankfully, you can change these settings, but you’ll need to dive into a few additional tools beyond just the standard Settings menu to do so.

More from CNET

I spent two hours setting up my new Samsung foldable. The process involved installing a couple of apps, changing a few settings and adding new Good Lock plugins. If you’re buying a Galaxy Z Fold 8 this holiday season or have had it for a while, I recommend these changes for a finer, more reliable and personalized experience.

Install the Good Lock app

The Good Lock app can supercharge your Galaxy Z Fold 8. Prakhar Khanna/CNET

Good Lock is a Samsung app made for Galaxy phones. You can download it through the Galaxy Store. It’s the first app I install on a Samsung flagship device because it offers customization options that aren’t available by default. For the Galaxy Z Fold 8, I want to highlight two plugins: Home Up and One Hand Operation Plus.

The Galaxy Z Fold 8’s cover screen doesn’t allow a five-column grid and wastes a lot of space on the home screen. You can’t go past the four-column layout, even if you reduce the icon size (its default icon size is too large for my liking).

If you want a more efficient use of this space, I recommend downloading the Home Up plugin through the Good Lock app (you can easily locate it under the Plugins tab). It lets you change this layout and place icons anywhere you want. You can add up to seven apps in a row or column for a 7-by-7 layout.

I installed it so I could place all my most-used apps and folders on the right side of the home screen for easy one-tap access. I can reach these apps without readjusting my grip. The layout also looks cleaner and more organized. You can perform similar changes to the app drawer by going to the Good Lock app > Home Up > Home screen > Apps list cover column.

Put an end to finger gymnastics

This plugin has made Samsung’s palm-sized phone easier to use with one hand. Prakhar Khanna/CNET

One-hand use is my top priority, and the Fold 8’s wide design isn’t the most ergonomic for system UI elements located on the left side or at the top of the screen. For example, when I need to pull down the Quick Settings Panel, I have to swipe down from the top (I’ve set the pull-down gesture on the home screen to open the Notifications panel). I don’t like readjusting my grip every time I need to adjust a “quick” setting. That’s why I installed One Hand Operation Plus and recommend you do the same.

This Good Lock plugin allows you to add gesture handles to the left and right sides of the screen. You can even reprogram Android’s default swipe back gesture. One Hand Operation Plus lets you add up to six shortcuts within the Short swipe and Long swipe gestures. You can choose from Straight, Diagonal up and Diagonal down swipes.

For my use, I have set the diagonal swipe down from the right side to open the Quick Settings panel. This is a minor change that you’ll appreciate in the long run. Day in and day out, when I need to access Quick Settings, it is no different than swiping down on the home screen to access the Notifications panel. I’ve also set a diagonal swipe up to open the Calculator app because I use it often.

You can also add more functionality with a Long swipe gesture. For instance, a Diagonal down swipe could open the Quick Settings panel, while a long Diagonal down swipe could open a specific setting or app. Samsung also lets you fine-tune the touch area by adjusting the Width, Size and Position.

The Camera Assistant is a must-have

Samsung’s Camera Assistant will unlock the true potential of your Fold 8 cameras. Prakhar Khanna/CNET

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 cameras aren’t as versatile as the less-expensive Galaxy S26 Ultra’s or the ones found in its more expensive Fold 8 Ultra sibling. It lacks a telephoto lens for optical zoom, so you can’t take sharp photos at 3x or 5x zoom. Instead, the phone’s digital zoom crops into the image captured by the 50-megapixel wide camera. However, you can improve the digital zoom results by changing a few settings within the Camera app.

The Samsung Camera Assistant might be mistaken for a pro feature, but it isn’t. I recommend installing this on every Galaxy flagship phone to get the best output from their camera sensors. To find these hidden settings, you need to go to the Camera app and tap the four-dot menu. Then go to Settings > Camera Assistant > Install.

The very first setting you need to change is the resolution. The Fold 8 has two 50-megapixel cameras but its default resolution is set at 12 megapixels, presumably to save space. I recommend changing it to 24 megapixels for more detailed shots and improved results in 2x as well as 4x zoom. You can do so by going to the Camera settings and then:

Scroll down to find Camera Assistant. Tap on it. Go to Photos settings. Tap on 24MP resolution. Toggle on two settings here: 24 MP in Photo mode and Keep 24 MP resolution.

While you’re at it, I also recommend adding a 2x zoom shortcut in the viewfinder. Open the Camera Assistant again and turn on the very first setting: 2x crop zoom shortcut.

I often use the 50-megapixel mode, but setting the default resolution to 24 megapixels is the most efficient way to get better-quality photos. It gives you sharper photos with better clarity (at both 1x and 0.6x zoom) without taking up as much storage as the 50-megapixel mode. For the best quality at 4x zoom, I recommend changing the resolution to 50 megapixels so you can get photos like those I embedded from Instagram.

A more intuitive multitasking experience is waiting for you

Samsung has improved the multitasking experience on its new foldables. Prakhar Khanna/CNET

This isn’t an additional app, but something you should be aware of on the Galaxy Z Fold 8. Samsung improved the multitasking experience on its 2026 foldable lineup. The Fold 8 series allows you to use the split-screen mode in a 90:10 split. It comes in handy when I’m typing in a Google Doc but need to keep my research material visible at a glance.

This is much more intuitive than a 50:50 split because I can, at any given moment, expand one app and trigger the on-screen keyboard comfortably without exiting the split-screen mode.

It is also more intuitive to drag and drop apps in a multitasking mode. You need to go to the Recents menu (swipe up and hold on the home screen), tap and hold the app and drop it on either half of the screen or use it as a pop-up app. The Recents menu then remembers your app grouping for easy access. For instance, if I add Chrome and Google Docs to a split-screen layout and then move to watch Reels on Instagram, I can move back to the split-screen mode by simply going to the Recents menu and tapping on the app group.

Tech.title: Tired of Sudden Outages? Your Go-To Prep Guide for Everyday Disruptions
Tech.content:
If you haven’t already been affected by one of the multiple major system outages that have taken place in November, count yourself lucky. Starting with a Nov. 12 Microsoft outage that kept people’s Outlook email from reaching them for hours and culminating most recently in a Nov. 22 Delta system outage that left travelers stranded, it’s been a rough month. Those incidents are part of a larger wave of disruptions across the US, including a nationwide ground stop of all air travel, an outage affecting classified national security communications and a disruption of online banking services.

Even worse? The month’s not even over yet.

With legacy systems struggling to handle updates and AI tools occasionally going haywire, it’s smart to brace for more outages ahead — and potentially bigger ones.

More from CNET

Governments globally are advising households to stock a basic supply checklist for potential emergencies — guidance that has inadvertently fueled public anxiety and online conspiracy theories.

If you haven’t already stocked up on supplies or made a plan for how you’ll handle a power blackout, a lengthy internet outage or a utility problem that could affect your water or sewage service, you shouldn’t wait.

“Emergency preparedness is NOT just about earthquakes, floods, hurricanes, severe storms or wildfires,” said Chris Reynolds, an emergency management professor and expert from American Military University. “As we all rely on digital infrastructure to conduct the business of our daily lives, a disruption in electricity through accidental or nefarious actions can interfere with banking, communications, online shopping and access to our favorite websites.”

Reynolds’ advice is simple: Prepare, but don’t panic.

“Family emergency preparedness is not a one-time thing,” Reynolds said. “It’s practice that should be continuous.”

What to do about internet, cell and website outages

Short-term internet, cell and website outages may be the easiest to deal with because they happen so often. We’ve been trained to either wait it out, reset our home router or try an alternate device.

If you have internet connectivity but can’t access certain services, visit Downdetector to see if others are experiencing the same issue. The site shows the number of people who’ve filed a report about an outage and places the most recent and severe outages at the top of its homepage.

Cell service outages are sometimes confined to one of the major service providers; it can be helpful to have a backup mobile device, like a phone or tablet, or an internet hotspot that uses a different cell service so you have a backup if necessary.

If internet service is out for a long time, however, it could cause major problems.

“We are all used to having all of our records stored on our computers or in the cloud,” Reynolds said. “It is important to have an offline version or paper copy of important records, emergency phone numbers, etc., in the event of electrical or digital infrastructure failures.”

While many people go cashless these days, a sustained internet outage could disrupt payment systems. It’s wise to have at least a modest amount of cash on hand. (No need to spring for gold bars just yet — dollars are fine.)

“The whole idea is to have a plan that works when technologies fail,” Reynolds said.

What to do about power outages

Luckily, November’s outages didn’t include a widespread electricity blackout, but experts have not ruled out the possibility of one in the future. It could even happen nationwide.

No matter how widespread the blackout is, the advice on how to prepare is largely the same as you might follow during winter storm outages or blackouts caused by summer power grid strain. Make sure you have portable chargers available and ready to charge devices like cell phones. Keep supplies, like water, flashlights and batteries, food and a first aid kit, in your home, as suggested by Ready.gov.

For sensitive data devices, like backup drives and computers, a UPS (uninterruptible power supply) is a must.

Portable power stations that can power even large appliances, such as refrigerators, have become popular among those worried about utility uncertainty. Devices that can quickly jump-start a car and emergency hand-crank radios, which can keep you in the know during a lengthy blackout, are other good supplies to have.

A lack of power could affect your family’s medical needs, especially for those who use home ventilators or refrigerated medications like insulin.

“Families should discuss a specific backup plan with their healthcare providers,” Reynolds said. “It is not advisable to power medical equipment with portable generators.”

Carbon monoxide poisoning can be a danger for those using gas-powered portable generators trying to power medical equipment during a blackout. Do not use them indoors or in enclosed spaces.

Other utility outages like water, sewage or gas

Utilities have become increasingly popular targets for hackers.

If you lose water or gas service, contact your utility to see how widespread the problem is and how soon it will be fixed.

For water disruptions, it may be necessary to boil water before drinking it, if you’re able to. Shutting off the main water valve to your home could prevent burst pipes later. Don’t flush your toilets when there’s a water or wastewater disruption.

While a gas outage simply means your supply has been interrupted, a rotten-egg odor or a hissing sound signals a dangerous gas leak. If you’re unsure and can’t reach someone at your utility, call for help from a safe distance.

General tips for any outage

Keep some shelf-stable pantry staples on hand in the event of service disruptions or widespread outages that may continue for an extended period.

“Remember, the goal is to have enough to sustain a family for a finite period of time,” Reynolds said. “It is not hoarding or stockpiling.”

The supplies you should have include:

Water, about one gallon per person per day, ideally for at least three days. Two weeks is a safer target.

Shelf-stable food and a manual can opener.

Flashlights, batteries, and a battery- or hand-crank weather radio.

Phone power banks and car chargers.

First aid supplies and medications.

Copies of important documents.

A plan for anyone with medical needs, such as refrigerated medication or powered medical equipment.

“Finally, and most importantly, decide in advance how family members will reconnect if separated during a crisis or emergency,” Reynolds said. A predetermined meeting spot avoids confusion when you can’t reach each other.

For more information on emergency supply kits and what to include on your list, check out Ready.gov.

Tech.title: Apple Stays Winning as Smartphone Sales Continue to Slump
Tech.content:
RAM prices are continuing to put the squeeze on smartphone sales, and even people who typically buy less expensive phones appear to be holding off on upgrading.

According to a new report from Counterpoint Research, smartphone sales in the third quarter of 2026 fell by 9% compared to the same period in 2025. The report attributed the drop to rising memory costs, which are hurting sales at the low end of the Android phone market.

In terms of market share, Samsung held steady at around 25%, while Motorola, Google and other companies saw their slice of the pie decline. Where did those sales go, you might be wondering? Unsurprisingly, Apple’s broad range of iPhone models — from the 17E to its newest foldable flagship, the $1,999 iPhone Duo — bumped the company’s share of the smartphone market from 50% to 57% since last year.

More from CNET

Smartphone-makers with cheaper phone lineups suffered due to component costs, particularly memory, eating into their margins. “There, OEMs have little room to absorb a higher bill of materials without raising prices or cutting volume,” said Counterpoint Senior Analyst Emily Herbert.

The slowdown in phone sales has been happening all year. In the last quarter, the market slumped by 20%, more than was expected at the time. The build-out of data centers to support the ever-expanding AI industry has led to shortages of memory components. In turn, the prices of those components have spiked, raising prices of not just smartphones, but game consoles, PCs and other electronics.



Will the holidays save smartphone-makers?

Black Friday, Cyber Monday and the Christmas gift-giving season typically mean strong phone sales for companies like Apple and Samsung. But the memory component crisis isn’t going to go away that quickly, and prices of phones are still higher overall.

Counterpoint predicts that smartphone sales will remain weak in the next quarter and that US carriers may be more selective about the promotions they offer this year. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon are also seeing declining sales and customers are getting choosier about committing to phones that often cost more than $1,000. People are also looking to second-hand and refurbished phones instead of buying new.

“Consumers are timing their purchases around the best deals more than ever, if they buy at all,” said Counterpoint Senior Analyst Maurice Klaehne. “This year’s holiday sales cycle will look quite different from usual.”

Tech.title: This Portable Spot Cleaner From Bissell Is an Affordable Alternative to the Shark StainForce on Black Friday
Tech.content:
A carpet cleaner may not be your first thought for a Black Friday purchase, but it’s actually a great time to buy one, since one of my favorite new cleaners I’ve tested is on sale. The Bissell Little Green Mini Portable Carpet Cleaner is $85 at Amazon, down from its usual $130 price. That’s a $45 savings and, according to Amazon, its lowest price in 365 days. That’s considerably cheaper than the Shark StainForce, which goes for around $200 and is $130 for Black Friday.

The Bissell Little Green cleaner offers tons of cleaning power in a small package at a reasonable price, though there are one or two catches regarding portability and setup that are worth knowing about before you decide which one to buy.

Bissell Little Green Mini vs. Shark StainForce

The Bissell Little Green Mini is a powerful portable spot cleaner. / CNET/Ajay Kumar $85 (save $45) Bissell Little Green Mini Portable Carpet Cleaner Pros & Cons Deep-cleans better than the StainForce, pulls dirt and stains up from deep in the carpet

Completely removed my cats messes with no trace left

Bigger tanks than the StainForce: 16 ounces clean, 13.5 ounces dirty

Corded, so no battery to run out mid-clean

Much more affordable at $130 at full price

Light and compact at 7 pounds, easy to store Corded — 12-foot cord plus 4-foot hose limits your reach and you need an outlet

More setup than the StainForce: fill the tank, add formula, plug in and clean afterwards

16 oz tank is fine for spot jobs but means refills on bigger areas (the full-size Little Green holds 48 oz) Get it now $75 at Walmart $80 at Amazon Expert Take The Bissell Little Green Mini is a corded portable spot cleaner, but it’s still lightweight at 7 pounds. Setup is definitely a little more involved, with a clean water tank that you need to mix cleaning solution into and the need to have an AC outlet somewhere in the area. The trade-off is a significantly deeper, more powerful cleaning than what you get with a handheld battery-powered spot cleaner like the Shark StainForce.



Using the Little Green on the toughest and oldest dried stains left by my pukey old man cat left me impressed with just how deeply it cleaned my carpets. The pristine result makes this corded cleaner well worth the extra setup, and even at full price ($130), you won’t find fault with its power or portability. Bottom Line At $85, its lowest price in a year on Amazon, the Bissell Little Green Mini is an easy buy if you have pets and carpet.

Shark StainForce cleaning a stain off my carpet. / Ajay Kumar/CNET $130 (save $70) Shark StainForce Pros & Cons Portable and lightweight for use around the house

Has worked great on multiple soft surfaces, including carpet and upholstery

Tackles both wet spills and dried-on stains

The included stain removal spray works better than anything I've used before Battery life is short

Relatively expensive at around $200

The waste tank needs regular cleaning and airing out to avoid odors Get it now $130 at Amazon Expert Take The Shark StainForce is a unique handheld vacuum because it doesn’t just clean dry messes — it’s primarily intended to remove stains and wet messes. It resembles other handheld vacuums, but comes with a caddy and a custom Shark stain cleaner that mixes a deep cleaner and oxy cleaner in the spray bottle to lift stains. It works incredibly well — I was blown away by how easily it lifted the worst messes off my white carpets. It removed yellow cat puke stains, wine stains and tomato sauce off both the carpet and couch. It works equally well for older dried stains and wet stains, using a mix of the stain cleaner spray and agitation with the included rubber scrubbing brush head that suctions up the mess at the same time. There’s also a smaller nozzle-brush cleaner included for tight spots. The StainForce will suction up dry waste like cat hair and chunks of half-digested cat food, but the waste tank is fairly small, and it’s not really meant for dry cleaning of a large area due to the limited battery life. The tank will also need to be cleaned out and dried after every use because wet messes will fester and smell if left too long. With all that said, this is the only portable spot cleaner I’ve seen with the design and usability of a handheld vacuum, which makes it an excellent choice if your primary need is portable spot cleaning. The $200 price may sound steep, but I’ve never seen a compact cleaner as good at tackling such tough stains. Specs & Configurations Runtime (as tested) 15 minutes Bin capacity 140 mL Attachments included Caddy, dual action spray, stain eliminator tool, crevice tool, reusable spray bottle head, charging cable

I love the Shark StainForce for its service as a grab-and-go cleaner. It’s cordless, it lives in its caddy ready to go, and for a fresh spill I can spray, scrub, and suction in under a minute with no setup at all. I’ve used it on my cats’ worst messes, including hairballs, vomit from eating too fast, and dirty paws tracked in from the litter box. It works remarkably well for something so small and it’s still the go-to cleaner for my wife and I. The dual-spray bottle that comes with it does an incredible job of lifting stains, even from my white carpet.

More from CNET

Here I am scrubbing away with the StainForce powered on. You can still see some stain, but it’s going away. Ajay Kumar/CNET

The Little Green Mini is a different kind of machine, and that difference shows in the results. On a day when my cats were in rare form and decided to throw up on the bedroom carpet three times in a row, I knew a small portable cleaner like the StainForce wouldn’t cut it, not with the sheer quantity of debris they’d left behind.

I pulled the Bissell Little Green, which, worth acknowledging, is corded. That means more setup: fill the 16-ounce clean tank with water and the included Oxy formula, plug in the 12-foot cord, and work within reach of the cord and its 4-foot hose. It’s still light at just 7 pounds, and it has a useful handle for moving it from room to room.

The StainForce, by contrast, has no clean tank at all. You spray from a separate bottle and only a tiny dirty-water collection tank of under 5 ounces, with about 15 minutes of battery before it needs a recharge. The Mini’s clean and dirty tanks (16 and 13.5 ounces) are much bigger, and because it’s plugged in, it never runs out of power mid-clean.

That proved to be the lifesaver in cleaning my cat’s horrible messes. The Bissell generously saturated the stain with its built-in sprayer that can dispense water and cleaning solution straight from the hose. The hose digs in deep, rinsing and pulling stains, mess and dirt from deep out of the carpet layers. The larger chunks were safely suctioned into the dirty tank, along with the used water.

What I can say is that it did an excellent job of deep-cleaning stains from the carpet — noticeably deeper than the StainForce. It completely removed our cat’s mess, with no trace left behind, though our carpets were left a little moist. My wife’s verdict was that she’s never seen the carpets so clean before and she audibly wondered if it was worth investing in a full-size carpet cleaner because clearly the StainForce and vacuuming aren’t cutting it.

Should you buy the Bissell Little Green Mini Portable Carpet Cleaner or the Shark StainForce?

If you want the fastest possible cleanup for a fresh spill, get the Shark StainForce; it’s hard to beat a cordless cleaner with zero setup. For a smaller mess that I just want to get off my carpet, the StainForce more than does its job. But if your problem is stains that have soaked into the carpet, the Bissell Little Green Mini is the better cleaner, and at $85 on Black Friday — its lowest Amazon price in a year — it’s $45 less than the StainForce right now. It’s the one I’d buy for a house with pets, kids and carpets where you don’t want a big and bulky carpet cleaner and don’t want to worry about running out of charge for a bigger mess.

Tech.title: Apple Brings Its iPhone Broadcasting to Formula 1 at the Las Vegas Grand Prix
Tech.content:
When you watch a Formula 1 race on TV, the screen is packed with lap times, driver stats and real-time video from inside the cars and around the track. During the Las Vegas Grand Prix race, some of those views were captured with iPhone Pro phones and transmitted in real time over T-Mobile’s 5G network.

Using iPhone cameras for big events is no longer a novelty. Apple has been shooting its event videos and ad spots with iPhone Pro models outfitted with cinema-grade lenses, SSD storage and broadcasting gear for several years now. In May, Apple broadcast a Major League Soccer game shot with iPhones strapped to professional lenses, following it up with a Major League Baseball game in September using its own camera hardware,

But compared to a ballpark, F1 ratchets up the complexity, especially in Las Vegas. At the Las Vegas Grand Prix, the race track snakes 3.9 miles through the city’s downtown core. Its route includes the famed Strip (South Las Vegas Boulevard), where most of the big hotels are.

More from CNET

“We control everything on baseball, so we can do whatever we want there,” said Royce Dickerson, executive producer of live sports at Apple TV. “We did 14 iPhones on top of our normal camera complement” during the baseball broadcast. He noted that 10 of those were connected via T-Mobile’s 5G wireless network.

But integrating iPhone cameras into an F1 broadcast, even for the sport’s US broadcaster, is more of a challenge. “I’ve been doing TV production for 20-plus years,” said Dickerson, “and the scale of their operation is unlike anything I’ve seen before.”

Dean Locke of Formula 1 and Royce Dickerson of Apple TV discuss cameras and fan experiences at the Las Vegas Grand Prix race. T-Mobile

Because F1 has agreements with other camera partners, Dickerson did not specify how many iPhones were set up around the track. Neither Apple nor T-Mobile explained where the iPhones were placed in order to capture the speedy F1 vehicles racing around the Vegas Strip. I suspect they were likely deployed in more conventional environments for smartphone cameras, like the team garages and roving to catch celebrities in the paddock area and in the stands, though the iPhone setups wirelessly broadcasting footage at earlier sporting events means they could be easily placed in many locations on and above the streets.

“You really have to work hard to earn the fans’ attention [and] that viewing experience,” said Dickerson. “How are you getting your fans closer to their favorite athlete, to their favorite driver, to their team, to the personalities that surround the sport?”

In the T-Mobile zone at the Sphere – an area sponsored by the carrier and open to T-Mobile customers – at least 10 iPhone cameras were used to cover a stage where concerts played between events. That number is based on a diagram shared during a tour of T-Mobile’s Tech Trailer, where the company’s event coordinators stay on top of things like crowd movements and line lengths.

A poster set up for press in T-Mobile’s Tech Trailer shows the locations of iPhone and conventional cameras being used in the T-Mobile zone at the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix. (Apologies for the reflected glare.)

Dean Locke, executive director of broadcast, media and race operations at Formula 1, sees the combination of multiple cameras streaming wirelessly over 5G as an essential component to the Las Vegas race.

“If we just did cameras at a low level, the fences and track, we haven’t done a very good job,” said Locke. “How can we open up stages, concerts and all of the activities? Each race has a real kind of personality to it. You can only [capture that personality] with huge amounts of cameras, huge amounts of technology.”

If Apple is using iPhones to record live sports, are they recording any of that footage using spatial video for viewing in the Vision Pro? Imagine getting a track-level view of a group of Formula 1 cars speeding past at 200 miles per hour with Apple’s depth effect. “[There’s] nothing at this time I can say about it,” said Dickerson.

Editors’ note: Jeff Carlson’s travel costs for the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix were covered by T-Mobile. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

Tech.title: After 24 Hours With Kodak’s SlideTag, Buying One for the Whole Family Is My Big Black Friday Splurge
Tech.content:
We don’t usually see companies announcing brand-new products just before Black Friday sales kick off, but after spending a day playing with Kodak’s new SlideTag, I’m sure glad it’s available now, because this is what most of my family is getting as a gift this year. Strictly speaking, it’s not even discounted, but its already cheap $35 price tag means this is just too good to pass up.

The SlideTag is a tiny digital photo frame that sits on a keychain, but it’s also a tracker compatible with both Apple’s Find My and Google’s Find Hub. You can load it up with photos and have the six-color E-Ink display cycle through them at set intervals, or you can put something more practical on the screen.

Russell Holly/CNET

The Kodak app makes it easy to generate a QR code, display a to-do list, countdown to a special event or just show you the current date in a nice calendar display. It’s incredibly easy to use, the color E-Ink display is surprisingly good and setting up the tracking feature is super easy. This thing does exactly what it says it does, and with very little learning curve.

More from CNET

So what’s the catch? You don’t really get to choose what the outside of your SlideTag looks like. These clever little photo frames are only available as a blind box, showcasing eight designs across the vibrant history of Kodak’s packaging and something Kodak calls a secret edition, which is unique to this set.

I ordered two, and while both designs I found in the packaging are great, there are other designs in the lineup I’d have chosen first. Some retailers are selling cases of eight SlideTags with promotional packaging, like you’d see at the checkout counter of a grocery store, but this case doesn’t guarantee you’re going to get all eight designs. There’s no real way to know what you’re going to get.

That level of risk may not be your thing, but if you’re looking for a way to add a stealthy little tracker with no shortage of personality to your bag, backpack or purse, I think this is a great option. It also makes a great little gift, perfect for a stocking or white elephant party. And if this level of cutesy fun isn’t your thing, Apple’s second-gen AirTags are on sale for $18 this week.

Tech.title: Best Black Friday E-Bike and Electric Scooter Deals: Save Up to $1,100
Tech.content:
If you’ve been thinking about buying an electric bike, scooter or electric unicycle, Black Friday and Cyber Monday are bringing some good opportunities to save. Segway, Apollo, Inmotion and several other manufacturers have marked down their rides, with discounts ranging from $100 to more than $1,000.

I’ve had several of these models in-house for testing, from everyday commuters to bikes capable of carrying passengers and cargo. Some also offer features riders will appreciate, including automatic lighting, turn signals, Apple Find My support and rear-approach detection.

Saving money shouldn’t mean compromising on safety. That’s why I’m focusing on models with UL-certified electrical systems, specifically UL 2849 for e-bikes and UL 2272 for electric scooters and unicycles. Read more about battery safety and proper charging.



With all of that in mind, here are the Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals worth checking out.

More from CNET

Best Black Friday electric bike deals

Segway Myon: $1,600 (Save $400)

Regular price: $2,000

The Segway Myon is one of the newer commuter e-bikes I’ve tried. It has a 500-watt motor, 85 Newton-meter of torque and pedal assistance up to 28 miles per hour. There’s also Apple Find My support, automatic lighting and Segway’s AirLock system, which can unlock the bike as you approach. You can also add the optional Rearview Radar for $100 to receive alerts about vehicles approaching from behind.

At $400 off, it’s worth considering if you’re looking for an everyday commuter with some useful technology built in.

Segway Muxi Pro: $1,800 (Save $200)

Regular price: $2,000

The Segway Muxi Pro is designed for carrying passengers and cargo, and I’ve been testing its practicality for everyday family use, including transporting my young son. The bike has automatic lighting, integrated turn signals and Apple Find My support, which can help locate the bike if it goes missing. It also includes the $100 Rearview Radar option.

The Muxi is an interesting alternative for errands and shorter trips where you might otherwise grab the car.

Segway Xyber Air: $1,800 (Save $200)

Regular price: $2,000

The Segway Xyber Air is another Segway I’ve tested, but this one is more about recreational riding than commuting or hauling groceries. Its moto-inspired design gives it a different look from your typical e-bike, and it supports Apple Find My, adding another layer of security when it’s parked.

Segway has additional deals on the Xafari and Xyber, with advertised savings reaching $1,300.

Shop all Segway Black Friday deals.

Aventon Current ADV: $3,999 (Free Fast Charger)

Regular price: $3,999 | Free charger valued at $259

The Aventon Current ADV isn’t discounted, but Aventon is including a fast charger valued at $259. I’ve tested this full-suspension electric mountain bike in-house. It has a mid-drive motor producing up to 120Nm of torque and a claimed maximum range of 105 miles. It also offers GPS-based security features, including location tracking and an alarm system. Even though it’s an e-mountain bike, I love how it handles New York’s bumpy streets.

Aventon has additional discounts of up to $200 on select Aventure, Level and Pace models.

Shop all Aventon Black Friday deals.

Best Black Friday electric scooter deals

Apollo Dash: $529 (Save $170)

Regular price: $699

The Apollo Dash is aimed at first-time scooter riders who want something practical without spending a fortune. It weighs 43 pounds, folds in about three seconds and has a claimed range of up to 25 miles. It also supports Apple Find My, a useful feature if your scooter ever goes missing.

I have the Dash in-house, but since I’m above its rated rider weight, my son and partner are handling the riding portion of the testing under my guidance. I’ll have more to share in a full hands-on review.

Apollo Go Stellar: $1,099 (Save $100)

Regular price: $1,199

The Apollo Go Stellar offers a step up in performance with dual motors, a top speed of up to 32 mph and a claimed range of 38 miles. At 55 pounds, it’s heavier than the Dash but adds dual-spring suspension and Apple Find My support. It’s another scooter on my testing list.

Apollo Phantom 2.0: $1,999 (Save $500)

Regular price: $2,499

For riders looking for considerably more power, the Apollo Phantom 2.0 has dual motors, a top speed of up to 44 mph and a claimed range of 50 miles. It also features regenerative braking, dual-spring suspension, an IP66 water-resistance rating and Apple Find My support.

At 102 pounds, however, this isn’t a scooter you’ll want to carry up several flights of stairs.

Apollo also has discounts on its City lineup and higher-performance Phantom Stellar.

Shop all Apollo scooter deals.

Segway Max G3 Plus: $1,000 (Save $500)

Regular price: $1,500

The Segway Max G3 Plus is another scooter we’ve had in-house. It has a claimed range of up to 56 miles, front and rear hydraulic suspension, 11-inch self-sealing tires, disc brakes and integrated turn signals. It also has Segway’s traction control system and electronic braking assistance.

At $500 off, it’s worth considering if you’re looking for something with more performance and comfort than a basic commuter scooter. I’ll have more to share about my experience with it in an upcoming hands-on review.

Vmax VX2 Hub: $959 (Save $640)

Regular price: $1,599

The Vmax VX2 Hub is one of the more powerful single-motor scooters we’ve tested, with 1,900 watts of peak power and an advertised top speed of 34 mph. What impressed me was how well it handled my weight, especially considering its relatively modest size. At $640 off, it’s worth considering if you’re looking for a compact scooter with some serious power.

Vmax VX2 Lite: $639 (Save $460)

Regular price: $1,099

The Vmax VX2 Lite is another scooter on my review list. It’s a more affordable alternative to the Hub, and at $460 off, it could be worth checking out if you don’t need the Hub’s additional performance. I’ll have more to share once I’ve had a chance to test it.

Best Black Friday electric unicycle deals

Inmotion V9: $799 (Save $500)

Regular price: $1,299

The Inmotion V9 is one of the more beginner-friendly electric unicycles I’ve reviewed. It has built-in cellular connectivity, allowing you to track its location if it goes missing, along with suspension for a more comfortable ride. It’s also UL 2272 certified, an important consideration when bringing a lithium-ion-powered ride into your home.

At $500 off, it’s an appealing option for anyone looking to get into electric unicycles without spending a fortune.

Shop Inmotion’s Black Friday deals.

More Black Friday e-bike deals

If none of these models fit your needs, there are a few other sales worth checking out.

Super73: Save up to $600

Super73 has discounts on select models, including the Z Miami Core and S2 Laguna, both priced at $1,895. Its sale runs through Dec. 2.

Velotric: Save up to $700

Velotric is offering savings of up to $700 on select e-bikes, including the Summit 1, advertised at $1,299. The Nomad 2 and folding Fold 1 Plus are also discounted.

Juiced Bikes: Save up to $445 on Scrambler e-bikes

Juiced Bikes has marked down several models in its Scrambler lineup for Black Friday. The Scrambler Mini starts at $949, down from $1,164, while the Scrambler Hardtail is $1,599 (save $445) and the Full Suspension is $1,799 (save $445). If you’re looking for more range, the dual-battery Hardtail is $1,899, down from $2,344.

Shop Juiced Bikes Black Friday deals.

More deals from these manufacturers

Segway also has discounts on several other scooters, including the Max G2 for $598.48, ZT3 Pro for $790 and E3 Pro for $500.

Many of the manufacturers featured here have additional Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals across their product lines. I wanted to spotlight the bikes, scooters and electric unicycles we’ve had or currently have in-house because we’ve actually spent time with them. There are other products we’ve tested that could have made this list, too, but I wanted to give readers a useful selection rather than overwhelm them with every discounted model.

Before you buy

Don’t get too caught up in the discount. Make sure the bike, scooter or unicycle fits your needs, particularly when it comes to rider weight, range, portability and storage. Manufacturers’ range estimates are generally based on favorable conditions, and your actual mileage will vary depending on weight, speed, hills and temperature.

Apple Find My and other tracking systems can help locate a missing ride, but they’re no substitute for a good physical lock. And when it comes to battery safety, look for the appropriate UL certification, use the manufacturer-approved charger and never charge your bike or scooter where it blocks your exit.

Most of these deals run through Cyber Monday, Nov. 30, although some promotions continue into December. Prices and availability can change.

Tech.title: 4 Security Devices I Rely On for Front Porch and Delivery Protection
Tech.content:
The latest and greatest home security products often start at your front door, and for good reason. That’s where burglars first try, too, and research shows thieves can be deterred with the presence of a security cam — but security technology can do so much more.

From protecting packages to managing access the smart way, here are the devices I use every day to guard my front door, and I couldn’t imagine my home without. Take a look to see what your porch could use, too, and the tech options I recommend looking at.

A smart lock to control access from anywhere

Smart locks add a new dimension to your security. Tyler Lacoma/CNET

Old deadbolts do well, but any entryway can get a powerful upgrade by adding digital features via a smart lock. Smart locks allow you to control your front door lock from anywhere using your phone, as well as creating temporary passes for guests. They can support digital wallet keys for touchless unlocking, and many have keypads or fingerprint readers. Plus, you can enable settings like auto-locking, so you never have to worry about forgetting to lock the door.

More from CNET

Smart locks come in two flavors: retrofits that leave your deadbolt largely intact and only replace your indoor thumb turn, and full deadbolt replacements that give you new locking power, inside and out. Don’t worry about installation: If you’ve never installed a deadbolt before, the process is generally easy and doesn’t take much time. I have a full guide where you can find more details.

What models do you recommend?

A video doorbell for smart alerts about what’s happening

Tapo’s large doorbell offers unique visual options. Tyler Lacoma/CNET

Say goodbye to dusty doorbells of the past. Today’s high-tech doorbells do far more than chime: Video doorbells keep an eye on your front porch, while also giving you a two-way audio intercom right on your phone to hold a conversation — or even let an LLM do the talking for you.

Video doorbells also have particularly useful object recognition features, sometimes even for free. That includes recognizing packages and alerting you whenever one shows up at your door, or when one suddenly vanishes. Video storage options can save recordings of key events, so you can check who came to the door if you need to.

These advanced doorbells come in both wired and wireless versions. I’m a fan of the battery-powered, wireless models, which you can set and angle to get just the right look at your porch, doormat and other key places. Many can also work with your current door chime, although you probably don’t need it anymore with phone-based chimes.

What models do you recommend?

A delivery box to protect packages

Yale’s delivery boxes are larger, so you need room for them in the right spots. Tyler Lacoma

Package theft concerns have reignited a centuries-old tradition of protecting mail. Today’s modern delivery boxes are specifically designed to allow delivery people to put packages inside, but make it difficult or impossible for thieves to take packages out, through clever lock models, auto-locking, smart controls and other various tricks.

I’ve been using a delivery box myself for a couple of years and find it very handy, as long as you have the space by your door. Some versions even come weighted or screwed down if you’re worried about a porch pirate absconding with the entire box. It’s a good idea to put notes in your deliveries to use the box, since despite signs not all delivery people will notice it’s there.

As a final plus, these boxes also keep your packages protected from the elements, which is nice when you live in an area that gets frequent winter snowstorms, as I do.

What models do you recommend?

A smart bulb for powerful lighting

Smart bulbs are cheap, support multiple voice assistants and have lots of fun tricks. Tyler Lacoma/CNET

Where front doors exist, there’s usually a light nearby, like an overhead porch light or a wall-mounted lamp, to illuminate the entryway and surrounding area. These lights can also get a major makeover if you switch to an LED smart bulb, which are available as both BR30 floodlights and standard A19 home bulbs.

These lights also give you phone app controls, which is more important than it might seem. With my apps, I can control brightness, set schedules for bulbs to turn on or off, and even adjust the color to whatever I want, say for a holiday event. All it takes is screwing in the bulb and connecting it to Wi-Fi, so you can be done in seconds.

If you feel like experimenting, you can usually link smart bulbs to other devices, too. For example, you could set the light to turn on automatically when a smart lock is unlocked, or when a security system is disarmed.

What models do you recommend?

Now that your front porch is up to date, take a look at the latest home AI tricks I’ve found are actually worth using and how to get them.
